Learn more about cohorts Learn more about cohorts Learn more about cohorts Talents Hire GTME Talent Find and connect with GTM talent who&#x27;ve demonstrated expertise in building advanced workflows Explore GTME talents Explore GTME talents Explore GTME talents FAQ Why are certifications paused? ​ GTM engineering and Clay are evolving quickly. We want to make sure the certification program keeps pace and that being Clay Certified continues to hold weight with employers, partners, and the broader community. We&#x27;re using this time to rethink assessment design, skill validation, and what mastery looks like. What if I currently hold a Clay Certification? ​ Your certification stands. Nothing changes. If you earned it, it&#x27;s yours. I was about to submit. What should I do? ​ Hang tight. Join the waitlist and you&#x27;ll be first to know when we reopen. Any submissions received before the pause are still being reviewed. When will certifications come back? ​ We don&#x27;t have a specific date yet, but it will be soon. We&#x27;ll share an update once we have a clearer timeline. Join the waitlist to make sure you hear about it. I need certification for a Clay partner requirement. What do I do? ​ The certifications program is paused for general applicants, but if you need a certification as part of becoming a Solutions Partner, the process is still open for you. Start by applying through the Solutions Partner application linked from our directory , where you&#x27;ll get access to rubrics, evaluation guidelines, and submission links. Will the same four tracks come back? ​ We&#x27;re rethinking the full program structure, so the tracks may look different when we return. That&#x27;s part of why we paused: we want to make sure the next version reflects where GTM engineering is headed, not just where it&#x27;s been. Can I give input on what the new program might look like? ​ We&#x27;d love to hear from you. Contact Aly Slater, our certifications program lead, directly at aly.slater@clay.com - or share your thoughts when you sign up for the waitlist. We&#x27;re building this with our community, not just for it. Who do I reach out to if I need help with my certifications submission and/or results? (previous program) ​ Please reach out to aly.slater@clay.com ! ‍ Does Clay offer team or organizational certifications? (previous program) ​ No. Certifications are individual credentials. Our system verifies that you created the table you&#x27;re submitting to make sure that it reflects your individual skills, not collaborative work or tables built by others. How many times can I resubmit? (previous program) ​ There is no limit to the number of times you can resubmit! ‍ Do I need a paid account to be awarded a clay certification? (previous program) ​ You should be able to complete the requirements for the Outbound and Inbound Certifications without needing a paid plan. However, for the CRM enrichment plan, Pro features are required. If you do not have a Clay Pro Plan, please fill out this form to be granted temporary access to Pro features: https://clayhq.typeform.com/prorequest ‍ Do certifications expire? (previous program) ​ Certifications expire one year after they are issued to ensure that all earners demonstrate up-to-date Clay knowledge. ‍ Explore, practice and master Clay Powered education Linkedin Youtube Slack community Explore Clay Visit Clay.com Integrations Multi-provider data enrichment Sculptor AI Claygent Audiences Sequencer Pricing Changelog Get started here Get started lesson Clay 101 Enroll in Clay cohorts Engage Find a Clay experts Hire a GTME talent GTM job board Community Join Slack FAQ Legal Privacy policy Terms of service Do not sell my data © Clay 2025 – Born in Brooklyn. Get started Before you begin ‍ 10-K reports are required by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to ensure that publicly traded companies provide a comprehensive and transparent overview so that investors can make informed decisions. They include detailed financial statements, management’s discussion of the company’s results, information about its operations, risks, and future outlook. ‍ They offer a gold mine of information about enterprise companies. However, because it&#x27;s such a tedious process, most SDRs and AEs don&#x27;t take the time to do it ... until now. ✨ ‍ In this Claybook, you&#x27;ll be able to extract 10-K details such as financial statements, operational risks, and future outlook from any publicly traded company in minutes. This can help you: ‍ Find good fit prospects who have problems you can solve Understand your prospect’s risks and challenges Align your messaging with their strategic initiatives Identify key decision makers and potential blockers Prepare for objections and questions Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will guide you through just how simple this is to use. 2 Step 2: Type company name Type the name of any publicly traded company into the first column. ‍ Claygent will automatically research the name of the company, find the website, then extract information from that company&#x27;s 10-K. 3 Step 3: Read the 10-K summary Click the company name and read the full 10-K report summary. You’ll find a summary of their top three initiatives, top three tech investments, and explanations for each company in the table. 3 Step 3: Read the 10-K summary Click the company name and read the full 10-K report summary. You’ll find a summary of their top three initiatives, top three tech investments, and explanations for each company in the table. 4 Step 4: Add hundreds of other companies You can add an unlimited number of new rows as you add more publicly-traded companies. And that&#x27;s all there is to it. Enjoy! Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. To do that, create a Serper account . Serper is a Google Search API that allows you to scrape search results into Clay. You’ll need a Serper account, Serper credits ($50 for 50K credits), and a Serper API key(found in your Serper dashboard once you login). Currently, this table is looking for accountants in Boston. Customize the HTTP API request column to search for keywords relevant to your business. But since we want to personalize our SEO reports with our target account’s brand colors, we’re going to use a tool called Imagga.com (and another HTTP API call) to find them. Then we’ll run those brand color results through ChatGPT to find color codes for primary, secondary, and backup colors. 4 Step 4: Customize Claygent prompt Next, we’re going to customize the Claygent ( Clay’s AI research agent ) AI prompt to find specific keywords related to your industry. 5 Step 5 Generate report in Replit Last, it’s time to generate your personalized SEO reports. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin If you’re part of an enterprise sales team, there’s a good chance you’re under-leveraging one of the richest sources of account insight available: 10-Ks, 10-Qs, and earnings calls. The problem? It’s a manual, time-consuming process. At best, you might load a 10-K into GPT once in a while, but there’s no easy system to stay updated. That’s why we built this Claybook: to show you how to automate financial insights using Clay + Oakie.ai (a platform for custom financial agents inside Clay). First, let’s set the stage: If you’re selling into Enterprise accounts right now (Q2 2025), you would need all three of the following: The company’s 2024 10-K The company’s Q1 2025 10-Q Insights from their latest earnings call One document alone isn’t enough. The 10-K covers last year but misses current updates. The 10-Q covers this quarter but isn’t as detailed as the 10-K. And earnings calls give you future-looking insights that neither document can capture. Tracking all three — across every account on different fiscal calendars — quickly becomes impossible to manage manually. That’s where Oakie.ai inside Clay changes the game. Oakie.ai lets you build custom agents. In this case, Israel Zalmanov (co-founder) built a financial agent that works directly inside Clay. With it, you can: Upload a list of accounts Add Oakie.ai as an enrichment Define the key financial questions you care about Instantly pull answers from the latest 10-K or 10-Q (with earnings call transcripts coming soon) And we’re not stopping there. By adding scheduled runs inside Clay, you can set your table to update automatically—daily, weekly, or monthly. The system will pull the latest filings, run your custom financial analysis, and deliver fresh insights into your CRM, Slack channel, or wherever your sales team works. With this setup, you’ll create a fully automated pipeline of backward-and forward-looking financial intelligence for every target account—without lifting a finger after setup. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. But since every business and category is different, take this time to analyze the AI prompts (both Claygent and Oakie) in case you need to customize them to your needs. For example, Claygent, Clay’s AI web research agent , summarizes earning call transcripts—if there’s something specific you want to add to the summary, adjust the prompt accordingly. And Oakie.ai analyzes growth objectives and operational challenges—if there’s something specific you want to find, adjust the prompt now. So we created this Claybook to help our team at Clay automate awards (in the form of Clay credits) to our most rabid Slack community upvoters. How? By using Tightknit , Typeform (optional), and, of course, Clay. How it works: We create an award in Tightknit for users who upvote Slack threads the most If you win, Tightknit sends you a Slack DM congratulating you on your victory Using a Tightknit webhook, we then send the winners information to a Clay table Since we want to award our users with Clay credits, we then automate a Slack DM with a Typeform link asking for their workspace email Once we receive it, we look up their workspace ID in Snowflake, and use an HTTP API call to distribute their credits automatically Want to award power users in your Slack community with credits to your platform? Keep scrolling! ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Set up a reference table First things first, you’ll want to create and customize a Clay table that lists all your awards, the award ID from Tightknit, their credit amounts, and any other relevant information. You’ll use this table as an internal record and reference table so you can standardize your credit gifts to users. For example, in our reference table, we include the Tightknit award ID (required), award name, credit amount, and award notes. We’ll reference this information in another table in order to distribute the right credit amounts. ‍ 3 Step 3: Send data to Clay via a Tightknit webhook Next, set up your Tightknit webhook (Table: Send Tightknit Typeform) so you can automatically send award information to Clay as soon as it’s announced through Slack. To do that, copy the Clay webhook URL in column one and paste it back in Tightknit. For more information on setting up your webhook in Tightknit, follow their documentation here . Once a new award gets announced via Slack, this table will send a unique Typeform link (optional) to the award winner via a Slack direct message using an HTTP API call. Why? At Clay, we need the user&#x27;s workspace email so we know which account to distribute credits to—Typeform asks for the email. ‍ 4 Step 4: Send data to Clay via a Typeform webook (optional) Next, if applicable, set up a Typeform webhook (Table: Tightknit Typeform Outputs). Here’s how it works: Once the user submits their Typeform, the Typeform webhook will send their workspace email back to Clay where we can look them up in our Snowflake database, find their workspace ID, and distribute the awarded credits. Then we’ll trigger an automated direct message via Slack notifying them that we’ve added credits. ‍ 5 Step 5: Set up an HTTP API call to send credits to your users Next, we’re going to use HTTP API to connect to our Clay API so we can automate the distribution of credits. Customize this step by connecting to your own HTTP API. Last, using the same type of HTTP API call we used previously to send a direct message via Slack, we&#x27;re going to send two different messages: one for successful credit distributions and one for failed distributions. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Automate free trial extension alerts and updates in your CRM - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Sales / Automate free trial extension alerts and updates in your CRM Automate free trial extension alerts and updates in your CRM Automated Slack alerts and Salesforce updates when a free trial extension triggers Start building now with Slack Salesforce Snowflake Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to import account data and automate free trial extension alerts via Slack Snowflake (or data warehouse): to import product usage data (e.g. free trial extensions) Salesforce (or CRM): to import and update account and AE records Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin When a trial gets extended, your AEs need to know and your CRM needs to reflect it. This Claybook helps you automate the entire trial extension workflow: pull account data from Snowflake when a free trial extension initiates, lookup the account’s AE in Salesforce, send them a real-time Slack alert, and log the extension in CRM—all without lifting a finger. No more chasing down trial status or forgetting to follow up. Your AEs stay in the loop, and your data stays clean. How it works: Import account-level data from Snowflake (or any data source) Lookup each account’s opportunity and owner in Salesforce Use Slack IDs to send real-time alerts to the right AE Create a new trial extension record in Salesforce to close the loop ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Import account data from Snowflake (or data warehouse) The table template you copy to your workspace won’t come with data in it. To import account data from Snowflake, just click on the “+” icon in the first column, log in to your Snowflake account, select your Snowflake database, and submit. Once imported, map each respective data point to its own column in the table. For us, we’re importing the following from accounts that just got a free trial extension: email and company URL, their Clay workspace ID, their account executives information, and their opportunity ID that we’ll use to lookup their record in Salesforce. Not using Snowflake? You can delete this column and import account data from any other data warehouse or source. ‍ 3 Step 3: Lookup account and AE in Salesforce (or CRM) Next, we’re going to use the opportunity ID we just pulled in from Snowflake to lookup the account’s record in Salesforce and import that data into the table. Then we’re going to use the owner ID attached to the account’s record to import the account executives&#x27; Slack user ID so we can automate trial extension alerts. Customize the “Get Owner” and “Get Opp” CRM lookups to do the same. ‍ 3 Step 3: Lookup account and AE in Salesforce (or CRM) Next, we’re going to use the opportunity ID we just pulled in from Snowflake to lookup the account’s record in Salesforce and import that data into the table. Then we’re going to use the owner ID attached to the account’s record to import the account executives&#x27; Slack user ID so we can automate trial extension alerts. Customize the “Get Owner” and “Get Opp” CRM lookups to do the same. ‍ 4 Step 4: Customize your Slack message Next, using data we pulled in from Snowflake and Salesforce, we’re going to automate a Slack message to our account executives every time a new trial extension gets added to one of their accounts. Customize the Slack message to fit your style and preferences. ‍ 5 Step 5: Create a free trial record in Salesforce (or CRM) Last, we’re going to close the loop by creating a new record in Salesforce that details the account’s recent free trial extension. Now, moving forward, every time a new trial extension gets triggered in Snowflake, each account’s respective AE will get a Slack alert and Salesforce will get updated with a new record. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/automate-monthly-or-quarterly-account-reviews

Automate monthly or quarterly account reviews - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / Automate monthly or quarterly account reviews Automate monthly or quarterly account reviews Stop manually wrangling account data across tools for every monthly or quarterly review. Automate the entire account review process in Clay. Start building now with No items found. Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to automate account reviews using AI ‍ Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Most customer experience leaders run regular account reviews: monthly or quarterly deep dives into the health and trajectory of strategic and enterprise accounts. These reviews are critical for driving renewals, identifying expansion opportunities, and preventing churn. But too often, they rely on scattered spreadsheets, manual data pulls, and last-minute scrambles to piece together a clear picture of each customer. That’s where Clay comes in. This Claybook shows you how to automate account reviews using Clay, pulling in up-to-date data from CRMs, product usage tools, support systems, and more to generate a living, breathing snapshot of each account. Instead of chasing down context, your team gets a single view that includes: Health rating + reasoning Current use cases and feature adoption Product feedback and support history Risks to renewal Opportunities for expansion How it works: Import account data from anywhere: CRM, data warehouse, support tool, billing software, Gong, etc. Customize account review inputs: create columns for every relevant data point your import Use AI to automate reviews: plug those account inputs into an AI prompt that summarizes and scores account health ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Import account data You can import account data from anywhere: your CRM, a data warehouse, Gong, billing tools, support platforms (e.g. Intercom), or directly from Clay’s out-of-the-box enrichment. For example, we’re importing data from Salesforce, which stores most of our account information like subscription data, product usage stats, and Gong calls, and Snowflake. Need help figuring out what data to import for your account reviews? Here’s some inspiration: Commercial summary: contract value (ARR/MRR), renewal date, expansion or contraction history, payment status or billing issues Product usage & engagement: logins / active users vs. licenses, key feature adoption (what are they actually using?), usage trends (flat, growing, or declining), last activity date or period of inactivity Support & satisfaction: support ticket volume / time to resolution, open/closed tickets, NPS / CSAT scores, escalations or major issues flagged Stakeholder health: who the key decision-makers and power users are, whether those people are still at the company, level of engagement (meeting attendance, feedback loops) Customer goals & success plans : what outcomes were promised or expected, progress toward those goals, documented success metrics (and whether they’re being hit) Renewal & expansion signals: license utilization (over or under), cross-sell / upsell opportunities, org changes, funding events, or tech stack shifts, intent data or buying signals (if available) ‍ Account notes & relationship context: internal notes from AMs/CSMs/sales, meeting summaries, previous challenges, wins, or executive sponsors 3 Step 3: Customize account review inputs Just because you import it, doesn’t mean you need to use it. For example, in this table, we import loads of account data from our CRM and Snowflake, but we only use the following: Basic CRM record data : account name, record ID, account manager, etc. Product usage: subscription plan, credit usage and pacing, ARR, days left on contract, one year credit limit, last 7-day usage, top use cases (extracted using an AI prompt) Product feedback: feedback, concerns, or suggestions extracted from Gong call transcripts Decide which inputs you want to use in your account review and which you don’t. In the next step, you’ll feed those inputs into ‍ 4 Step 4: Customize account review AI prompt Next, customize the account review AI prompt to fit your business and needs. Currently, it’s using the inputs mentioned above to report on the overall health of the account, identify risks and opportunities, and spotlight product use cases and feedback. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Customer experience / Automate QA reports and score on all customer support tickets Automate QA reports and score on all customer support tickets Use Clay and Intercom to QA customer support tickets and pinpoint areas of improvement. Start building now with Slack Intercom Download the template What we used Clay ( Explorer ) to analyze support tickets and send them to Slack Intercom ( Advanced ) to pull customer support tickets Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin As our customer support team grows at Clay, maintaining consistent, qualitative feedback regarding support effectiveness has gotten much harder. While individual support ticket reviews were helpful, they were also time-consuming. So we built a QA engine in Clay to automate feedback on customer support tickets. This Claybook sends closed tickets from Intercom to Clay where ChatGPT runs them through four qualitative checks: understanding and clarity, problem solving and resolution, communication and tone, setting expectations. We then send summaries and feedback to the team through Slack for review (see below). I’m morally against using AI to measure the success of our support team. So we use this system to find areas of opportunity, not to measure how well each individual is doing. If we get a low QA score, we can see where in the support conversation we could have improved and what to do better next time. All in real time. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 4 Step 4: Customize GPT prompts Customize any of the OpenAI prompts to better fit your needs. Certain prompts include reference to Clay.com, for example. Update with your business name and adjust as needed. Currently, ChatGPT runs four prompts to analyze four separate customer support call criteria: Understanding and clarity (column 9) Problem solving and resolution (column 11) Communication and tone (column 14) Setting expectations (column 17) 5 Step 5: Connect to Slack Last, if your Slack account isn’t already connected to your Clay account, add it now, along with the ID of the channel you want to send feedback to. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/classify-ticket-complexity-to-prioritize-route-and-improve-support

Classify ticket complexity to prioritize, route, and improve support - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Customer experience / Classify ticket complexity to prioritize, route, and improve support Classify ticket complexity to prioritize, route, and improve support How to import support tickets from Intercom and classify difficulty on a scale from “very easy” to “very hard.” Start building now with Intercom Download the template What we used Clay ( Explorer ): to import Intercom support tickets, clean data, and rate ticket difficulty Intercom (Paid): to push support tickets to Clay for analysis Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Support tickets are chock full of valuable information that you can use across every department in your business. For example, we use support tickets to catalog bugs, reference recurring issues, find support article topics, and identify Fin AI (Intercom’s AI agent) success rate. But in this specific Claybook, we’re going to show you how to import support conversations and classify the complexity of a ticket as “very easy,” “easy,” “medium,” “hard,” or “very hard.” Scoring support tickets by difficulty might sound like overkill—but it’s actually a game-changer. When you classify tickets from very easy to very hard , three big things happen: You work smarter. Harder tickets get routed to senior agents, simple ones get handled (or deflected) faster, and your team’s time is better spent. You spot patterns. Repeated bugs, complex features, and low-AI-deflection areas become easier to flag and fix. You track what matters. CSAT means more when you know how hard the ticket was. And performance benchmarks finally have context. In short: it’s not just about labeling tickets—it’s about leveling up your entire support operation. How it works : Import Intercom support conversations via webhook and HTTP API Clean support tickets of any irrelevant content that may cause AI to hallucinate Analyze customer support conversations for specific criteria Use AI (and our customer support inputs) to score ticket difficulty ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Import Intercom conversations into Clay This happens in two phases: first, connect to Intercom via webhook (column one) and import conversation IDs from Intercom; second, using HTTP API and the conversation IDs, import all support ticket transcripts into Clay too. ‍ 3 Step 3: Clean support responses of any irrelevant information (blue columns) Next, we analyze all support responses and clean them of any irrelevant information that doesn’t directly address the customer’s issue, like “Happy to help!” or “Can you send the table link?” This leaves you with a “Cleaned Support Response” column focused only on useful, issue-solving content. It helps reduce noise and avoid AI hallucinations later on. Next, we use formulas to calculate: How many cleaned messages there are Where that count ranks (percentile-wise) vs. other tickets Total word count of the convo Word count percentile Add, delete, or customize the formulas and AI prompts in this step (all blue-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ 4 Step 4: Analyze customer responses (yellow columns) Next, we extracted client messages into CLIENT_RESPONSE, counted them, and ranked their volume—more messages often meant higher complexity. We then flagged frustrations, troubleshooting attempts, and topic count to identify harder tickets. Last, we used AI to infer client experience and receptiveness, which impact resolution time. Add, delete, or customize the formulas and AI prompts in this step (all yellow-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ 5 Step 5: Look for any bugs (green columns) Next, we used only the support agent’s messages (SUPPORT_AGENT_RESPONSE) to detect bugs, avoiding false flags from clients mislabeling issues. The Bug Detection column flags the bug and shows the triggering message. If flagged, Bug Functionality reads the full convo to identify the broken enrichment and summarize what the client was doing. Splitting this into two steps reduced hallucinations and improved accuracy. Customize the AI prompt and outputs in this step (all green-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ 6 Step 6: Score ticket difficulty (violet columns) Last, we used ChatGPT-4 and Claude 3.7 to rate ticket difficulty (Ticket Complexity 1 and 2). If their ratings were close, we averaged them. If they differed by 2+ levels—or disagreed on “medium”—we flagged it. Binary Response Complexity forced a choice between the two. If confidence was low, Ticket Difficulty Reasoning Model reviewed both explanations and chose the stronger one. Add, delete, or customize the formulas and AI prompts in this step (all violet-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/clean-crm-with-names-domains-headcount-and-acquisitions

Clean CRM with accurate names, domains, headcount, and company-to-company associations if recently acquired - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Other / Clean CRM with accurate names, domains, headcount, and company-to-company associations if recently acquired Clean CRM with accurate names, domains, headcount, and company-to-company associations if recently acquired How Nook.ai keeps CRM records clean and updated, even if companies have recently been acquired. Start building now with APIVoid Apify Download the template What we used Clay (Explorer+) to research and enrich companies and identify M&A APIVoid (Paid) to check website status of companies who were acquired Apify (Optional) fallback to find employee headcount if needed ‍ Free resources Copy the Clay table template Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . I&#x27;m also personally available to help troubleshoot. You can send me, Jacob Tuwiner , a message on LinkedIn, or schedule a meeting with my Claygency, Sculpted , to learn how we can help. ‍ Get started Before you begin Most go-to-market workflows break down before they even begin because the data at the top of the funnel is already flawed. Inaccurate company names, stale headcounts, and unresolved M&A records lead to bad routing, missed opportunities, and bloated CRMs. For Nooks.ai (one of our Sculpted.agency clients), the problem was no different. So we created this Claybook that introduces a structured data workflow purpose-built to solve the problem. It’s a modular workflow that transforms messy company inputs into clean, enriched records ready for routing, enrichment, and reporting. Here&#x27;s how it works: Intake & Normalization: It starts by cleaning raw company names and domains—removing URL junk, fixing casing, and standardizing formats. B2B SaaS Classification: Next, it determines whether the company is both B2B and SaaS, so you can filter out irrelevant records early. M&A Detection: It checks for acquisitions, identifies the acquiring and acquired companies, and corrects name/domain mismatches. Acquisition Status Check: If a company was acquired, it flags whether the brand is still active (sells independently) or inactive (fully absorbed). Headcount Enrichment: Finally, it pulls accurate employee counts from LinkedIn with two fallbacks—ensuring >95% coverage and 99% accuracy. With this Claybook, you can tackle three of the most common go-to-market data issues: M&A Chaos: Acquisitions often leave duplicate records and misnamed brands that confuse routing logic. Headcount Errors: Reps get SMB accounts routed as Enterprise—or the reverse—due to stale or misattributed employee counts. CRM Bloat: Inactive brands clutter reporting and confuse account ownership. Watch the full guided demo below, or skip ahead for a step by step breakdown: Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 2 Step 2: ‍ Add company names and domains to the first table To start this workflow, manually enter record IDs (optional, but recommended), company names, and company domains into the first three columns, respectively. From there, Clay will automatically normalize company names and domains, then write that data to a second table for further enrichment. To learn how to write data to a different table, take the Clay 101 lesson: Mastering Write to Table. ‍ 3 Step 3: Edit AI prompts to fit your category and business The second table “B2B SaaS Check” uses a series of Claygent and ChatGPT prompts (six total) to identify whether or the company is a SaaS company in B2B: SaaS Research (3 prompts): Company description What they sell Pricing model B2B Research: Single Claygent prompt to analyze target customers. Decision prompts: Two separate evaluations: SaaS check: Reviews 3 SaaS Research summaries → returns is_saas B2B check: Analyzes target custom summary→ returns is_b2b Replace the six prompts with your own category definitions to tailor the table to your needs. After the table determines whether or not the company fits your stated criteria (in our example, B2B SaaS), it writes those companies to a new table for further enrichment. To learn how to master AI prompting, take the Clay 101 lesson: The S.P.I.C.E Framework 5 Step 5: Enrich companies with employee headcount Next, we’re going to enrich companies with employee headcount. To do that, we enrich companies with their LinkedIn company data. If a company doesn’t exist in Clay’s database (rare, but it happens), you can use Apify (natively integrated with Clay but you need your own account to run it) to find additional company headcount. 6 Step 6: Update CRM records Last, it’s time to update your CRM with clean company names, domains, and employee headcount, and create a company-to-company association if a company was acquired by another company. This final table includes all of the data we collected in the previous tables that you need to push to your CRM to update, organized into one pane of glass. Simply add a CRM lookup column, or create/update object column. You can push data to any CRM or export via CSV as well. To learn how to create or update objects in CRM, take the Clay 101 lesson: Mastering CRM data export. You&#x27;ll need to bring your own Beauhurst API key to connect the integration inside Clay. Your CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, or other): The source of your existing account data and the destination for enriched records once the workflow runs. ‍ Free resources Download the template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert Get started Dirty CRM data is one of the biggest blockers to effective outbound and account management — missing fields, outdated funding information, and unclear corporate structures mean reps are working with incomplete context and routing decisions are made on bad data. This Claybook solves that by applying Beauhurst&#x27;s three core actions to your existing CRM accounts. Enrich Company fills in missing firmographic details like company registration numbers and LinkedIn URLs so every account is actually actionable. Find Company Funding adds funding data at scale — grants, total fundraising, and investment history — so you can build routing logic, identify growth signals, and trigger re-engagement at the right moment. Find Company Corporate Structure maps parent-subsidiary relationships so you can merge duplicates, route complex accounts to strategic sales, and disqualify records whose parent company puts them outside your ICP. Once enriched, everything syncs automatically back to your CRM on whatever cadence you set. ‍ How it works: Pull in your CRM data from Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other CRM integration to populate your Clay table with the accounts you want to clean and enrich. Run Enrich Company to fill gaps in your company records — pulling registration numbers, LinkedIn URLs, and other missing firmographic data directly from Beauhurst&#x27;s dataset. Run Find Company Funding to layer in funding history at scale — number of grants, total fundraising, and investment rounds — so you can build routing logic, flag growth signals, and trigger re-engagement workflows. Run Find Company Corporate Structure to map parent-subsidiary relationships for every account — giving reps clarity on true buying centers, surfacing duplicate records, and flagging accounts whose parent company falls outside your ICP.. Sync enriched data back to your CRM using an Update action to keep Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other CRM automatically up to date on whatever cadence you set. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Copy this template First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Pull in your CRM data Use your CRM integration to import existing account records into Clay as the starting point for enrichment. Customize your import using the following available inputs: CRM source (Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other connected CRM) Account filters (e.g. only pull accounts missing key fields, or accounts within a specific segment or ownership tier) Fields to import (company name, domain, existing firmographic data, owner, and any other relevant CRM fields) ‍ 3 Step 3: Run Enrich Company Use the Beauhurst: Enrich Company action to fill gaps in your company records with Beauhurst&#x27;s dataset. Customize your enrichment by mapping the following available identifiers and outputs: Company name or domain as the identifier Company registration number LinkedIn URL Firmographic details (industry, headcount, location, and more) ‍ 4 Step 4: Run Find Company Funding Use the Beauhurst: Find Company Funding action to layer detailed funding history onto each account. Customize your funding data capture using the following available outputs: Number of grants received Total fundraising amount Individual funding rounds (round type, date, amount, and investors) Use as a routing trigger — e.g. flag accounts that have raised a Series A or above for enterprise routing Use as a re-engagement signal — e.g. trigger outreach when a new funding round is detected ‍ 5 Step 5: Run Find Company Corporate Structure Use the Beauhurst: Find Company Corporate Structure action to map parent-subsidiary relationships for each account. Customize your structure mapping using the following available outputs: Parent company identification Subsidiary list Use to merge duplicate records (e.g. same parent company appearing multiple times in your CRM) Use to route complex accounts to strategic sales based on parent company size or tier Use to disqualify records whose parent company falls outside your ICP ‍ 6 Step 6: Sync enriched data back to your CRM Use the Update CRM action to automatically push all enriched fields back to your Salesforce, HubSpot, or other CRM instance. Customize your sync using the following available inputs: Fields to update (registration number, LinkedIn URL, funding data, corporate structure, ICP score) Update cadence (set the table to rerun on a schedule to keep records continuously up to date) Conditional update logic (only overwrite empty fields, or overwrite all with latest Beauhurst data) CRM destination (Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other connected CRM) ‍ Get Started Start cleaning and enriching your CRM accounts with Beauhurst to fill data gaps, layer in funding signals, and map corporate structures — then sync everything back to your CRM automatically. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin According to research from Arcade , interactive product demos increase product usage, reduce sales cycles, and grow pipeline significantly. And now you can use Clay to scale thousands of personalized Arcade demos in seconds. For example, say you just launched a new product feature and want to send personalized product demos to potential buyers that fit your ICP. Traditionally, you’d have to personalize a new demo for every potential customer, or send one generic demo to everyone. Nevermind the process you’d have to perform to actually find ideal companies worth reaching out to in the first place. Now, using Clay and Arcade, you can find target companies in seconds and insert personalized snippets into Arcade demos using their custom variables feature—automatically. Customers use this workflow to send personalized product demos to new prospects via outbound email, new users who just signed up, and existing customers to showcase new features and encourage upsells or renewals. ‍ How it works: Find target companies (and their LinkedIn profiles) based on specified criteria like location, size, employee count and more Use Claygent, Clay’s AI web researcher, to enrich companies with ICPs, pain points, feature sets, and company narratives Use Clay AI to turn enriched data into personalized product demo snippets Insert those personalized snippets into custom variables inside Arcade, automatically Scale thousands of personalized product demos in seconds Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. Using Arcade’s custom variables feature , select which steps you’ll personalize with Clay’s AI-generated snippets. 3 Customize AI prompts in Clay Next, before running the table, customize AI prompts to fit your business. There’s three prompts in the second table. The first one likely doesn’t need customization. The other prompts create snippets for specific custom variables in Arcade (currently two different variables). Note: If your Arcade includes more than two variables, add an additional prompt column for each additional variable. 4 Paste Arcade URL into Clay This Clay table doesn’t require any HTTP API connections. Instead, it uses custom variable URL strings. Simply paste the URL of your Arcade into the last column of the second table and replace our custom variables with yours. 5 Add your company URL to the first table Next, in the first table, enter your company URL in the first column. Clay’s AI will find your company description, create an ideal customer profile (ICP), and define your feature set in seconds. We’ll use this information in the second table to tailor your Arcade demo variables. 6 Step 6: Import companies and run the table Last, select your targeting criteria and import companies and the table will run automatically. Download the template What we used Clay account to manage and automate domain analysis workflows Domain list or emails with extractable domains API keys (optional, for custom WHOIS or DNS tools) ‍ Free resources ‍ https://app.clay.com/shared-table/share_6VpwoE7yKyUj Need help? Ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before you begin Cold email deliverability issues don’t usually come from bad messaging—they come from bad data. Risky domains with no inboxes, recent registrations, or spam traps can quietly wreck your sender reputation before your campaign even gets off the ground. This Claybook helps you stop that at the source. ‍ But first, here’s a quick refresher on some key technical terms you’ll see throughout this workflow: MX Records (Mail Exchange): These DNS records determine if a domain is capable of receiving emails. No MX = no inbox. TTL (Time to Live): A DNS metric that can indicate how secure or stable a domain’s setup is. Very low TTLs can be a red flag. WHOIS Data: Public records about domain registration—like when a domain was created, who owns it, and when it expires. Trap Domains: Domains set up specifically to catch and block spammers. Emailing them hurts your reputation. Catch-All Domains: Domains that accept emails sent to any address (even invalid ones). They’re risky because they hide bounces. ‍ For RevOps, Demand Gen, and Deliverability teams, the challenge is always the same: how do you catch these risks before the damage is done? So we created this Claybook to automate domain risk detection before you press send. It’s a modular workflow that transforms raw domain lists into clean, enriched, and fully risk-assessed records—so you can protect your sender score and filter with confidence. ‍ Here’s how it works: 1. Domain Intake: Start with any list of emails or domains—Clay parses and normalizes them automatically. 2. Email Config Check: Confirm valid MX records and assess TTL to gauge email readiness and potential red flags. 3. WHOIS Metadata: Pull domain age, expiration timing, and change history to spot sketchy or disposable domains. 4. Risk Detection: Use tools like Hunter.io to flag trap domains, catch-alls, and other high-risk patterns. 5. Aggregated Scoring: Combine all risk signals into a simple “Domain Red Flags” column to make fast decisions. ‍ With this Claybook, you can avoid three of the most common outbound killers: Silent Deliverability Decay: Catch dangerous domains early—before they degrade your sender reputation. Mystery Bounce Spikes: Know which domains are likely to fail before launch. Wasted Effort: Stop chasing unreachable leads that never had valid inboxes to begin with. Watch the full walkthrough below, or skip to the step-by-step setup. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Base Table Setup Make a Copy of this template Create a new Clay table Add / Upload your list of company domains as the primary column 2 Step 2: Add Email Configuration Enrichment Use the Google MX Records enrichment to check for: Whether the domain has email inboxes configured (MX records) TTL (Time to Live), which loosely reflects email security processing time ‍ 3 Step 3: Add WHOIS or domain metadata enrichments Add WHOIS or domain metadata enrichments to pull: Days since domain registration Days until domain expiration Days since last update or change Enrich domain security events (e.g., clientDeleteProhibited, clientTransferProhibited) 4 Step 4: Add Email Risk Enrichment Use Hunter.io (or similar) to check for: Catch-all domains Trap domains 5 Step 5: Output or Sync Filter your table to show only domains without red flags Export or sync clean contacts into your CRM or outbound tool For flagged domains, optionally create a second flow (e.g., waterfall validation for catch-alls) Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ ‍ Get started Contact enrichment is only as good as the data it returns — and many providers struggle with accuracy, coverage, or compliance, particularly across European markets. Bad emails hurt deliverability. Unverified phone numbers waste rep time. And scraped data exposes your team to compliance risk on every dial. This Claybook solves that by adding Lusha&#x27;s Enrich Person action to your existing contact enrichment chains. With ~85% phone accuracy and non-scraped data, Lusha surfaces verified emails with confidence scores and direct dials with Do Not Call list indicators — so your reps stay compliant and your outreach actually connects. It works across every major motion: inbound enrichment, outbound list building, and CRM hygiene. ‍ HOW IT WORKS: Bring in your contact list from any people source — a Clay Find People search, a Lusha lookalike result, a CRM export, or any other integration that populates a Clay table with contact rows. Run Lusha&#x27;s Enrich Person action using a few key identifiers per contact — LinkedIn URL, email, full name and company domain, or full name and company name — to retrieve verified contact data at scale. Pull verified emails with confidence scores to trust your deliverability metrics before contacts ever hit a sequence. Pull direct dials with Do Not Call indicators so your reps know exactly who they can legally call before picking up the phone. Feed enriched contacts downstream into your inbound routing, outbound sequencer, or CRM sync — with cleaner data and fewer bounces across every motion. ‍ Note: Lusha requires you to connect your own API key inside Clay to activate the Enrich Person action. Customize your enrichment by mapping any of the following available identifiers: LinkedIn URL / professional profile URL Email Full name and company domain Full name and company name ‍ 4 Step 4: Pull verified emails with confidence scores Use the Include Emails toggle within the Enrich Person action to return email data for each contact. Customize what you capture using the following available outputs: Verified email address Email confidence score (to filter by deliverability threshold before contacts hit your sequencer) ‍ 5 Step 5: Pull direct dials with Do Not Call indicators Use the Include Phone Numbers toggle within the Enrich Person action to return phone data for each contact. Customize what you capture using the following available outputs: Direct dial phone number Do Not Call list status (to automatically flag contacts your reps cannot legally call) ‍ 6 Step 6: Feed enriched contacts downstream Use a Filter , Push to CRM , or Send to Sequencer action to route your enriched contacts into the appropriate downstream motion. Customize your routing logic using criteria such as: Email confidence score threshold (only route contacts above a set deliverability score) Do Not Call status (exclude flagged contacts from call-based sequences) Enrichment match status (only push fully enriched rows) Motion type — inbound routing, outbound sequencer, or CRM hygiene sync ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/extract-data-from-paginated-databases-in-seconds

Extract data from paginated databases in seconds - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / Extract data from paginated databases in seconds Extract data from paginated databases in seconds Don’t let pagination stop you from extracting the custom data you need to fuel your marketing and sales. Extract it with Clay instead. Start building now with ZenRows Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ) to scrape and clean paginated data Free resources Download the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Manually scraping data from large, paginated databases takes forever. And many web scrapers simply can’t navigate pagination easily to do it automatically. Good news: this Claybook uses Zenrow and Clay’s custom formulas to scrape paginated databases in seconds. How it works: Create thousands of paginated database URLs using Clay formulas, automatically Use Zenrows (natively integrated in Clay) to scrape each page, one by one Use scraped data for enrichment, personalization, outbound, and more Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. 2 Step 2: Add paginated page numbers How many pages exist in the paginated database you want to scrape? Add them to the first column, giving each page its own row. We’ll use these page numbers in the next step to create dynamic URLs. 3 Step 3: Create pagination URLs using Clay formulas Next, so you don’t have to manually paste URLs into Clay, we’ll use a formula to add the page number to the database URL string automatically. Simply paste the URL of the database in the formula and insert the page number cell in the proper spot. Once finished, run the Zenrow data scrape column. 4 Step 4: Edit AI data cleaning prompt to fit your needs Next, to ensure we’re pulling usable data from often complex databases, use ChatGPT to clean the dataset. 5 Step 5: Write data to another table for further enrichment Last, write your newly scraped database data to a new table. Why? We want to get all the datapoints into their own columns. The only way to do that is to write to a new table. In the new table, you can use this data for anything, like further enrichment or for outbound messaging. Why is it so important to know when you and a partner share a customer? You can frame your solution as complementary to your partner’s to strengthen your position and product usage. For example, Clay can be used with hundreds of integration partners, and we want our users to know that. With this workflow, we can notify customers the moment they start using a partner tool so sales and success teams can reach out with tailored messaging, recommended use cases, or even co-marketing offers. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Influencer marketing is one of the most effective ways to reach new audiences, but finding the right influencers, qualifying them, and reaching out at scale can be a challenge. This Claybook will walk you through a streamlined process using Clay, MoDash , and Twain to automate influencer discovery, enrichment, and outreach, saving you hours of manual work. What is MoDash? MoDash.io is a powerful influencer discovery and analytics platform that helps brands and marketers find the right influencers across YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok. With advanced filtering options such as audience demographics, engagement metrics, and credibility scores, MoDash makes it easy to identify influencers who align with your brand’s goals. It also provides enriched influencer data, including contact details and audience insights. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/how-connectwise-uses-clay-to-keep-their-account-database-clean

How ConnectWise uses Clay to keep their account database clean - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / How ConnectWise uses Clay to keep their account database clean How ConnectWise uses Clay to keep their account database clean See how ConnectWise keeps their account database updated with live website URLs, accurate headcount and addresses, and custom segmentation and account scoring Start building now with APIVoid Download the template What we used Clay ( Explorer ): to clean, segment, score, and tier accounts APIVoid (Paid): to check website status of accounts Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? I&#x27;m also personally available to help troubleshoot. You can send me, Jacob Tuwiner , a message on LinkedIn, or schedule a meeting with my Claygency, Sculpted , to learn how we can help. ‍ ‍ ‍ Get started ‍ Before we begin Keeping your account database clean is the foundation of any successful outbound strategy. But for teams like ConnectWise, it&#x27;s also a massive operational challenge. Dead domains: 10–20 % of CRM records point to sites that no longer resolve. Generic industry tags: Vendors lump SaaS and MSPs into one “IT” bucket—reps waste time disqualifying. Manual segmentation drag: 250 k site-checks by hand (or offshore) is slow, pricey, inaccurate. So our team at Sculpted helped ConnectWise build a smarter workflow with Clay that updates their database with live website URLs, up-to-date address and headcount, account segmentation, scoring and tiering. How it works: Intake / Normalization Cleans raw company names and domains (e.g., strips LLC/LTD, fixes casing) Website Status Check Pings domains (via APIVoid) to flag 404s, server errors, or redirects Address & Headcount Enrichment Pulls company location and employee count from LinkedIn (fallbacks to Claygent or Apify if blank) AI Segmentation Uses GPT-4o summaries and prompts to classify business type and market (e.g., SaaS vs Traditional, B2B vs B2C) Scoring & Tiering Weighs factors like URL health, LinkedIn presence, industry fit, and headcount to assign account scores and tiers ‍ Watch the guided demo (or scroll down for a step-by-step breakdown) to learn how to customize this workflow for your business. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Set up APIVoid HTTP API call to check website status First, connect to APIVoid via HTTP API in the first table. You’ll need your own APIVoid account (credits are dirt-cheap; one key covers 1M hits), along with the API key, for this step to work. 3 Step 3: Import records with names and domains Next, import records into the first table by filling out the first three columns: record ID (optional), company name, and company website domain. You can add records by typing them in yourself, uploading them via a CSV file , or automating it via a webhook . Once you insert records, manually run the “Normalize Domain” column to kickoff the rest of the table. We keep this column on manual so bulk imports don’t fire the whole workflow by accident. Note: Only working URLs designated by APIVoid will get sent to the second table for further enrichment (and credit usage). 4 Step 4: Customize AI segmentation (table 2) Next, in the second table, customize the account segmentation AI prompts (highlighted in gren). There’s two types of prompts: research prompts and decisions prompts. The research prompts find the company’s summary, its services, and target customers.The decision prompts use that information to segment accounts. In our example, we’re using ChatGPT to help us segment accounts in three ways: SaaS vs. Brick-and-mortar Managed service provider (MSP) vs. Managed security service provider (MSSP) B2B vs. B2C Customize both research and decision prompts to fit your industry and business. Once customized, run the “Enrich Companies” column. This action uses Clay credits, so we set it to manual so you don’t waste money on poor-fit accounts. Additionally, we added a conditional formula so LinkedIn enrichment runs only when industry category is relevant. 5 Step 5: Customize account scoring and tiering (table 2) Next, in the second table, customize the account scoring (0-100) and account tiering (1, 2, 3) criteria to fit your business (account scoring is a native feature in Clay). In our example, we’re weighing five criteria: URL health, LinkedIn presence, industry fit, country, and employees to surface scores and tiers. ‍ 6 Step 6: Update CRM (optional) Last, push updated and enriched data back to your CRM. Just add a Create/Update Object column for HubSpot or SFDC (or a different CRM), or just export to a CSV. To learn more about pushing data to your CRM, check out the Clay 101 lesson: Mastering CRM data exports. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/identify-hard-to-reach-prospects-automate-personalized-gifting-via-sendoso

Start building now with Sendoso Download the template What we used Clay (Free): Clay natively integrates with Sendoso (gifting) Free resources Download the template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ ‍ Get started Before we begin Identifying and utilizing intent and firmographic data for high-touch outreach is a significant challenge, as access to actionable, localized gifting data is often limited. Without clarity on which stakeholders are showing interest—and which gifts are actually available in their region—targeting becomes inefficient and physical mailers often go to waste. ‍ This Claybook resolves this issue by leveraging real-time intent signals and firmographic data to build a prioritized buying committee. When paired with Sendoso , it enables the automated selection of personalized, budget-compliant gift recommendations, empowering fast and effective high-touch campaigns that break through the noise. What is Sendoso? Sendoso is the leading platform for launching gifting and direct mail programs at scale, with the same ease as a digital campaign. We handle everything from sourcing and logistics to integrations with your GTM tech stack, so B2B teams can cut through digital fatigue and connect with buyers in more personal, thoughtful ways. With options across global a marketplace and AI-powered personalized gift recommendations, Sendoso is trusted by industry leaders like Gong, Verkada, and Meta, Sendoso helps GTM teams double win rates, drive 6x higher second-call rates, and close deals 29% faster. How it works: Build your target list using Clay’s native firmographic data to identify high-fit companies. Score and qualify each prospect by layering in real-time intent signals to prioritize accounts with the highest propensity to buy. Map prospect budget tiers to ensure every gift recommendation is automatically aligned with your ROI and spend limits per persona. Generate personalized gift recommendations for each prospect by querying the live Sendoso catalog based on their specific country and seniority. Trigger gift fulfillment directly from Clay, sending the order to your Sendoso account for final approval and shipping. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. ‍ The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Next, use the Find People action to build your list using Clay’s native firmographic data. Customize your search criteria from the list of available options, including: ‍ Industries Company Size Location Job title Seniority ‍ 3 After building your list, you can use signals to quality the prospects to proceed with. To do this, customize your scoring criteria using these available options: ‍ Claygent to identify the number of physical locations each company has Chatgpt to identify the category of leadership each prospect belongs to Use Find active job openings action to see if the company is employing for related roles ‍ 4 Next, use a Formula Column or AI Column to assign a budget tier to each prospect based on their profile. This ensures your high-touch gifting is reserved for the highest-value opportunities. Customize your logic using criteria such as: Leadership category Number of physical locations they have Number of active job openings available ‍ 5 Next, use the Sendoso: Get Gift Recommendations action to automatically pull relevant gift ideas from their live catalog. Customize the recommendation engine by mapping your prospect data to these key inputs: Recipient Email Maximum price (USD) Ship to Country ‍ 6 Finally, use the Sendoso: Send Gift action(s) to push your chosen selection directly into your Sendoso dashboard. Customize the final fulfillment logic using these available options: Product variant ID Recipient email Recipient first and last name Message to accompany the gift Sender’s details ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . I&#x27;m also personally available to help troubleshoot. You can send me, Scott Tousley , a message on LinkedIn. Get started Partnering with influencers can significantly boost your brand reach on LinkedIn. ‍ However, filtering the signal from the noise can be challenging. Vanity metrics like follower count don’t tell the full story. It’s far more useful to understand the actual engagement (reactions and comments) influencers generate on their posts. ‍ In this Claybook, I’ll show you how to analyze influencer post engagement on LinkedIn to make smarter, more informed decisions. ‍ What you can do with this Claybook: ‍ Add LinkedIn profiles of your influencers and see their most recent posts Sync that data to Google Sheets to analyze that information in more detail Compare the performance of each influencer to optimize your agreements Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, duplicate the template to add your influencers. 2 Step 2: Add influencers LinkedIn profiles Paste influencer LinkedIn profiles into the first column. You’ll see details automatically enriched in Clay, such as number of followers, their recent posts, and average engagement per post. Next, we’ll write each post into a new row on another table. We&#x27;ll add your API key to enable this functionality. 3 Step 3: Copy the posts template Next, copy the posts template to your workspace. Go back to the original table and select this new template from the dropdown. This will link the two Clay tables together. 4 Step 4: Map columns between both tables Now you’ll map the columns between the Influencers table and the Posts table. Click the Play button after they’re mapped and watch the magic happen in Clay. 🪄 Now when you add a LinkedIn profile into the Influencer table, their most recent LinkedIn posts will automatically populate in the posts table. 5 Step 5: Sync to Google Sheets Finally, make a copy of this Google Sheet into your Google Drive account. Copy the URL and paste into Clay. Then authorize your Google account. Map your columns to the Google Sheet and your data will flow automatically into the pivot table for custom analysis. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/instantly-enrich-intercom-support-tickets-every-time-a-new-one-gets-opened

Instantly enrich Intercom support tickets, directly in your chat thread, in real time - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Customer experience / Instantly enrich Intercom support tickets, directly in your chat thread, in real time Instantly enrich Intercom support tickets, directly in your chat thread, in real time Deliver better customer support by using Clay to enrich Intercom support tickets with custom contact and company data, in real time. Start building now with Intercom Download the template What we used Clay ( Explorer ) to enrich support tickets and access Intercoms API Intercom ( Advanced ) to manage support tickets and post enriched data Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin ‍ What’s one of the most common challenges support teams face every day? ‍ Identifying which person and company has opened a support ticket in the first place. ‍ At Clay, ten support specialists handle over 6,000 support tickets every month. By quickly identifying who’s on the other line (and their history with our product), we can make each response more relevant and helpful. ‍ So we created a system for it. ‍ Each time a ticket opens, an Intercom workflow triggers a webhook to Clay. In Clay, we: ‍ Enrich user data with our people/company information. Pull relevant data from Salesforce. Use the Intercom API to post this information as a note on the ticket. ‍ Why not just connect our CRM to Intercom? ‍ We do, but here’s two reasons why this works better: ‍ Coverage : Sometimes users reach out before creating a Clay account, so this method helps us recognize who they are even if they haven’t reached Salesforce. ‍ Visibility : Intercom sidebar data is overwhelming, so adding this info directly in the ticket keeps it front and center for our specialists. Plus, we can adjust the info to align with our goals. For example, we can see how many enrichments a customer has run in Clay which helps with activation goals. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Create a webhook and workflow in Intercom Set up your webhook and workflow in Intercom so it can send data to Clay when new support tickets open. 3 Step 3: Set up your HTTP API call Next, so Clay can send enriched data back to Intercom in the form of notes, customize your HTTP API column with your Intercom API key and admin ID. To find your Intercom API key, follow the instructions here . To find your admin ID in Intercom: settings > workspace > teammates > click on the teammate you want > copy the ID at the end of the URL of the page. For example: intercom.com/a/apps/w14l1kwz/admins/ 1633147 (in this URL, “1633147” is the admin ID). 4 Step 4: Set up CRM Lookup Last, so Clay can check if someone exists in Salesforce (and pull information if they do), update both Salesforce lookup columns with your credentials. Using a different CRM? Replace lookups with your respective CRM by navigating to add enrichment > integrations > find your CRM > select contact or company lookup.
