## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/monitor-and-act-on-linkedin-brand-mentions

Signals: Capture and activate brand mention signals, natively in Clay - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Sales / Signals: Capture and activate brand mention signals, natively in Clay Signals: Capture and activate brand mention signals, natively in Clay How to automate LinkedIn brand mention monitoring in Clay Start building now with No items found. Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to import social posts from LinkedIn that mention your company name, and enrich people who comment Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin Whether it’s a shoutout, a question, a critique, or a casual name-drop, every public mention is an opportunity to engage, qualify, or learn. But most companies let these signals slip by unnoticed, buried in the feed or locked inside a team member’s notifications. Missed opportunity. This is where brand mention signals come in. By automatically tracking and enriching mentions of your brand across LinkedIn posts, you can turn passive noise into actionable insight: Spot buyers in the wild without waiting for a form fill Route warm leads to sales or CS in real time Understand how people are framing and interpreting your product Prioritize advocates and influencers in your network Respond quickly to negative or confused mentions before they snowball In this Claybook, we’ll show you how to automate brand mention alerts using Clay’s out-of-the-box brand mention signals. It pulls in LinkedIn posts, enriches the data with author and sentiment info, writes to your contact table, and even sends alerts to Slack so your team never misses a moment that matters. How it works : Find and enrich posts: use "find social posts" to pull linkedin posts (e.g. mentioning “clay”) and enrich them with metadata (author, content, comment count) using "enrich social post". Extract core post data: create fields to extract key details like post text, url, creation date, and update time. Enrich author info: use "enrich person" to pull the author’s name, title, and organization from their linkedin profile. Analyze and classify content: use "clay category & sentiment" to assess sentiment and categorize the post’s mention of clay; extract those values into fields. Capture and route comments: use "get comments on a social post" and write those, along with the original post data, to the "all social post reactors" table. Notify via slack: send a message to a slack channel when a post about clay is detected, including author info, sentiment, category, and post link. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 5 Step 5: Send notifications to Slack (optional) Next, to send Slack alerts to sales when someone mentions your company name on LinkedIn, connect your account to the last column in table one. ‍ 6 Step 6: Lookup accounts in CRM (optional) Last, this table looks up target contacts in our CRM to see whether or not one of them commented on a post that mentioned Clay. You can replicate this step with any CRM (either through a native integration or with HTTP API). ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/prioritize-outreach-with-buying-intent-signals-via-lusha

Prioritize Outreach with Buying Intent Signals via Lusha - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / Prioritize Outreach with Buying Intent Signals via Lusha Prioritize Outreach with Buying Intent Signals via Lusha Layer Lusha&#x27;s contact and company signal actions into any Clay workflow to reprioritize account lists, give reps a timely reason to reach out, and trigger sequences based on real buying momentum — not just firmographic fit. Start building now with Lusha Download the template What we used Clay (Paid): Powers the signal enrichment workflow — connects your people and company sources, runs Lusha&#x27;s signal actions across every row, applies scoring and filtering logic, and routes prioritized records to your sequencer or CRM. Lusha: Provides signal actions — that surface timely buying intent at both the contact and company level. Note that signal actions are charged on a per-result basis, so configuring your inputs carefully before running is important. ‍ Free resources Download the template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Most enrichment workflows treat every contact and account equally — but timing is everything in outbound. A perfectly enriched contact means little if there&#x27;s no trigger to act on. The signal is often already there; it&#x27;s just not being captured. This Claybook solves that by layering Lusha&#x27;s four signal actions into your existing Clay workflows. At the contact level, Find Person Signals detects promotions and company changes — two of the strongest indicators that a buyer&#x27;s priorities have shifted. At the company level, Find Company News surfaces funding rounds, acquisitions, and leadership changes, while Find Company Headcount Growth and Find Company Jobs Growth track hiring momentum by department over time. Together, they give you the context to reprioritize lists, score accounts dynamically, and trigger personalized outreach at exactly the right moment. ‍ HOW IT WORKS: Bring in your contact or account list from any Clay people or company source — a CRM export, a lookalike result, a Find People search, or any existing Clay table you want to reprioritize. Run Find Person Signals at the contact level to detect promotions and company changes for each contact, and use the results as run conditions to filter or trigger downstream steps. Run Find Company News Signal to surface funding rounds, acquisitions, and leadership changes at the account level — with article highlights, titles, event dates, and source URLs you can feed directly into AI columns for personalization. Run Find Company Jobs Growth Signal to track hiring surges by department, capturing historical averages, change rates, and new job postings from the last month to identify accounts in active growth mode. Run Find Company Website Traffic Signal to monitor web traffic trends at the account level. Score and reprioritize your list using a Formula or AI column that weighs signal recency and strength — then route high-signal accounts and contacts to your sequencer or rep queue for timely, context-rich outreach. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Copy this template First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Bring in your contact list Use any people or company source to populate your Clay table. Customize your input using any of the following sources: CRM export (HubSpot, Salesforce, or other) Lusha&#x27;s Find Company or People Lookalikes Clay&#x27;s native Find People or Find Companies action Any existing Clay table you want to reprioritize with signal data ‍ 3 Step 3: Run Find Person Signals Use the Lusha: Find Person Signals action to detect recent career activity for each contact in your table. Customize your enrichment using the following available inputs and outputs: LinkedIn URL or email as the contact identifier Monitoring date (how far back to look for signal activity) Promotion detected (boolean — use as a run condition to trigger downstream steps) Company change detected (boolean — use as a run condition to filter or re-route contacts) ‍ 4 Step 4: Run Find Company News Signals Use the Lusha: Find Company News Signals action to surface timely account-level events. Customize your signal capture using the following available inputs and outputs: Company domain or name as the identifier News topic filters (specify before running as this action charges per result) Article title and highlights (feed into AI columns for outreach personalization) Event effective date (use to filter for recency) Article URL (for rep context and source verification) ‍ 5 Step 5: Run Find Company Jobs Growth by Department Signal Use the Lusha: Find Company Jobs growth by department signal action to track hiring momentum by department. Customize your signal capture using the following available inputs and outputs: Company domain or name as the identifier Max departments to return (specify before running as this action charges per result) Department-level hiring surge indicator Historical average and change rate New job postings in the last month ‍ 6 Step 6: Run Find company website traffic signal Use the Lusha: Find Company Website Traffic Signal action to monitor web traffic trends at the account level. Customize your signal capture using the following available inputs and outputs: Company domain or name as the identifier Signal type selection (increase or decrease in traffic — choose based on whether you&#x27;re targeting growth or churn risk) Signal date (to filter for recency) Historical average visits ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin Most companies qualify prospects by job title and company. But does that really show who can buy your product? For higher-ticket or luxury purchases, wealth and income matter. Minerva (natively integrated in Clay) provides estimated wealth and income data so you can better qualify inbound and outbound leads. Here are a few common use cases: Prosumer SaaS & Fintech tools The pain: Free signups flood in with no context, and only a fraction have true upgrade potential. The fix with Minerva: Resolve signups to employers and titles, then fast-track ICP fits into your sales-assisted or enterprise funnel. High-ticket consumer brands Examples: Luxury travel, high-end fitness/wellness, private education, wealth management. The pain: Inbound lists are full of Gmail signups, and CAC is too high to waste on unqualified buyers. The fix with Minerva: Link personal → professional to filter for households with discretionary income. Build wealth-tiered segments so you only chase customers who can actually buy. Education & training (B2C → B2B cross-sell) The pain: Applicants use personal emails, but fit depends on career stage, employer sponsorship, or disposable income. The fix with Minerva: Enrich leads with professional background and wealth signals. Price correctly, tailor offers by career tier, and surface corporate training opportunities. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Input identifiers Minerva’s endpoint works with name, email, phone, or LinkedIn URL. You can enrich with just one, but providing more details increases match rates. Once your identifiers get entered, the enrichment will run automatically. ‍ 4 Step 4: Make it your own Last, get creative! You can further enrich the profile (using Minerva’s “Enrich person wealth & income”) to get professional background, contact info, and more. You can connect the table to your inbound lead form to enrich every net-new lead. Or you can layer in any of Clay’s enrichments—firmographics, technographics, hiring signals, news, social profiles, intent data, and more—to build the exact view you need. ‍ ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to find ICP-fit prospects, enrich them with emails, and capture custom signals from their website, job openings, and recent hires ‍ Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin We love individual buying signals: recent hires, job openings, news mentions, fundraising announcements, tech stack, and more. But so do all your competitors, and so does every GTM tool on the market. Today, individual signals won’t help you reach GTM Alpha . But what will give you an edge is stacking multiple signals—like an active blog plus new GTM hires plus open roles in your problem area—and curating custom signals relevant to your business. Good news: This Claybook shows you how to create custom website signals and combine them with hiring and job opening signals so you can spot companies that aren’t just a good fit, but are showing signs of change, growth, or intent. How it works: Import website leads to Clay using a webhook (or manually import with CSV) Score and qualify leads based on specific ICP criteria Use Claygent to find custom website signals Use Clay to find recent hires and current job openings Use a Clay formulas to easily spot when a qualified prospects matches all signals Schedule table updates weekly ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. To create your own webhook, copy the webhook URL from the first column and paste it back in your source. Once the webhook is established, the form leads will get added automatically and Clay will run the rest of the table, enriching contacts and their companies, validating their emails, qualifying them based on specified criteria, checking for blog posts and new hires, and more. Learn more about importing data via webhooks: The power of webhooks in Clay . 4 Step 4: Use Claygent to find custom website signals This table uses Claygent, Clay’s AI research agen t, to identify if our qualified prospects’ company websites have active blogs. You can keep this prompt untouched, or you can modify it to find different website signals, like if the company is PLG, if they have pricing tiers, if they have a sales demo, and literally anything you can imagine. 5 Step 5: Find recent hires and current job openings Next, find out whether or not the qualified lead works at a company with current job openings or recently hired roles relevant to your industry and product. First, customize the Find Contacts enrichment to pull in contacts from your lead’s company who were recently hired in departments that you sell to. For example, we’re looking for GTM, GTM engineering, and go-to-market job titles within the last three months so we can find companies with newly hired GTM teams. Next, customize the “Find Active Job Openings” column with your job criteria (job title, seniority, location, etc.). Together, you can find current hiring trends related to your problem area. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin ‍ How does GoNimbly streamline multi-threading and next steps after sales calls? ‍ By automating the entire process using Gong, Hubspot, and Clay. ‍ This Claybook helps sales reps efficiently multi-thread by automatically capturing meeting attendees&#x27; emails, enriching their profiles, sending them directly to the CRM, and messaging them at the right time. ‍ Here’s how it works: ‍ Capture meeting attendees emails Enrich their profiles in Clay Send enriched contact data back to your CRM Receive Gong call summaries in Slack Automate multi-threaded outbound via Gong Flows Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy both templates in Clay: Gong HTTP/API Calls and enrichment If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. Then paste your Gong API token in the marked spot. Clay will store all calls within the timeframe—directly in the table. No data warehouse needed. This table uses the “Basic Authorization” HTTP header. You can also retrieve calls through Oauth using the Bearer token. Learn how to create both here: Gong API , retrieve call data . 3 Step 3: Set up “Write to other table” Next, send call data to your second table (Calls and enrichment) where we’ll pull in all details, enrich contacts, find emails, and draft quick, informed follow ups. 4 Step 4: Configure “Transcripts” HTTP/API To get transcripts for calls in the “Calls and enrichment” table, open the “Transcripts” column and paste your API token in the marked spot. Learn more about Gong’s “transcript” documentation here . To get detailed call data from Gong records, open the “Get call details” column and paste your API token in the marked spot. In order to change what call details you want to retrieve, edit the body (optional). Currently, the main call details include: brief, topics, parties on the call, outline, keywords tracked, highlights, and points of interest. Learn more about Gong’s “extensive” documentation here . 5 Step 5: Set up HubSpot lookups and add to Gong “Flow Next, add your HubSpot account so you can “lookup” contacts in your CRM and update or create a deal. This table repeats this step seven 7 times, so add your Hubspot account to each of the seven columns. If you don’t use HubSpot, you can delete these columns and replace them with your CRM. Last, add your enriched prospects to your Gong “Flow” (their version of an automated outbound sequence) for multi-threaded outreach. Stay connected when they land in new roles. Workflow created by our community: https://www.clay.com/experts/profile/josh-whitfield Start building now with HubSpot Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to monitor champions who have recently changed jobs to new companies ‍ Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin Your best champions don’t stay put. If you’re not tracking where they go, you’re missing out on pipeline. For example, when a customer champion changes jobs, two things happen: you risk losing influence at the account they’re leaving and miss a golden opportunity to land with them at their new company. Most teams only notice after it’s too late. This Claybook helps you stay ahead by automatically monitoring your customer champions and flagging when they land somewhere new so you can protect existing revenue and create warm leads with people who already know your value. How it works: Import your current customer champions into a Clay from your CRM Use the “Monitor for Job Changes” action to track their moves Automatically capture new company, old company, and start date Enrich job movers with work emails and their LinkedIn profile URLs Reach out with context and timing on your side ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Import champions from your CRM Import champions from your CRM. This template example uses Hubspot, but for those that don&#x27;t use Hubspot, you can import customers from any CRM using one of Clay’s native CRM integrations or via HTTP API. Once champions get imported to the table, the workflow will start and Clay will automatically find their LinkedIn profile URLs. ‍ 3 Step 3: Find champions who have recently changed jobs Next, use the “Monitor for job changes” action to track when current champions move jobs (and where they go). You can track champions who moved jobs in the last 3, 6, or 12 months, and you can schedule the table to update daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly. Clay will automatically find job movers, their new company name and domain, their LinkedIn profile URLs, and their work emails. ‍ 4 Step 4: Act on job mover signals From here, you can customize the table any way you want: Update your CRM with new companies and contacts, stack additional signals to qualify your job movers new company, send Slack alerts to AEs, and much more. For example, in our table, we look up our job mover in the CRM, update their record with their new company, or create a new company if it doesn’t exist. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. ## http://university.clay.com/claybooks/turn-closed-won-accounts-into-net-new-pipeline-with-lusha-lookalikes

Turn Closed-Won Accounts into Net-New Pipeline with Lusha Lookalikes - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / Turn Closed-Won Accounts into Net-New Pipeline with Lusha Lookalikes Turn Closed-Won Accounts into Net-New Pipeline with Lusha Lookalikes Turn your closed-won accounts and top-converting contacts into a repeatable prospecting engine — Lusha&#x27;s proprietary lookalike algorithm finds similar companies and people so you can replicate what&#x27;s already working. Start building now with Lusha Download the template What we used Clay (Paid): Powers the full lookalike workflow — runs Lusha&#x27;s table source actions to generate net-new rows, stacks enrichment actions at the company and contact level, applies ICP scoring logic, and routes qualified records to your CRM or sequencer. Lusha: Provides the Find Company Lookalikes and Find People Lookalikes source actions that surface net-new accounts and contacts matched to your best customers by firmographic profile, title, seniority, and company context. ‍ Free resources Download the template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Finding net-new accounts and contacts that fit your ICP is one of the hardest parts of outbound — most teams either rely on static lists or manually hunt for companies that "feel similar" to their best customers. The signal is already in your CRM; it&#x27;s just not being used. This Claybook solves that by using Lusha&#x27;s Find Company Lookalikes and Find People Lookalikes — two table source actions that generate net-new rows from your seed inputs. Feed in 5–100 of your best customer domains or top-converting contacts&#x27; LinkedIn URLs or emails, and Lusha&#x27;s proprietary algorithm returns similar companies matched by firmographic profile, or similar people aligned by title, seniority, and company context. From there, Clay enriches the results, scores them against your ICP, and pushes them to your sequencer — or Clay&#x27;s own — for personalized outreach. ‍ How it works: Seed your lookalike search with 5–100 of your best customer domains (for account-level prospecting) or your top-converting contacts&#x27; LinkedIn URLs or emails (for people-level prospecting). Generate net-new lookalike rows using Lusha&#x27;s Find Company Lookalikes or Find People Lookalikes — both are table source actions, meaning they create new records matched by firmographic profile, title, seniority, and company context rather than enriching existing ones. Enrich the results by running Lusha&#x27;s Enrich Company or Enrich Person actions — or any other Clay enrichment provider — to layer in full firmographic and contact data on every returned record. Score each record against your ICP using a formula or AI column to rank accounts and contacts by fit — filtering out noise before anything hits your sequencer. Push to outreach by routing qualified accounts and contacts to your sequencer of choice — or directly into Clay&#x27;s built-in sequencer — for personalized, high-relevance campaigns. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Copy this template First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Seed your search and generate net-new lookalike rows Use the Lusha: Find Company Lookalikes or Lusha: Find People Lookalikes action as your table source, inputting your best customers and top-converting contacts as seeds to generate net-new rows. Customize your lookalike search using the following available inputs: Find Company Lookalikes: Seed company domains (minimum 5, maximum 100) Exclusion list (domains to exclude from results — use to filter out existing customers or previously contacted accounts) Max results to return per seed Find People Lookalikes: Seed LinkedIn URLs, professional profile URLs, or emails (minimum 5, maximum 100) Exclusion list (profiles or emails to exclude from results) Max results to return per seed ‍ 3 Step 3: Enrich the results Use Lusha: Enrich Company , Lusha: Enrich Person (both require API key) , or any other Clay enrichment provider to layer full firmographic and contact data onto every lookalike record returned. Customize your enrichment by mapping the following available identifiers: Enrich Company: Company domain Company name Returns: employee count, annual revenue, follower count, industry, and more Enrich Person: Professional Profile URL Email Full name and company domain Returns: verified email, direct dial, title, seniority, and more ‍ 4 Step 4: Score each record against your ICP Use a Formula Column or AI Column to assign a fit score to each returned record before anything moves to outreach. Customize your scoring logic using criteria such as: Industry or vertical Employee count or annual revenue range Seniority level or job title Geography or region Technology stack (e.g. CRM type from waterfall enrichment) Keywords from enriched firmographic data ‍ 5 Step 5: Find and enrich contacts at matched companies Use Clay&#x27;s Find People action to identify relevant contacts at your highest-scoring lookalike companies, then stack contact-level enrichments to fill in outreach details. Customize using the following available inputs: Company domain (pulled from enriched lookalike rows) Job title or function filter Seniority filter Find Work Email or Enrich Person to retrieve verified contact information ‍ 6 Step 6: Push to outreach Use the Clay&#x27;s built-in sequencer or any other sequencer to route qualified records into a personalized outreach campaign. Customize your outreach logic using the following available inputs: Recipient email First and last name Personalization fields drawn from enriched company or contact data Sequence or campaign assignment Filter conditions to ensure only records above your ICP score threshold are pushed Destination — CRM, third-party sequencer, or Clay&#x27;s native sequencer ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Get started Before we begin ‍ This Claybook will help you create a list of target accounts using Google Maps as your source. Note: Not all Google Maps businesses have a website, in which case the enrichment won’t run for these specific rows. It can be intimidating given how fast the tools are evolving, but the daily exercises are the best starting point and the community is incredibly supportive and engaged Melissa Jimenez Sales Ops Specialist, Studeo View instagram View instagram ​ View twitter View twitter ​ View website View website ​ What else is included? Quick support Access live support from the Clay team and a group of peers through a private Slack channel – and attend live office hours to hone your skills Hands on excercises Go through daily, practical exercises that will help you rapidly scale your Clay skills. Private community Access a private slack channel during the course for collaboration + feedback. Clay AI Skils Cohort Timeline We’ll start with AI foundations, level up through real projects, and bring everything together through peer-to-peer discussions. By the end, you&#x27;ll feel confident in AI-powered GTM automation! Day 01 Kickoff Day 02 Foundations of AI-Powered GTM Day 03 GTM Automation with AI Formulas Day 04 Prompting Masterclass Day 05 Limitless Research with Claygent Day 06 Graduation & Alumni Community FAQ Is it mandatory to join the Clay Slack community? ​ Yes! All cohort communication takes place in a private channel in the Clay Slack community. You must join the community before submitting a cohort application. What is the time commitment? ​ All cohorts run for 1 week. You should expect to set aside 3-4 hours each day to go through the content and build workflows. It is an intensive and involved learning experience so keep that in mind before you apply! How many live sessions take place during a cohort? ​ While the cohort is designed to help you learn at your own pace async, we offer several optiona l live sessions alongside to help you meet other learners, ask questions about the Cohort content, and dive deeper into GTM Engineering related topics outside of the immediate lessons! You can find all live sessions on the course calendar on Uplimit once you’re enrolled. Remember - these optional live sessions are offered to complement the async learning + peer-to-peer discussions happening on your private Cohort Slack. If questions come up, please feel free to post the question on private Cohort Slack following best practices for asking & answering a question, instead of waiting until a live session so that you are treading forward with your learning 🩷 We try our best to have at least one live session that works well for you, regardless of which timezone you’re in. We’d love for you to join, be on camera, and bring any and all questions and discussion points you have 🫶🏻 All calls are recorded unless announced otherwise. ‍ How many live sessions take place during a cohort? ​ While the cohort is designed to help you learn at your own pace async, we offer several optiona l live sessions alongside to help you meet other learners, ask questions about the Cohort content, and dive deeper into GTM Engineering related topics outside of the immediate lessons! You can find all live sessions on the course calendar on Uplimit once you’re enrolled. Remember - these optional live sessions are offered to complement the async learning + peer-to-peer discussions happening on your private Cohort Slack. If questions come up, please feel free to post the question on private Cohort Slack following best practices for asking & answering a question, instead of waiting until a live session so that you are treading forward with your learning 🩷 We try our best to have at least one live session that works well for you, regardless of which timezone you’re in. We’d love for you to join, be on camera, and bring any and all questions and discussion points you have 🫶🏻 All calls are recorded unless announced otherwise. ‍ Do I get upfront credits to work on the cohort assignments? ​ We offer a small amount of credit to help you get started. As you complete each assignment, you will get additional credits based on your performance. (*this does not apply to Clay Enterprise Cohort) This is done only once per workspace for the same cohort type in your lifetime – and will be issued automatically following the Kickoff call. Even if you have multiple users joining a cohort, the joining credits will remain the same. Please note that the joining credit does not expire for 1 year. If you’re seeing that your joining credits are gone, it’s likely that you or someone else in your workspace has already used them so please check before inquiring. ‍ When should I submit my cohort application after creating a new Clay account? ​ You must wait at least 24 hours after creating a new Clay account before submitting your cohort application. Do I need to be on a paid plan to join a cohort? Do I need to pay to enroll in a cohort? ​ Cohorts are free to join. For AI Skills Cohort, you can be on any plan to apply. For Enterprise Cohort, you must be on an enterprise plan to enroll. What do I get if I graduate from a cohort? ​ Graduation perks change from time to time. Currently, we provide access to our exclusive graduates community as well as additional credits that you earn along the way! Please Note: Clay reserves the right to change cohort perks without prior communication. The terms communicated during the cohort in the private channel are applicable. ‍ What should I know about credit expiration? ​ For free accounts, credits earned during a cohort will expire at the end of each month. Plan your cohort applications accordingly. For paid accounts, refer to the info on this page . What if I run out of credits during the cohort? ​ While additional credits aren&#x27;t normally offered for cohort purposes, you can open a support ticket to explain your case if you run out during your cohort. Please use this template for the support ticket. How can I switch to a different cohort? ​ To switch cohorts, submit the Cohort Application Update form . This can be done during a cohort or after it ends (if you haven&#x27;t graduated). How do I change my Clay Email or Workspace ID? ​ If you need to update the Clay Email or Clay Workspace ID you submitted in your application form, please contact Support ( support@clay.com ). Include both your original Email and Workspace ID, as well as the new ones you’d like to use. What should I expect after applying? ​ Cohorts are exclusive and submitting an application doesn&#x27;t guarantee acceptance. You will be informed whether your application was accepted at least 1 week before the cohort start date. Can I join a cohort as part of my team? ​ Multiple users belonging to the same Clay workspa

## http://university.clay.com/docs/access-settings-for-connections

Access settings for connections - Clay Docs Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers All docs / Settings & admin / Access settings for connections Access settings for connections Determine who in the workspace is allowed to build with certain connections or MCP servers. Overview Note: This feature is currently in beta for Enterprise customers. ‍ Every connected account in Clay (e.g., Salesforce, OpenAI, Snowflake) has access controls, so you can determine who in the workspace is allowed to create workflows and columns with certain connections. Admins and connected account owners can determine who in the workspace is allowed to build with certain connections or MCP servers. When building workflows or columns in Clay, users will only see connections they have access to. All users in the workspace can run workflows and columns that are already set up. Managing connections as an admin Admins and connection owners can set allowlists per connection to control who in the workspace can configure actions with that connection. Setting permissions on a connection Navigate to Settings → Connections Find the connection you want to manage (e.g., OpenAI, Salesforce, HubSpot). Under access settings, choose one of the following options: Anyone in the workspace — All workspace members can configure columns or workflows with this connection Specific people and groups — Only admins and the people or user groups you name can configure workflows or columns with this connection If you selected Specific people and groups : Search for and add individual members or user groups who should have access Add user groups to grant access to all members of that group To remove access, simply remove individual members or groups from the allowlist. Click Save to apply the changes To update access later, just edit the connection and add or remove users or user groups from the allowlist. What users can and cannot do If a user does not have access to a connection, they can or cannot do the following across Clay: Not allowed ❌ Configure a workflow or column using that connection Edit existing column logic and mappings Duplicate the column or rename it Save it as a function (the function will be saved, but the connection will not be copied over — you&#x27;ll need to select a connection you have access to) Edit or reorder steps in a waterfall that uses that connection Leverage that connection for Claygent context or AI snippets in campaigns Allowed ✅ Run the column and view run info View column logic in read-only mode Swap the restricted connection to a different connection the user does have access to Edit table data and build derived tables/columns (unless in view-only mode) Controls by feature Columns If the column uses a connection the user doesn&#x27;t have access to, users can see the column logic in read-only mode. They can swap the restricted connection for one they have access to. Once they do, the column becomes fully editable under their credentials. Waterfalls A waterfall is a priority-ordered list of providers tried in sequence until one returns a usable result. A user&#x27;s ability to edit a waterfall depends on how many of connections in the waterfall they&#x27;re allowlisted for: Access level Enable/disable providers Edit provider settings Reorder / add steps Delete connections Swap connections No connection access ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ ✅ Mixed connection access ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ ✅ Full connection access ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ‍ Regardless of access state, users can always view the full waterfall configuration (providers, order, selected connections) and swap in connections they&#x27;re allowlisted for. Signals Signals follow the same access rules as a single column: The connection dropdown only shows connections the user is allowed to use. If the user doesn&#x27;t have access to the connection currently on the signal, the logic editor is read-only. They can swap in a connection they do have access to to unlock editing. Functions When building a function, you can only leverage connections you&#x27;re allowed to use When using an existing function, any columns that leverage connections a user doesn’t have access to appear as read only. Users must swap in their own key to unlock edit functionality. To prevent others from editing your function, use view-only permissions on the function itself until a more comprehensive permissions model is available. Claygent When creating a Claygent, connection access controls apply when adding documents or connecting data sources. When running an existing Claygent, users can only leverage connections they&#x27;re allowlisted for. For example, if you run a Claygent, it will use your own OpenAI connection rather than another user&#x27;s connection. Within the Claygent builder experience itself, no functionality is limited. Audiences, Sculptor, and Prospector Enrichment columns within bulk enrichment tables (Audiences) and Sculptor/Prospector surfaces follow the same access rules described above for individual columns and waterfalls. FAQs Can admins access every connection in the workspace? Admins do not, by default, have access to build workflows with every connection in the workspace. All admins can, however, add themselves to any connection in the workspace. Admins are always able to manage and view all connections in the workspace. What&#x27;s the default for new keys? Admins and connection owners must explicitly add users or user groups to build workflows and columns with that key. Can a user still run a column that uses a connection they don&#x27;t have access to? Yes. Controls are enforced at configuration time, not run time. Users can run existing columns and view run results even if they can&#x27;t edit the underlying logic of a column. What if I want to use a different connection for my own work? You can swap the restricted connection out for any connection you&#x27;re allowlisted for. This lets you run the same logic under your own credentials without changing it for others. What happens when an employee leaves the workspace? When a user is deactivated, their personal credentials are disabled by default. How do I set up controls for my workspace? Enterprise customers can configure allowlists independently or with the help of their Growth Strategist. ## http://university.clay.com/docs/actions-data-credits

Actions & Data Credits - Clay Docs Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers All docs / Getting started / Actions & Data Credits Actions & Data Credits Learn about credits, the virtual currency system used for running actions in Clay. Overview Clay uses two separate metrics to track your usage: Actions and Data Credits . Actions measure the orchestration you do in Clay: enriching data, running AI research, and sending data to other tools. Each Action costs a few tenths of a penny. Data Credits are used to buy data or AI from 3rd party vendors in Clay&#x27;s data marketplace—costs vary by data type. Each Data Credit costs a few pennies. This separation gives you transparency and control—you know exactly what you&#x27;re paying for. Quick comparison Actions Data credits What it measures Platform usage capacity Data marketplace purchases Cost per enrichment Always 1 action Varies (0.5–10+ credits based on data type) How to get more Upgrade action capacity tier Upgrade tier OR purchase one-time top-up Rollover No Yes (up to 2× monthly limit) How Actions and Data Credits work together Activity Actions Data credits Sourcing accounts and contacts No Yes (unless accessing free data or using your own API keys) Importing 1st party data into Clay No No Enriching accounts and contacts with net-new data (including signals) 1 per enrichment Yes (unless accessing free data or using your own API keys) Transforming data within Clay No No Using AI 1 per AI run Yes (unless using your own API keys) Exporting and executing GTM tasks 1 per record No Understanding Actions What are Actions? Actions measure when you use Clay to either enrich accounts/contacts with net-new data (e.g., enrichments from Clay&#x27;s data marketplace, AI web research, signals) or execute GTM work (e.g., send emails, sync to CRM, export ads audiences, write copy with AI). Each record enriched or exported counts as 1 Action—regardless of data source or provider. What consumes Actions? Features that use an Action: Each enrichment from any provider (e.g., "Find email via Hunter"). Using your own API keys (still counts as platform usage). AI uses Signals Executing GTM work: sending emails, posting to Slack, generating Notion briefs. Clay sequencer : 1 Action per lead added to campaign (not per email sent). External sequencer : 1 Action per record exported to the external sequencer. CRM exports and syncs (Salesforce, HubSpot, etc.). Data warehouse exports and syncs. HTTP API calls. Ads audience exports (e.g., LinkedIn, Facebook). Features that don&#x27;t use an Action: Sourcing lists of accounts or contacts (e.g., Find People returns 100 contacts). CRM imports (bringing data into Clay from your CRM). Data warehouse imports (bringing data into Clay from your warehouse). Webhook imports. Clay formulas and filters. Manual data entry. Using formulas for scoring and normalization. Sculptor. Creating audiences (only the export counts). How many Actions do I need? Your Actions capacity is determined by your plan tier. Plan tiers are designed so 90% of customers do not hit the limit of their Actions capacity. Plan Actions/month Best for Launch 15,000 Enriching ~10,000 records/year Growth 40,000 Enriching ~50,000 records/year Enterprise 100,000+ Enriching millions of records/year How to get more Actions Upgrade your plan tier in Settings → Plans & billing . Actions cannot be purchased as one-time top-ups because they represent fixed platform capacity tied to your plan&#x27;s tier. Understanding Data Credits What are Data Credits? Clay connects to 150+ data and AI providers. When you purchase data from these providers through Clay&#x27;s marketplace, you spend Data Credits. Think of Data Credits as: API call credits for data enrichments or AI use. A currency for buying data from the marketplace. The "fuel" that powers enrichments (when not using your own keys). Using your own API keys If you already subscribe to data providers (ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clearbit, etc.) or AI providers, connecting your API keys to Clay will eliminate the Data Credit cost. Note that an Action will still be consumed. How many Data Credits do I need? Each fully enriched record typically costs 6–20 Data Credits , depending on: The data types you enrich (emails are cheap, phone numbers are expensive). How many of your own API keys you use. Whether you&#x27;re using waterfalls with multiple providers. ‍ ‍ General guidelines: Plan Data Credits/month Best for Launch 2,500–10,000 ~1,000 records/month Growth 6,000–100,000 1,000–10,000 records/month Enterprise 100,000+ 10,000+ records/month Note: The more API keys you connect, the fewer Data Credits you&#x27;ll need. Example: Data Credits in practice Scenario: You want to enrich 100 contacts with LinkedIn profiles and emails. Using Clay&#x27;s data marketplace: Find 100 people (Clay database) → 0 Data Credits Enrich LinkedIn profiles → 50 Data Credits (0.5 per profile) Find emails (90% success) → 45 Data Credits (0.5 per email × 90) Validate emails (90% success) → 0 Data Credits (select validator providers are free in Clay under new pricing) Total Data Credits consumed: 95 Using your own email API key for steps 3–4: Total Data Credits consumed: 50 (just the LinkedIn enrichments) You saved 45 Data Credits by using your own key How to get more Data Credits Two options: 1. Upgrade your Data Credits tier (recommended) Go to Settings → Plans & billing . Select a higher Data Credits tier. No premium charged. 2. One-time top-up Available for emergency needs during your billing cycle. 30% premium applies. Subject to rollover limits. Data Credits for AI Data Credit pricing varies for AI models in Use AI , with rates determined by which model you select. Find out more in AI pricing doc. Data Credit costs are based on prompt and token usage. You can control spending by setting custom budgets for each run. Action and Data Credit usage To see detailed Data Credit consumption across your workspace, workbooks, and tables, visit the credit usage dashboard: Click your account name in the corner Go to Settings → Credit usage . For a complete guide on tracking and analyzing your Data Credit spend, see this doc . Workbook credit limits (Enterprise only) This feature is for users on the Enterprise Plan. Admins can set Data Credit spend limits for individual workbooks to control and monitor Data Credit usage at the workbook level. How to enable workbook credit limits: Open your workbook. In the settings panel, under Credit spend limit , click Manage . Toggle Enabled credit spend limit and add a number to Workbook limit . Click Save changes . Once enabled, all Actions run within that workbook will contribute to the workbook&#x27;s Data Credit spend. When the limit is reached, you&#x27;ll see an error message preventing further Actions from running. ‍ Note: Only workspace admins can modify workbook Data Credit limits. Editors and Viewers cannot manage Data Credit limits, even if they have editing access to the workbook. Rollover Data Credits Actions: No rollover Actions represent your fixed monthly capacity. Unused Actions expire at the end of each billing cycle. Why no rollover? Each plan tier is designed with sufficient capacity for typical use cases at tha

Overview ActiveCampaign is a customer experience automation platform that combines email marketing, marketing automation, and CRM capabilities. Using this integration, you can look up, create, and update information in ActiveCampaign directly within your Clay table. Enriching data with ActiveCampaign While in a Clay table, click Add enrichment and search for ActiveCampaign . Under Integrations , select one of the ActiveCampaign options. In the modal, you will be asked to Select ActiveCampaign account . If you haven&#x27;t already connected your ActiveCampaign account, click + Add account and go through authentication. Action Create object Creates a new object in your ActiveCampaign. Inputs : Object type : Account or Contact For Account : Company name Website (Optional) Owner (Optional) Description (Optional) Address (Optional) Number of Employees (Optional) Annual Revenue (Optional) Industry/Vertical (Optional) Phone Number (Optional) For Contact : Email First Name (Optional) Last Name (Optional) Phone Number (Optional) Action Update object Updates an existing object in ActiveCampaign. Inputs : Object type : Account or Contact Object ID : ID of the object you want to update. For Account : Company name Website (Optional) Owner (Optional) Description (Optional) Address (Optional) Number of Employees (Optional) Annual Revenue (Optional) Industry/Vertical (Optional) Phone Number (Optional) For Contact : Email First Name (Optional) Last Name (Optional) Phone Number (Optional) Action Lookup object Finds an object in ActiveCampaign. Inputs : Object Type : Account or Contact Filter Type : ActiveCampaign ID or Email Action Create an association Links a contact to an account in ActiveCampaign. Inputs : Contact ID Account ID Job Title (Optional) Action Add to automation Adds a contact to an automation workflow in ActiveCampaign. Inputs : Contact ID Automation ID Run settings Auto-update Only run if: The enrichment will only run if conditions are met. ## http://university.clay.com/docs/ai-in-clay

AI in Clay - Clay Docs Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers All docs / Getting started / AI in Clay AI in Clay A comprehensive guide to how Clay uses AI across its features. Overview A comprehensive guide to how Clay uses AI across its features, with a focus on data privacy, security, and responsible AI practices. Your data is never used for AI model training. Clay has contractual agreements with all AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others) that strictly prohibit using customer data to train their models. Core AI principles Clay is committed to transparent and responsible AI use. Here&#x27;s what you need to know: No training on your data : Customer data is never used to train Clay&#x27;s AI models or those of our AI providers. Enterprise-grade security : Industry-standard encryption for data at rest and in transit, with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliance. You control your data : As a data processor, Clay only uses your data to provide services to you. Transparent partnerships : Full list of AI subprocessors available at trust.clay.com . AI features in Clay Email sequencer What it does : Email Sequencer is Clay&#x27;s built-in email outreach tool that lets you run email campaigns directly from your tables, using AI to create personalized messaging at scale. View Email Sequencer documentation → How AI is used : AI generates email copy based on your business context and prospect information. AI snippets within messages automatically create personalized content using lead data. Content generation happens in real-time when you create campaigns. Data privacy : Your campaign data and prospect information are processed only to generate your email content. No data is retained by AI providers after processing. Data is not used to train models or shared with other Clay customers. You can optionally use your own API keys with supported providers. Message drafting What it does : AI-powered message drafting within Clay tables helps you create personalized outreach messages for individual prospects. View Email sequencer documentation → How AI is used : AI reads context from your table columns (company info, prospect details, etc.). Generates tailored messages based on your prompts and business context. Uses your "My Business Context" settings to maintain brand voice. Data privacy : Only the specific table data you select is sent to AI models. Messages are generated on-demand and data is not retained post-processing. No training occurs on your messaging or prospect data. Access is controlled by Clay&#x27;s role-based permissions. Use AI action What it does : A powerful table action that gives you access to AI for web research, content generation, and image generation. View Use AI documentation → How AI is used : Web research : AI searches and synthesizes information from the web. Content generation : Transforms unstructured text (like call transcripts) into structured data. Image generation : Creates images based on text prompts. Model options : Access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other leading AI providers. Option to bring your own API keys for supported providers. MCP (Model Context Protocol) server support when using your own keys. Different models offer different capabilities (document upload, specialized research, etc.). Data privacy : Data from your table rows is only sent to AI when you explicitly run the action. You control which columns are included as context. Contractual agreements prohibit training on customer data. Claygents What it does : Build repeatable AI agents for web research and prospecting that can navigate websites, extract information, and make decisions. View Claygent builder documentation → How AI is used : AI agents follow your instructions to research prospects, companies, or topics. Navigate web pages and extract specific information. Make intelligent decisions about which sources to consult. Data privacy : Claygents process data row-by-row as they run. Research results are stored in your table, under your control. No customer data used for training agent capabilities. Sculptor What it does : A chat interface for Clay that helps with table building, debugging, and analysis using conversational AI. View Sculptor documentation → How AI is used : Reads your "My Business Context" to understand your goals. Accesses information in your current table to provide relevant help. Suggests formulas, identifies issues, and helps analyze data. Data privacy : Only accesses the specific table you&#x27;re working in. Uses table metadata and visible data to provide context-aware assistance. Chat history and table context are not used for training. Data is processed transiently to provide real-time assistance. Formula generator What it does : AI-powered tool that helps you create Clay formulas using natural language. How AI is used : Converts your natural language description into working formulas. Understands Clay&#x27;s formula syntax and functions. Suggests appropriate formulas based on your use case. Data privacy : Only your formula description and relevant table schema are sent to AI. Actual row data is not transmitted. Generated formulas are not used to train models. Processing is instantaneous with no data retention. API generator What it does : Helps you build HTTP API requests using AI, making it easier to connect to external services. View HTTP API documentation → How AI is used : Generates API request configurations based on your description. Understands common API patterns and authentication methods. Suggests appropriate parameters and headers. Data privacy : Only your API description is sent to AI models. API keys and credentials are never sent to AI providers. Generated configurations are not used for training. Debug with AI What it does : When errors occur in Clay, AI helps diagnose and suggest fixes using error logs and Clay documentation. How AI is used : Analyzes error messages and logs. References Clay&#x27;s documentation to suggest solutions. Provides step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. Data privacy : Only error logs and relevant system information are sent to AI. Personal data in your tables is not included in debug requests. Error analysis is done in real-time with no retention. Debug data is not used to train models. Find companies with natural language What it does : An import feature that lets you describe your ideal customer profile (ICP) and searches Clay&#x27;s database of 50M+ companies. How AI is used : Interprets your natural language ICP description. Converts your criteria into database queries. Ranks and filters companies based on fit. Data privacy : Only your ICP description is processed by AI. Search results come from Clay&#x27;s company database, not your data. Your search criteria are not shared with other customers. No training occurs on your ICP descriptions. Data Security and Compliance Encryption At rest : All customer data is encrypted using industry-standard encryption. In transit : TLS 1.2/1.3 encryption for all data transmission. Access controls : Role-based permissions control who can access your data. Compliance Certifications SOC 2 Type II : Active certification for security and privacy controls. ISO 270

## http://university.clay.com/docs/ai-pricing

How AI is priced - Clay Docs Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers All docs / Getting started / How AI is priced How AI is priced This guide explains how each works, which models they apply to, and how credits are calculated. Overview Clay uses two pricing structures for AI models—fixed and variable—so you pay based on actual usage. This guide explains how each works, which models they apply to, and how credits are calculated. Two pricing structures Fixed AI pricing charges a flat number of data credits per task. It applies to 80% of models in Clay, including all of Clay&#x27;s own models (Neon, Helium, Argon). The cost is exact and known before you run. Variable AI pricing charges data credits based on the actual cost of each run, with 0% markup . It applies to 20% of models—the most advanced reasoning models available in Clay, typically used for sophisticated web-research tasks with multi-step reasoning—where the underlying compute cost can vary significantly from one prompt to the next. You&#x27;ll see the exact cost per row in your Clay table once the run is completed. Rather than setting a flat rate high enough to cover the most expensive use cases—which would overcharge most users—variable pricing ensures each task is priced according to what it actually costs to run. This blended model of fixed and variable pricing results in customers paying less overall for AI in Clay. You can always see which pricing structure applies when selecting a model in the product. ‍ Select model pricing reference Provider Model Content Generation Web Research Clay Helium — 1 Argon — 3 OpenAI GPT-4o 1 variable GPT-4.1 1 variable GPT-5.1 2 variable GPT-5 Mini 0.4 1 GPT-5 Nano 0.2 0.5 o3 5 variable Anthropic Claude 4.5 Haiku 1 variable Claude 4.5 Sonnet 1.5 variable Claude 4.6 Opus 7.5 variable Gemini 2.5 Pro 3 variable 2.5 Flash 0.5 1 2.5 Flash Lite 0.5 1 Costs are in data credits. How variable pricing works Data credit formula: Credit Charge = Actual LLM Cost ($) ÷ Workspace Cost Per Credit ($) The actual LLM cost is the cost charged by the AI provider of the model you&#x27;ve selected. Clay applies 0% markup on variable AI pricing for the most sophisticated reasoning models. Your cost per credit (CPC) is determined by your subscription plan. What happens during a run Withhold. Clay withholds an estimated number of data credits upfront—based on the 75th percentile of past runs for that model—multiplied by the number of rows. Execute. The model processes your task. Calculate. Clay calculates the actual LLM cost for each row. Reconcile. The withheld amount is compared to the actual cost. Any surplus is refunded; any additional cost is deducted. You only pay for what was used. Every AI prompt counts as one action . The variable component affects only the data credit cost of that action. Balance protection If your data credit balance reaches zero during a run, processing stops. You will never be charged beyond your available balance. Rows that haven&#x27;t started will not run, and results from completed rows are retained. Fixed vs. variable: a comparison The example below details a fixed vs variable AI model being run on 100 rows in Clay. The fixed rate model is priced at 1 credit per row. The variable rate model withholds 1 credit per row as an estimate, but after running the realized cost is only 0.8 credits. Fixed Pricing Variable Pricing Starting balance 100 credits 100 credits Start of run Charges 100 credits Withholds 100 credits End of run — Refunds 20 credits Ending balance 0 credits 20 credits In this scenario, the variable model&#x27;s withholding mechanism protects both the customer and Clay from unexpected cost overruns—while returning unused credits at the end. Using your own API keys You can always use your own API keys instead of Clay data credits. That said, many customers prefer Clay&#x27;s built-in AI for two reasons: Model selection. Clay gives you access to a broader set of models than any single provider. Speed. Actual usage data shows that AI tasks run through Clay&#x27;s APIs run up to 2× faster than tasks run through customers&#x27; own API keys because Clay has negotiated significantly higher rate limits than most customers have independently. FAQs How do I know if a model uses fixed or variable pricing? The product displays the pricing type when you select a model. Fixed-price models show a flat credit cost (e.g., 3/row ), while variable-price models show an estimate (e.g., ~2) with a note that the final charge depends on actual usage. Will I always know what a task will cost before I run it? For fixed-price models, yes—the cost shown is exact. For variable-price models, you&#x27;ll see an estimate upfront. The final cost may differ, but credits are withheld before the run starts so there are no surprises to your balance. Could a variable-priced task cost significantly more than the estimate? In most cases, the final cost will be at or below the estimate. Complex, multi-step tasks can cost more, but these are a small minority of runs. Most customers pay less under variable pricing than they would under a flat rate for the same model. Customers who are configuring complex, multi-step web research tasks may wish to run their prompt on 10 or 50 rows so they are able to see the credit charge for each row before running the prompt across their full table. What happens if I run out of data credits mid-run? Processing stops when your balance reaches zero. You won&#x27;t be charged beyond your available credits. Rows that haven&#x27;t started will not run; rows that completed successfully retain their results. Why not just use fixed pricing for everything? Advanced reasoning models have high cost variability from task to task. A fixed rate would need to be high enough to cover the most expensive use cases—overcharging the majority of users on simpler work. Variable pricing ensures every task is priced according to its actual cost. Does Clay charge a markup on variable AI pricing? No. Clay charges 0% markup on variable AI pricing for reasoning models. You pay exactly what Clay pays the AI provider, making this the most fair and customer-friendly pricing possible. ## http://university.clay.com/docs/ai-tokens

AI Tokens - Clay Docs Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers All docs / Gen AI / AI Tokens AI Tokens Understand AI Tokens Overview Understanding AI Tokens In the world of Large Language Models (LLMs), tokens are the fundamental building blocks for processing and understanding text. Think of tokens as small chunks, each typically representing 3-4 characters. A 100-word passage generally breaks down into approximately 125–135 tokens . When working with AI models, you&#x27;ll encounter two types: Input tokens : The prompts you send to the AI. Output tokens : The AI’s generated response. Note: In Clay, you can control usage by setting a maximum output length in your model configuration. What Is TPM? TPM (Tokens Per Minute) refers to how many tokens a model can process within one minute—across both input and output. Different features and providers have different TPM requirements, often tied to your API tier. API tier requirements ChatGPT Generate Text Requirement : 30,000 TPM Access : Works with any paid tier as long as the API key has access to GPT-4 or GPT-4 Turbo (Note: Free-tier or unpaid OpenAI keys may not have access) ClayGent Web Research OpenAI : Requires Tier 2 or higher (≥450,000 TPM) Anthropic : Requires Tier 4 or higher (≥400,000 TPM) Gemini : Requires Tier 2 , but only works with the Gemini 2.0 Flash model Gemini 1.5 models may require additional access through Vertex AI or custom tiers Upgrade API tier If you need higher token limits or access to advanced features, you&#x27;ll need to upgrade your API tier with your chosen provider. Here&#x27;s how to find more information on upgrading, with each major provider. OpenAI Anthropic Gemini Monitoring API Usage Each platform provides tools to track your usage: OpenAI Anthropic Gemini AI pricing in Clay When using AI features in Clay, you&#x27;ll consume both Actions and Data Credits : Actions : Each AI enrichment consumes 1 Action (platform orchestration work) Data Credits : Cost varies by model—Clay offers both fixed and variable AI pricing Clay uses two pricing structures for AI models: Fixed pricing : A flat number of data credits per task (applies to most models, including Clay&#x27;s own models like Neon, Helium, and Argon) Variable pricing : Data credits based on actual token usage plus a 20% premium (applies to advanced reasoning models used for sophisticated web research) You can control AI spending by: Setting maximum output length in your model configuration Setting custom budgets for each run Choosing more cost-effective models for simpler tasks Selecting fixed-price models when cost predictability is important To learn more about how AI is priced in Clay, see our guide on how AI is priced . Clay credits vs. personal API keys When you&#x27;re using Clay&#x27;s AI tools, you have two options for managing your API access: using Clay credits or connecting your own personal API keys. Each option has different benefits and considerations in terms of cost, convenience, and management requirements. Let&#x27;s explore these options: Clay credits Clay manages rate limits, tier access, and scaling for you No need to worry about upgrading API tiers manually Pricing varies by model (fixed or variable depending on which model you select) Cost visibility in Clay UI shows data credit consumption Personal API Keys Can reduce data credit costs (you only pay Actions, not Data Credits) Requires meeting provider-specific tier requirements You manage your own API billing directly with the provider ‍ Note: When using a personal API key, price breakdowns won't appear in the Clay UI. You'll need to monitor your usage and upgrade tiers manually. Overview Airtable Overview The Airtable integration lets you sync data within your Clay table with your Airtable bases. With this integration you’re able to: Create records Lookup records Update records Upsert records Setting up Airtable and Clay To get set up, you’ll need to add your Airtable account to Clay from either the enrichment panel or the Settings > Connections page. Make sure your linked Airtable account has the right level of access to the bases you want to connect with Clay. Available Actions with the Airtable Integration Action Create records Create and push a new record to your Airtable directly from Clay. Input Fields : Base ID (Required): The ID for the Airtable Base you’d like to create the record in. Additional Fields : Any other fields you want to include as part of the record. Action Lookup records Check if a specific record exists in your Airtable. Input Fields : Base ID (Required): The ID for the Airtable Base you’d like to search within. Lookup Criteria : Fields or criteria to define which record to look up. Action Update records Modify an existing record in Airtable. Input Fields : Base ID (Required): The ID for the Airtable Base you’d like to update. Record ID : The unique ID of the record to update. Fields to Update : Specify the fields and values to modify. Action Upsert records Create or update a record in Airtable based on matching values. Input Fields : Base ID (Required): The ID for the Airtable Base where you want to perform the upsert. Match Criteria : Fields to match for determining whether to insert or update. Fields to Include/Update : Specify fields and values to include in the operation. ‍ Table of contents TOC Heading TOC Heading Plan Explore other docs Audiences (Beta) View article View article View article Settings & admin User groups User groups let you share Clay workbooks and connected accounts with multiple members at once. ## http://university.clay.com/docs/apify-integration-overview

Apify integration - Clay Docs Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers All docs / Find / Apify integration Apify integration Web scraping and automation platform providing data for AI and custom solutions. Overview Apify Integration Overview With Clay’s Apify integration, you can quickly retrieve data from Apify actor runs or launch actors directly in Clay to get results on demand. Setting up in Apify Login to Apify to select an actor. Select the scraper, and click Create Task . This will add it to your library of actors. Switch from Manual to JSON and copy the body text. This will serve as your input data in Clay when you run the actor. Connecting to Apify in Clay You can connect your Apify account to Clay in two ways: Method 1: Connect Apify account within enrichment panel When running an Apify integration in Clay, you’ll be prompted to Add account . Add your API key and name it to create an account. You can find your API token on the Integrations page in the Apify Console. Method 2: Connect Apify account through Clay settings : Navigate to Settings > Connections in your Clay dashboard. Click on Add Connection and select Apify from the list. Enter your Apify API key to establish the connection. Using the Apify integration Step 1: Choose Apify integration To connect Apify as a source: In a workbook, click + Add at the bottom. Search for Apify and select from the results. If you are using Apify as an enrichment for an existing table, access the enrichment search bar by selecting Add enrichment in the top right corner. Type in “Apify” in the search bar and select Run Apify Actor . Step 2: Select Apify account Within the enrichment pane, select your Apify account, and add your account if you haven’t already. Step 3: Select Apify actor and configure input data Select the Apify actor you want to run. Then In the Input Data section, you’ll need to specify the data the actor will use. Enter the data body in JSON format. When referencing column tokens (dynamic data from your Clay table), ensure the key is in quotes, but do not put quotes around the token itself. For example: Step 4: Configure run settings If you want to only run this enrichment under set circumstances, you are able to input formulas where the column runs only if the formula is true. Autoupdate: By default, the auto-update automatically enriches new rows when they were added to the table. Make sure to toggle this step off if you do not want to auto-update, however, you might run into stale data problems. Conditional run: If you want to only run this enrichment under set circumstances, you are able to input formulas where the column runs only if the formula is true. Learn more about conditional runs in this Clay University lesson . Now you can run your Apify actor within your Clay table! Utilizing your Apify data Click into the Source Cell for overlapping accounts to see all the data you pulled in from your Apify actor. From here, you can create new columns with the data or reference this data in an enrichment. ‍ Table of contents TOC Heading TOC Heading Plan Explore other docs Audiences (Beta) View article View article View article Settings & admin User groups User groups let you share Clay workbooks and connected accounts with multiple members at once.
