lesson About this lesson 00:00 Create Multi-Step Sequence Messaging with Twain In the last lesson we covered AI Snippets . These are a modular, high-control approach to generating content where you can customize every part of a message. But what if you don&#x27;t want or need to customize every step? What if you&#x27;re looking for a lower-friction way to start your outbound sequences… and just want the AI to generate full email copy for you? That&#x27;s exactly what the Twain enrichment is for. 🧩 How Twain Structures Your Messaging Instead of asking AI to generate a single block of text, Twain walks the model through a multi-step process , typically including: Subject Line Intro Line Body or Value Prop Call to Action (CTA) PS or Signature (optional) And it can automatically use the enriched data in your Clay table, like: Company name and description Job title Recent funding Tech stack Or any other signals you&#x27;ve pulled in All that data gets plugged into a structured template behind the scenes. ✅ When to Use Twain Twain is a good solution when: You want full email copy, not just snippets You need to ensure you&#x27;re not overloading AI with too much unstructured data You still need to customize tone, length, or structure You want outputs that are clean, modular, and easy to edit 🔄 Using Twain with Your Research Data Let&#x27;s go back to our previous example. We&#x27;ve got our leads and we&#x27;ve done some research. Now we want to start sending personalized outbound messages. Using the same leads we want to contact, let&#x27;s look at what this looks like with Twain. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Setup Process Here&#x27;s how to set up your sequence: Choose your sequence type: Select a pre-defined sequence (1-4 steps) from the dropdown menu If you have a Twain account, you can use your own sequence by selecting your Twain account and entering a sequence ID Configure your prompt parameters: Add your prospect description Define your outreach signal Describe your ideal customer profile State the problem you&#x27;re solving And more… Add your prospect information: Enter first name, last name, and social media profile URL for each prospect Don&#x27;t have social media profile URLs? Use Claygent to find them using prospect emails Map and execute: Map Twain&#x27;s multi-step messages to your Clay columns Run the table to generate your sequences 🤔 AI Snippets vs. Twain: When to Use Each This might leave you wondering – when should you use AI snippets vs Twain? Use AI Snippets when you want full control and flexibility at the sentence level Use Twain when you want a faster , more structured way to generate outbound messaging at scale Both are powerful. Choose the one that best fits your workflow. Experiment with both. Scale what works. 💼 Benefits of a Multi-Step Approach The multi-step approach that Twain uses offers several key advantages: Better structure : By breaking the generation process into discrete steps, the AI focuses on one task at a time, producing more coherent results Improved personalization : Each step can incorporate different aspects of your prospect data Easier editing : If you don&#x27;t like a particular part of the message, you can regenerate just that section Sequence consistency : Ensures your follow-up messages maintain a consistent voice and approach 🌟 Real-World Applications Beyond basic outbound sequences, you can use Twain for: Multi-touch campaigns that gradually build on previous messages Post-event follow-up sequences Re-engagement campaigns for dormant prospects Content distribution sequences that share different resources over time 🔮 What&#x27;s Coming Next We&#x27;ve covered effortless output when it comes to writing copy. There&#x27;s still a number of creation workflows, like video, slides, and more. We&#x27;ll cover those in future lessons. As you move forward with your AI-powered GTM automation, remember that the tools and techniques we&#x27;ve covered in the FETC framework work together as a system. The Find, Enrich, and Transform steps all feed into your Create step, giving you the data and structure you need to generate high-quality, personalized content at scale. About this lesson 00:00 Create Personalized Content at Scale We talked about the philosophy behind Create, how AI helps distill large amounts of data into high-quality, focused content. Now it&#x27;s time to put that into practice. In this lesson, we&#x27;ll show you how to create personalized content at scale using modular AI Snippets in Clay. 🌐 Applications of Create Across Your GTM Motion We can create personalized content across your entire GTM motion: Ad copy for account-based marketing campaigns Direct messages across social media platforms Content for blog posts, landing pages, or social media posts And of course, highly tailored sales emails The most common use case is outbound messaging. And with Clay, you can take a deep personalization table and create dynamic snippets tailored not just to the person, but to the hypothesis you&#x27;re running. 📈 The Evolution of Personalization In the past, personalization meant using simple variables like: "I see you&#x27;re working at {{company}}" Now, the personalization is richer, more dynamic — and powered by AI: {{subj line}} : "Congrats on the new GTM hire" {{body}} : "Saw you closed out Q1 with a 2x jump in pipeline. Curious how the team&#x27;s prioritizing RevOps this quarter?" You&#x27;re still using a template. You&#x27;ll have sections like intro, body, close, ask… but now each variable can contain an entire AI-generated sentence or phrase. You can even change tone and voice using dynamic prompting. This means adjusting copy depending on whether you&#x27;re writing to a VP or an individual contributor. 💪 Benefits of AI-Powered Snippets This approach helps you: Enhance email deliverability Adjust tone and voice per persona Increase message quality without writing every word yourself 🧠 Scaling Strategy, Not Just Messages The real power of AI Snippets is how they reflect your hypotheses , not just your data. For example: If you think a company values innovation, you can generate a subject line that highlights that If you&#x27;re targeting accounts with closed/won pipeline growth, your intro can reference their velocity If someone&#x27;s on the ASU board and you&#x27;re a fellow alum, your CTA can reflect shared context Each variable becomes a reflection of why this person was selected in the first place. 🔬 Example: Personalized Email Intros at Scale Let&#x27;s say you&#x27;re reaching out to 100 marketing leaders at recently funded SaaS startups. You&#x27;ve pulled in: Company descriptions Job changes Funding round details Personal bios Using AI Snippets, you can generate: A subject line based on their funding news A personalized intro based on their latest hire A CTA that reflects the growth stage of their team All without writing a single line of copy by hand. 📋 Implementation in Clay Let&#x27;s see what this looks like in Clay: Start with a deep personalization table Begin with your list of prospects Enrich with social profiles to get detailed information Use AI formulas to transform the enriched data Apply Claygent to find additional context (thought leadership, blogs, interviews) Create modular AI Snippets Generate subject lines that reference specific insights Craft personalized intros based on research findings Develop custom P.S. lines that connect on a personal level Combine into complete messages Use formula columns to combine snippets into cohesive messages Maintain consistent core messaging where appropriate Preview and refine your results 🚀 The Power of Scaling What Works With Clay, you&#x27;re not writing 100 emails. You&#x27;re writing one great play — and then letting AI turn it into 100 unique, relevant messages. That&#x27;s what scaling personalization looks like. You identify what works, and then apply it systematically across your entire prospect list. 🔮 What&#x27;s Coming Next In the next lesson we&#x27;ll show you how to take these snippets and stitch them into complete emails, faster and with better copy, using tools like Twain . 💡 Conclusion Traditional personalization has always faced a fundamental tradeoff between scale and depth. With AI Snippets, you get both and more: Deeper personalization : Each message can reference specific, nuanced details about your prospect Greater scale : You can reach more people without sacrificing quality Consistent messaging : Your core value proposition remains clear and focused Testable hypotheses : You can systematically track which personalization approaches work best By breaking messages into modular components, you gain both flexibility and control, allowing you to maintain your brand voice while adapting to each prospect&#x27;s unique context. Progress Intro to CRM Enrichment ✔ 1 Intro to CRM Enrichment Importing from your CRM ✔ 2 Importing from your CRM Clay x HubSpot Actions ✔ 3 Clay x HubSpot Actions Clay x Salesforce Actions ✔ 4 Clay x Salesforce Actions Enriching your CRM Data ✔ 5 Enriching your CRM Data Keeping your CRM data fresh ✔ 6 Keeping your CRM data fresh Taking action on enriched CRM data ✔ 7 Taking action on enriched CRM data Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / CRM Enrichment / Enriching your CRM Data Lesson 5 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Enriching your CRM Data Introduction In our previous lesson, we covered the technical foundations of CRM enrichment: connecting Clay to your CRM, importing contacts, and understanding the different actions available in HubSpot and Salesforce. Now we&#x27;re getting into the strategic execution: how to actually build enrichment workflows that transform your raw contact data into actionable intelligence. By the end of this lesson, you&#x27;ll have a comprehensive playbook for turning basic contact information into the rich, contextual data your sales team needs to have meaningful conversations and drive better sales outcomes. 🔑 The Power of CRM Contact ID You can unlock tremendous enrichment value just by using the CRM contact ID as your starting point. This single identifier acts as a master key that unlocks a treasure trove of data about both the contact and their company, making it incredibly efficient to build comprehensive profiles from minimal starting information. The contact ID connects to your CRM&#x27;s existing data while enabling you to layer on external intelligence from multiple sources. This approach ensures you&#x27;re building on your existing data foundation rather than starting from scratch, which maximizes efficiency and maintains data consistency. Let&#x27;s walk through some of the most valuable and common enrichment use cases that GTM teams use to drive revenue results. 📈 Use Case 1: Enriching New Inbound Leads When inbound leads enter your CRM, you often know very little beyond their name and email address. This minimal information creates challenges for effective qualification and routing, making enrichment crucial for converting inbound interest into qualified opportunities. Note: This use case is covered in depth in our Inbound Automation course, where you can learn the complete workflow and advanced techniques. The Foundation Identifiers Contact Email and LinkedIn URLs serve as the golden identifiers that unlock most other enrichment possibilities. These two data points provide reliable connections to external databases and social profiles that contain comprehensive professional information. Use waterfall enrichment strategies to maximize coverage across multiple data providers. If one source doesn&#x27;t have complete information, the waterfall automatically tries additional sources until you get comprehensive data or exhaust all options. You can extract the company domain directly from the email address to enable company-level enrichments that provide organizational context for individual contacts. The domain data then allows you to enrich company size, industry, technology stack, and other firmographic data that influences qualification and messaging. 🔄 Use Case 2: Updating Existing Contacts with Enriched Data Updating existing contacts with new enriched data requires more sophisticated workflow logic to prevent data conflicts and maintain CRM integrity. The Safe Update Process First, run the Lookup action to identify contacts that already exist in your CRM. Then, create a conditional run formula for Create or Update actions so you&#x27;re not executing both operations unnecessarily. Only Create a new record if the Lookup doesn&#x27;t return anything, and only Update if specific conditions are met. Critical Scenarios to Avoid There are two main problems that can derail update workflows: Credit Waste and Data Overwriting : If conditionals aren&#x27;t configured correctly, you might end up overwriting valid existing data while unnecessarily spending enrichment credits on records that don&#x27;t need updates. Manual Data Conflicts : Be careful about updating fields that are manually maintained by your sales team. Accidentally overwriting manually-entered notes, custom scores, or relationship information can delete valuable institutional knowledge stored in your CRM. Implementation Best Practices Before setting up any update workflow, take time to understand why and how each field is being used by different team members. Document which fields are automatically managed versus manually maintained, and create update rules that respect these distinctions. Consider implementing confidence scoring for enriched data, only updating fields when new information has higher confidence than existing data. This prevents low-quality automated data from overwriting high-quality manual entries. 🚨 Use Case 3: Detecting Contact Job Changes This represents one of the most powerful signal-based enrichment workflows you can implement, providing real-time intelligence about prospect and customer career movements that create new opportunities. The Job Change Detection Process The systematic process for identifying job changes looks like this: Pull existing contacts from your CRM along with their social media URLs. If you don&#x27;t already have social media URLs stored, Clay offers waterfall enrichments that can find these easily using just email addresses or names. Enrich each person using their email and social media profile to get current company information, job title, and employment status. Compare the current company domain from social media with the company domain stored in your CRM to identify discrepancies. Flag mismatches as potential job changes and route these flagged contacts to your sales team for immediate follow-up. Update contacts in your CRM with new emails and job titles as needed to maintain data accuracy. You can use similar logic to detect internal role changes within the same company, identifying contacts who&#x27;ve been promoted to decision-making roles or moved to departments that might need your solution. Job change detection creates natural conversation starters for re-engagement and helps you identify new opportunities at both the contact&#x27;s previous company and new company. 🏢 Company-Level Enrichment Strategies Company enrichment enables sophisticated account-based marketing and sales strategies by providing comprehensive organizational intelligence that informs targeting and messaging decisions. Company Scoring Use native scoring and/or formulas to automatically score and qualify companies based on your ideal customer profile. This systematic approach ensures consistent evaluation across all prospects and customers. this lesson also appears in Clay 101, Automated Inbound, and CRM Enrichment, so feel free to skim or skip if you&#x27;ve already seen it somewhere else ‍ Now that you’ve gathered a wealth of company and contact data, it’s time to clean it all up. Getting data is just the first part of the journey. But if you’ve worked with data in the past, then you know that “garbage in leads to garbage out”. Luckily, with some clever native integrations we’ve built into Clay - you can turn “garbage” data into “golden” data. Let&#x27;s explore how these tools can transform your workflow. ‍ 🛠️ Our Data Cleaning Arsenal ‍ Nestled within our enrichment panel, under the "Tools" section, you&#x27;ll find a treasure trove of functions designed to manipulate and clean your data. These tools go beyond what AI formulas alone can offer, providing specialized solutions for common data challenges. View all your cleaning data functions in the tools modal 🏷️ Normalizing Company Names: A Game-Changer One of our most popular cleaning tools addresses a common pain point: inconsistent company names. How often have you encountered company names cluttered with legal suffixes or unnecessary prefixes? Our normalize company names function tackles this issue head-on. For instance, "Panamax Inc." becomes simply "Panamax," and "Cora, a company of blank" is streamlined to "Cora." This clean-up not only makes your data more uniform but also prepares it for seamless use in email copy or other communications. Utilizing the “Normalize company names” function to clean up company data 📞 Beyond Company Names: Versatile Normalization Our normalization tools extend far beyond company names: Text Whitespace : Ensure consistent spacing across all your text data. Phone Numbers : Standardize formats, removing or adding parentheses as needed. Locations : Create uniformity in how addresses and locations are represented. These are just a few examples – we encourage you to explore the full range of normalization options available in Clay. ‍ 🚀 Putting It Into Practice Let&#x27;s walk through a quick example of how to use our normalize company names function: Navigate to the enrichment panel and locate the "Tools" section. Scroll past the AI options to find our pre-built functions. Select "Normalize Company Names." Choose the appropriate input column (in this case, the company name from your companies table). Optionally, you can normalize the case and add additional fields as needed. Run the action across your rows. The result? Clean, consistent company names ready for your next campaign or analysis. ‍ 🌟 Unlocking the Potential of Clean Data By leveraging Clay&#x27;s data cleaning and normalization tools, you&#x27;re setting yourself up for success. Clean data leads to more accurate analyses, more effective outreach, and ultimately, better business outcomes. Remember, while we&#x27;ve highlighted some key features here, there&#x27;s always more to explore. We encourage you to dive into our various normalization options and discover how they can enhance your specific workflows. Data cleaning might not be the most glamorous part of data management, but with Clay&#x27;s tools, it can be surprisingly straightforward – and even enjoyable. Happy data cleaning! Progress Introduction to TAM Sourcing ✔ 1 Introduction to TAM Sourcing Understanding your ICP ✔ 2 Understanding your ICP TAM Sourcing Workflows in Clay ✔ 3 TAM Sourcing Workflows in Clay Advanced TAM Sourcing Techniques ✔ 4 Advanced TAM Sourcing Techniques Activating your TAM: From Intelligence to Revenue ✔ 5 Activating your TAM: From Intelligence to Revenue SMB TAM Sourcing ✔ 6 SMB TAM Sourcing Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers ✔ 7 Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / TAM Sourcing / Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers Lesson 7 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers 🔍 Third-Party Scrapers: Accessing Hidden Market Intelligence Introduction Previously, we covered advanced TAM sourcing techniques using Clay&#x27;s native capabilities. Today, we&#x27;re expanding your toolkit with third-party scrapers like Apify and Phantombuster to access data sources that traditional B2B providers simply can&#x27;t reach. By the end of this lesson, you&#x27;ll know exactly when and how to use these powerful tools to build comprehensive TAM databases from virtually any corner of the internet, creating competitive advantages through unique market intelligence. 🔍 The Gaps in Traditional B2B Data Traditional B2B data providers like ZoomInfo and Apollo excel at capturing enterprise companies with strong digital footprints, active social media presence, and structured business profiles. But they systematically miss entire market segments that could be goldmines for your business. Think about local businesses like restaurants, medical practices, and retail stores. These companies often have minimal social media presence but significant revenue potential. They&#x27;re running successful operations with real budgets but remain invisible in standard B2B databases. Consider niche industries with specialized directories, geographic markets with region-specific business listings, and real-time signals like job postings, product launches, or pricing changes that indicate immediate buying opportunities. Traditional providers update quarterly or monthly, far too slow to capitalize on these timing-sensitive signals. 🌐 The Untapped Data Universe The internet contains far more business data than any single provider can capture or commercialize. Every industry has its own ecosystem of information sources that traditional aggregators don&#x27;t touch. Review sites like Yelp, G2, and Capterra contain thousands of businesses with rich behavioral data that traditional firmographic databases can&#x27;t provide. The challenge isn&#x27;t necessarily finding this data but collecting it systematically and at scale. Manual copying from websites doesn&#x27;t scale beyond a handful of prospects. That&#x27;s where tools like Apify, Phantombuster, and Chrome scrapers provide the infrastructure for systematic data collection. ⚡ Apify: Systematic Web Data Collection Apify is the most powerful option for systematic data collection from virtually any website, turning unstructured web pages into structured datasets you can analyze and enrich. The Actor Library Apify&#x27;s library contains over 2,000 pre-built actors, ready-made scrapers optimized for popular platforms. Want to scrape Instagram business profiles for follower counts and engagement rates? There&#x27;s an actor for that. Need company data from social media including employee counts and recent posts? There&#x27;s an actor for that too. This extensive library means you rarely need to build scrapers from scratch. Practical Restaurant POS Example Here&#x27;s a concrete example demonstrating Apify&#x27;s TAM expansion power. Say you&#x27;re targeting local restaurants for point-of-sale software. Traditional B2B providers might give you 20% market coverage because most independent restaurants don&#x27;t appear in business databases. With Apify, you can scrape Yelp for restaurants in specific zip codes, extract contact information, revenue estimates based on review volume and pricing, and review sentiment data revealing operational pain points. This approach provides 90% market coverage with rich behavioral data showing which restaurants struggle with service speed or order accuracy—perfect indicators they need better POS systems. Apify: Setup and Configuration Here&#x27;s the step-by-step setup process: Step 1: Create Your Apify Account and browse their actor library to find scrapers matching your data needs. Each actor targets specific platforms—Instagram Business Scraper, Google Maps Scraper, and hundreds more specialized options. Step 2: Configure Your Actor by clicking "Create Task" to add it to your library of actors, which Clay will be able to access directly. Switch the input format from Manual to JSON mode and copy the body text—this becomes your input data structure in Clay. Step 3: Connect to Clay by navigating to Actions → Run Apify Actor. Select the task you just created in Apify and paste the JSON configuration under "Input Data" to define what the scraper should collect. 🎯 Building GTM Alpha Through Creative Data Collection Let&#x27;s examine how creative scraping strategies create genuine competitive advantages that traditional prospecting can&#x27;t match. The E-Commerce Marketing Agency Example Say you&#x27;re a marketing agency trying to target e-commerce brands. The standard approach is searching for mid-sized e-commerce companies in traditional B2B databases. You get the exact same list as every competitor, leading to identical outreach that prospects have seen dozens of times. Generic data leads to generic outreach, which leads to terrible response rates and commoditized positioning. The Strategic Insight But here&#x27;s a valuable insight: Brands with huge social followings but low website engagement are essentially signaling "We have marketing budget and audience but need help with conversion optimization." This represents your perfect prospect: they&#x27;ve proven they can build an audience but struggle to monetize it. The challenge is systematically identifying these businesses when traditional databases don&#x27;t track this behavioral mismatch. The Clay Apify Workflow Here&#x27;s how to build competitive advantage through creative data collection: Step 1: Social Following Discovery - Use Instagram Business Scraper to find brands with 50K+ followers in your target industry. Step 2: Website Performance Analysis - Use Similarweb Scraper to check their websites for in-depth traffic data—visit counts, session duration, bounce rates, and traffic sources to detect any conversion gaps. Step 3: Intelligent Outreach - Use Clay&#x27;s AI to compose personalized copy referencing specific data points you&#x27;ve discovered about their business. From social media platforms like Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram to more specialized sources like Yellow Pages or apartments.com, Apify actors cover an impressive range of data sources. Whether you&#x27;re looking to analyze Google search results, explore job listings, or dive deep into niche forums, there&#x27;s likely an Apify actor tailored to your needs. The beauty of Apify lies in its versatility. Users have leveraged these scrapers for everything from market research and competitive analysis to finding housing in new cities. This integration allows users to tap into a vast pool of specialized scrapers, each designed to extract data from specific sources with precision and efficiency. Whether you&#x27;re a marketer looking to gather customer insights, a researcher collecting data for analysis, or a business owner tracking industry trends, Apify in Clay provides the tools you need to access and utilize web data effectively. 🖥️ A Practical Example: Scraping Reddit with Apify To illustrate the power of Apify in Clay, let&#x27;s walk through a practical example: scraping a Reddit thread. Imagine you&#x27;ve identified a Reddit thread discussing Clay tables that could provide valuable insights for your product team, marketing strategies, or customer understanding. Using Apify&#x27;s "Unlimited Reddit Web Scraper," you can extract a wealth of information from this thread, including posts, comments, user data, and more. This particular actor allows you to crawl Reddit content without the need for logging in, making it an efficient tool for gathering public data. The process is straightforward: Select the appropriate Apify actor (in this case, the Reddit scraper). Configure the scraper settings, such as the target URL and data extraction preferences. Initiate the scraping process. Wait for the results, which typically arrive within minutes. Once the scraping is complete, you&#x27;ll have access to a rich dataset that can be seamlessly imported into Clay for further analysis and utilization. Configuring the Apify <> Reddit Scraper 🤔 Considerations and Best Practices While Apify opens up exciting possibilities, it&#x27;s important to approach web scraping responsibly and ethically. Always ensure you&#x27;re complying with the terms of service of the websites you&#x27;re scraping and respect privacy and data protection regulations. Additionally, some Apify actors may require a subscription or per-use fee. In our Reddit example, the scraper costs $45 per month after a one-day free trial. Use Clay&#x27;s powerful data manipulation and analysis tools to make the most of your scraped data. By providing access to a vast array of specialized scrapers, we&#x27;re empowering our users to gather and utilize web data more efficiently and effectively than ever before. Whether you&#x27;re conducting market research, tracking competitor activities, or seeking customer insights, Apify in Clay offers the tools you need to stay ahead in today&#x27;s data-driven world. As you explore the possibilities of Apify in Clay, remember that the key to success lies not just in the data you collect, but in how you analyze and apply those insights. With Clay&#x27;s robust suite of tools and the vast scraping capabilities provided by Apify, you&#x27;re well-equipped to turn raw web data into actionable intelligence that can drive your business forward. We&#x27;ve designed this tool to help you effortlessly scrape web pages and import that valuable information directly into your Clay tables. Today, we&#x27;re excited to walk you through how to leverage this powerful feature to streamline your data collection process. 🔍 Identifying Scrape-Friendly Pages Before we dive into the nitty-gritty of using the extension, it&#x27;s important to understand that some web pages are more scrape-friendly than others. We&#x27;ve found that pages with data presented in a tabular format, like our experts directory, are particularly easy to target. Why? Because the HTML tags for this type of data are typically structured in a table format, making extraction a breeze. That said, don&#x27;t be discouraged if you encounter pages with less structured lists. While these might require a bit more finesse, our Chrome extension is up to the task. We&#x27;ll show you how to develop custom recipes for these trickier scenarios. 🚀 Getting Started with the Clay Chrome Extension When you click into the Clay Chrome extension, you&#x27;ll notice its intelligent auto-detect feature. This nifty function attempts to identify any lists on your page automatically. In many cases, like with our experts directory, you&#x27;ll find that the extension has already detected and prepared to scrape all the relevant entries—78 in this particular instance. Using the auto-detect feature on the Clay Chrome Extension 🛠️ Creating Custom Recipes But what if the auto-detect doesn&#x27;t quite hit the mark? No worries! We&#x27;ve built in the ability to create custom recipes. Here&#x27;s how: Navigate to the "Select Data" option Create a new recipe (let&#x27;s call it "ClayU Test Experts Recipe") Set the URL pattern (e.g., clay.com/expert) Select the data you want to scrape When selecting data, our extension guides you through the process. You&#x27;ll click on two items inside the list you want to scrape, and voila! The list selector pops up automatically. From there, you can choose specific attributes like agency name, location, average cost, and description. As you add these attributes, you&#x27;ll see a preview of your scraped data in a neat, tabular format. Once you&#x27;re satisfied, save your recipe, and you&#x27;re ready to add this data to your workspace. Creating custom recipes in the Clay Chrome extension for non-mapped URLs 📊 From Web to Workspace: Your Data Journey With your recipe saved, adding the scraped data to your workspace is just a click away. A new tab will open, presenting you with a ready-made table filled with all the agency information you specified. This table serves as a powerful starting point for further analysis and action. 🔮 Unlocking New Possibilities Now that you have this structured data in Clay, the possibilities are endless. You could use Claygent to look up these agency names, analyze costs, or dig into the descriptions to identify specific services. This approach isn&#x27;t limited to agency directories—imagine applying this to competitor pages, case studies, or even conference attendee lists. By mastering the Clay Chrome extension, you&#x27;re able to transform unstructured web data into actionable insights within your Clay workspace. Whether you&#x27;re sourcing leads, conducting market research, or building comprehensive databases, this tool empowers you to work smarter, not harder. Remember, the web is full of valuable data just waiting to be structured and analyzed. With Clay&#x27;s Chrome extension in your toolkit, you&#x27;re well-equipped to capture, organize, and leverage that information to drive your business forward. Happy scraping! While we&#x27;ve previously explored some of our more advanced scraping options, today we&#x27;re excited to dive into Clay&#x27;s native scraping tool. Though it might not be the first option that comes to mind, this tool has some unique advantages that make it a valuable addition to your data collection toolkit. 🔍 Where Clay&#x27;s Native Scraper Fits in the Ecosystem When it comes to web scraping, we typically recommend a hierarchy of tools based on the complexity of your needs. For general web and public infrastructure browsing, Claygent is often our go-to solution. When Claygent hits its limits, we usually turn to Zenrows. And for specific tasks requiring bulk sources, Apify is our preferred choice. So where does Clay&#x27;s native scraper fit into this ecosystem? While it may not be our top recommendation for complex scraping tasks, it shines in its simplicity and cost-effectiveness. This makes it an excellent default option, especially for straightforward scraping needs. 💼 The Power of Simplicity One of the key strengths of Clay&#x27;s native scraper is its ease of use. Take, for example, the task of scraping company websites. Most company homepages are static and relatively easy to parse, making them perfect candidates for our native scraper. But the real magic of our native scraper lies in its built-in extraction capabilities. We&#x27;ve designed it to easily pull specific types of data that are commonly needed. Need to extract emails or phone numbers from a conference attendee list? Looking to gather links from a collection of customer case studies or a "Top 100 Startups" list? Clay&#x27;s native scraper has got you covered. Setting up the simple extractions you might want from a webpage 📊 From Raw Data to Actionable Insights One of the most powerful applications of our native scraper is its ability to extract body text from web pages. This might seem simple, but it opens up a world of possibilities. Consider a company&#x27;s homepage: it&#x27;s likely filled with valuable information about their mission, target audience, and the problems they solve. By scraping this text, you&#x27;re gathering raw material that can be transformed into powerful insights through AI-generated analysis. 🎯 When to Reach for Clay&#x27;s Native Scraper So when should you consider using Clay&#x27;s native scraping tool? We see two primary use cases: Structured Data Collection: When you need to gather data in a pre-generated format, such as lists, phone numbers, or emails, our native scraper excels. AI-Ready Text Extraction: When your goal is to collect all the text from a page to feed into an AI for further processing - whether that&#x27;s for copywriting, categorization, or intelligent data manipulation. While it may be the simplest scraping tool in our suite, don&#x27;t underestimate its power. The Clay native scraper can be incredibly effective, depending on your specific use case. In the ever-evolving world of data collection and analysis, having a diverse set of tools at your disposal is crucial. Clay&#x27;s native scraping tool, with its simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and built-in extraction capabilities, is a valuable addition to your data toolkit. Whether you&#x27;re looking to quickly gather structured data or feed raw text into AI algorithms, our native scraper is here to help you unlock the power of web data. Automated Outbound / Deep Dive: Clay Sequencer Lesson 16 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Deep Dive: Clay Sequencer In this lesson, we&#x27;ll explore one of Clay&#x27;s newest and most powerful features: our own native Sequencer, built directly inside of Clay. You can now create and run email campaigns directly inside Clay, without ever leaving the platform. Instead of the traditional workflow where you enrich data in Clay, export it to Outreach or Salesloft or HubSpot, and then run your campaigns, you can now enrich, sequence, and measure everything inside the Clay environment. For RevOps teams, this means you don&#x27;t need to export enriched leads from Clay into other sequencing tools. For SalesOps, no more CSV juggling or CRM exports. For marketers running ABM campaigns, no more waiting for marketing ops or engineering. You can instantly build personalized sequences and trigger campaigns when Clay enrichment detects certain signals, going from idea to execution in minutes. 🚀 Two Ways to Start with the Sequencer There are two ways to start with the sequencer: The first and easiest way is through the Campaigns tab. Here you&#x27;ll see all your campaigns and their status, which is either running or inactive. The second way is if you want to build a campaign from a pre-existing table of leads. To do that, you&#x27;d go to the Actions tab and either create a new campaign or launch Clay Sequencer. For now, we&#x27;ll start from the Campaigns tab. 📋 Campaign Setup Process When you click New Campaign, Clay provides a template campaign. This is the simplest possible setup to get you started, and it has three steps: Step 1: Sourcing Leads For now, we&#x27;ll pull in leads from your target market. Once these leads get added, we move to Step 2. Step 2: The Contacts Table In the contacts table, you&#x27;ll see the leads are automatically pushed in with a pre-configured work email waterfall. The key column in this table is the Send Table Data action. This action syncs your lead data from your parent table into the campaign. This is crucial; it&#x27;s the main way data flows from your enrichment tables into your sequencing campaigns. The best part: if you add additional columns or enrichments, those will automatically sync to your campaign via the Send Table Data action. Step 3: The Campaign Interface Once your data syncs, you&#x27;ll see the campaign interface, which looks familiar if you&#x27;ve used Clay tables before. ALL the lead data from your contacts table is now available here for your campaigns, and any edits in the campaign table will automatically sync. ⚙️ Campaign Settings and Email Configuration You&#x27;ll want to choose an internal name that makes sense for tracking. Most importantly, you need to select the correct email address column. We try to auto-detect this, but it&#x27;s what determines where your emails actually get sent. You also have an HTML option here. While this enables inline images and links, I&#x27;d recommend keeping it off for outreach campaigns because HTML hurts deliverability. Plain text performs better for cold outreach. ✍️ Drafting Your Message Sequences Here&#x27;s where things get really powerful. Clay&#x27;s AI can draft messages using your business context, which scrapes information about your company and ideal customer profile from your website, and then uses it in your campaign. The AI snippets feature is particularly useful. You can generate personalized copy using job titles, names, company data, or any other enriched fields. You can preview how this output looks across different leads in real-time, so you know exactly how your personalization will appear. Then you can click into the snippet and tweak the configuration parameters however you see fit. For follow-ups, you can add additional messages either as new threads or continuing the same thread, and schedule them with specific delays - like 3 days later. The message drafting includes some sophisticated features: Clean variables provide safe substitutions with fallbacks - so if a company name is missing, it won&#x27;t break your email Spin-tax lets you rotate phrases to avoid spam filters - things like alternating between "hi," "hello," and "hey" 📤 Sender Setup and Scheduling For sending, you have two main options. You can use SMTP for direct account integration, or Google OAuth if you&#x27;re using Workspace. If you open up the SMTP settings and have no idea what you&#x27;re looking at, then you should probably use Google OAuth. Note that using Google OAuth does require admin authorization. Scheduling is straightforward and flexible: You can set timezone and business hours like Monday through Friday 9 to 5 Set spacing between emails - Clay recommends about 20 minutes between sends, which gets you roughly 24 emails per day Set delayed start dates if you want to prepare campaigns in advance When you launch, certain elements get locked in: Your AI snippets and core campaign settings can&#x27;t be changed after launch. But you can pause campaigns to edit copy, or complete them to permanently end the sequence. 📊 Analytics and Reply Management Once launched, the Analytics tab shows live stats that you can refresh to see current performance. The Clay Sequencer includes Reply Management. Every meaningful campaign event gets captured in a Campaign Events table: emails sent, replies received, and categorization of those replies. Clay provides two pre-built actions: The Reply to Lead action can automatically generate AI responses to replies The Add Email to Blocklist action handles unsubscribe requests automatically For the AI replies, I&#x27;d recommend set

Automated Outbound / Deep Dive: Tavus AI Video Generation Lesson 14 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Deep Dive: Tavus AI Video Generation 🎭 Revolutionizing Personalized Outreach with Tavus AI in Clay At Clay, we&#x27;re constantly pushing the boundaries of what&#x27;s possible in personalized outreach. Today, we&#x27;re excited to dive into one of our most cutting-edge AI integrations: Tavus AI. This remarkable tool takes personalization to a whole new level by creating AI replicas that can speak your chosen script in a video format. Let&#x27;s explore how this integration can transform your outreach strategies. 🤖 The Power of AI Replicas Tavus AI offers a selection of pre-trained models that can recite scripts in various environments. While this alone is impressive, the real game-changer is the ability to create your own personal replica. By submitting a consent video and a training video, you can have your very own AI avatar ready to deliver custom messages in just 3-5 hours. This opens up endless possibilities for scaling your personal touch in outreach efforts. Creating your own personal replicas in Tavus 🔗 Integrating Tavus AI with Clay To harness the full potential of Tavus AI within Clay, we start with our deep personalization table. We take the final email content and use AI to transform it into a video script. We then generate a unique video name for each prospect and optionally include their company&#x27;s website as a background image for the video. In Clay, we set up the Tavus integration using our replica ID, the generated script, the company domain (for the background), and the unique video name. After running the integration and waiting a few minutes, we&#x27;re presented with personalized videos for each prospect. Navigating your inputs for Tavus in Clay 🎥 The Result: Personalized Video Outreach at Scale Let&#x27;s take a look at an example video generated for a prospect named Varun: "Hey Varun, really loved your insights on the importance of agility in adapting to new healthcare workflows and hope this personalized video shows you how excited I am to chat. As the head of GTM at Acme, I&#x27;m fascinated by how you&#x27;re infusing AI at Clay. Would you be open to a quick virtual coffee to discuss further? I&#x27;d be happy to share my learnings from other industry leaders as well." 🧐 Evaluating the AI-Generated Content Overall, we&#x27;d rate this experience an 8 out of 10. The voice sounds reasonably similar to the original, though as the subject, I might be overly critical. The main area for improvement lies in the synchronization between audio and video, which can sometimes be slightly off. This is likely a technical hurdle that Tavus will continue to refine over time. It&#x27;s worth noting that the quality of the replica can potentially be improved by providing more training data. This highlights the importance of thorough preparation when creating your AI avatar. 🚀 The Future of Personalized Outreach The implications of this technology for sales and marketing teams are profound. Imagine being able to scale the personal touch of your top performers across a much larger prospect base. BDRs, SDRs, and other lead generation professionals can now create customized, personal video messages for each prospect without spending hours recording individual videos. This level of personalization, combined with the efficiency of AI, opens up new possibilities for engagement and conversion. Prospects receive a unique, tailored message that feels personal and authentic, potentially increasing response rates and fostering stronger connections from the outset. 🤔 Ethical Considerations and Best Practices As with any powerful technology, it&#x27;s crucial to use Tavus AI responsibly. Always be transparent about the use of AI in your outreach efforts. The goal is to enhance personalization and efficiency, not to deceive. Consider including a brief disclaimer in your videos or follow-up communications to maintain trust and integrity. Additionally, ensure that you have proper consent and adhere to data privacy regulations when creating and using AI replicas. The power of this technology comes with the responsibility to use it ethically and respectfully. 🌟 Conclusion: Embracing the Future of Outreach The integration of Tavus AI with Clay represents a significant leap forward in personalized outreach capabilities. By combining AI-generated video content with our existing personalization strategies, we&#x27;re opening up new avenues for engaging prospects in meaningful, scalable ways. As we continue to explore and refine these technologies, we&#x27;re excited to see how our users will leverage them to create more impactful, personalized outreach campaigns. The future of sales and marketing is here, and it&#x27;s more personal than ever. We encourage you to experiment with AI avatars in your outreach strategies and share your experiences. Together, we can push the boundaries of what&#x27;s possible in personalized communication and drive better results for our businesses. Deep Dive: Zenrows Scraping [Limitless Research] - Clay University Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Courses ​ Clay 101: GTM Automation ​ Limitless Research ​ AI-Powered GTM Automation ​ Automated Outbound ​ Signals & ABM ​ CRM Enrichment ​ Automated Inbound ​ How to Use HG Insights in Clay ​ TAM Sourcing ​ Clay in ChatGPT Course index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Courses ​ Clay 101: GTM Automation ​ Limitless Research ​ AI-Powered GTM Automation ​ Automated Outbound ​ Signals & ABM ​ CRM Enrichment ​ Automated Inbound ​ How to Use HG Insights in Clay ​ TAM Sourcing ​ Clay in ChatGPT Course index ​ Back to course Back to course Limitless Research Stop copy/pasting data into your CRM and learn how to harness the power of web scraping to turbocharge your revenue org Progress Intro to Web Scraping ✔ 1 Intro to Web Scraping Prompt Engineering Crash Course ✔ 2 Prompt Engineering Crash Course Claygent: AI Web Scraper ✔ 3 Claygent: AI Web Scraper Deep Dive: Clay Chrome Extension ✔ 4 Deep Dive: Clay Chrome Extension Deep Dive: Apify Actors ✔ 5 Deep Dive: Apify Actors Deep Dive: Zenrows Scraping ✔ 6 Deep Dive: Zenrows Scraping Deep Dive: Clay Scrapers ✔ 7 Deep Dive: Clay Scrapers Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Limitless Research / Deep Dive: Zenrows Scraping Lesson 6 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Deep Dive: Zenrows Scraping 🚀 Unleashing the Power of Zenrows: Clay&#x27;s Secret Weapon for Web Scraping In the ever-evolving landscape of data collection, web scraping stands as a crucial tool for businesses and researchers alike. At Clay, we&#x27;re committed to providing our users with the most robust and efficient scraping solutions. Today, we&#x27;re excited to dive deep into one of our most powerful integrations: Zenrows. 🌟 Why Zenrows Stands Out in the Crowd The world of web scraping can be intimidating, with a plethora of options available. From Clay&#x27;s Native Scraper to Claygent, from our Chrome Extension to Appify, the choices seem endless. However, Zenrows has emerged as a go-to solution for many of our users, including myself. What sets Zenrows apart is its exceptional ability to bypass traditional anti-scraping measures. This makes it an invaluable tool when dealing with websites that have robust protections against data collection. 🔍 Putting Zenrows to the Test: A Real-World Example To demonstrate the power of Zenrows, let&#x27;s revisit a scenario we explored in our Claygent video. We&#x27;re researching 10 startups and seeking funding information. While Claygent can gather this data from the broad web, some users might prefer more specialized sources like Crunchbase for their perceived reliability. Crunchbase presents a perfect challenge for Zenrows. Its pages are accessible without login, but they employ strong anti-scraping measures. Even a simple click on a Crunchbase URL triggers a human verification process. Once past this, the information isn&#x27;t structured in an easily scrapeable format. Yet, the wealth of data available - from funding rounds to investor details, from company rankings to recent news - makes it a goldmine of information. Setting up your Zenrows scrape for Crunchbase pages 🛠️ Harnessing Zenrows&#x27;s Capabilities Here&#x27;s where Zenrows shines. Through Clay&#x27;s interface, you can easily set up a Zenrows scrape without any complex configuration. By inputting the Crunchbase URL and enabling key features like auto-parse (which formats the scraped data for Clay), JavaScript rendering with Premium Proxy (crucial for sites with high scraping protections), and anti-bot measures, you&#x27;re ready to go. With these settings in place, Zenrows can navigate Crunchbase&#x27;s defenses and extract a wealth of data from each company&#x27;s summary page. The results are impressive - from funding rounds and investor names to partners and more. This raw data can then be refined using Clay&#x27;s column extraction tools or intelligent AI formulas to suit your specific needs. 💡 The Zenrows Advantage: Accuracy and Cost-Effectiveness One of the key benefits of using a specialized source like Crunchbase through Zenrows is the potential for more up-to-date information. In our example, we discovered that one company (Magic) had recently closed a Series C round - information that our earlier Claygent search hadn&#x27;t captured. Moreover, Zenrows offers this powerful scraping capability at a remarkably low cost. For users looking to further optimize their expenses, Clay even allows direct management through a personal Zenrows account. 🌈 Embracing the Future of Web Scraping As we continue to navigate the complex world of data collection, tools like Zenrows stand out as beacons of innovation. They enable us to access valuable information from even the most protected sources, opening up new possibilities for research, analysis, and decision-making. At Clay, we&#x27;re proud to offer Zenrows as part of our suite of scraping tools. Whether you&#x27;re a seasoned data professional or just starting your journey into web scraping, Zenrows offers a powerful, cost-effective solution to your data collection needs. Remember, when you encounter a website that seems unscrappable, Zenrows might just be your new best friend. Happy scraping, and may your data collection endeavors be fruitful and insightful! University All courses / Clay 101: GTM Automation / (Enrich) Add Data To Your Table Lesson 8 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 (Enrich) Add Data To Your Table Welcome to the "Enrich" phase of FETE! Now that you&#x27;ve mastered the Find phase—finding companies, people, and businesses—we&#x27;re moving into the next critical stage of building powerful Clay workflows. Over the next few lessons, we&#x27;ll cover how to enrich for companies and people using Waterfalls and AI. In future courses, we&#x27;ll cover more advanced enrichment methods, like enrichment through HTTP/API integrations (which lets you connect to any external data source or service). 🔍 What Does "Enrich" Mean? Enrich is the phase where you take your basic data and add layers of valuable information that help you better qualify leads, personalize outreach, and understand your market. Think about it this way: Finding data gives you company names and contact information. Enriching data tells you whether: That company just raised funding What technology they use How many employees they have What challenges they might be facing This connects directly to our Jigsaw framework. If finding data gives you the corner pieces, enrichment helps you build the edges of your puzzle. You&#x27;re adding the essential context that surrounds and supports your core identifiers. 🎯 Where the Value Lives This additional context is where the value is. It&#x27;s the unique data that your competitors don&#x27;t have. While they&#x27;re working with basic firmographics, you could be targeting companies that just posted engineering jobs and mention AI on their website. That&#x27;s the kind of insight that creates GTM alpha. ⚠️ Avoiding Common Mistakes A common mistake is treating enrichment as just a data gathering exercise. This is the wrong way to think about it. Enrichment is about gathering the right data that gives you a competitive advantage in your market. You&#x27;re transforming raw data into GTM intelligence. 🚀 What&#x27;s Coming Next Our next lesson will focus specifically on enriching companies using waterfalls—the foundation skill you&#x27;ll use in almost every Clay workflow. Now let&#x27;s move to the second step in the FETC ("fetch") framework: Enrich . This is where you start to add real context to your prospecting data. Automated Outbound / Enrich Companies (Waterfalls) Lesson 2 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Enrich Companies (Waterfalls) Enriching Companies (Waterfalls) 🌊 Note: this lesson also appears in Clay 101, Automated Inbound, and CRM Enrichment, so feel free to skim or skip if you&#x27;ve already seen it somewhere else ‍ 💪 Using Waterfalls for Data Enrichment Superpowers Once you’ve gotten your base list of Company Data into Clay, it’s time to augment that list with everything else you need to get razor sharp on your ICP, and how you’re going to reach out to them. At the company level, that data most often looks like recent news, tech stack, funding, revenue, headcount, and more. Really any technographic or firmographic data that will either help you better qualify your leads, or better personalize your messaging. ‍ 🧩 Data Enrichment is Just a Digital Puzzle On first encounter, data enrichment can feel incredibly daunting. While you might know that you want to grab tech stack and revenue, you may not know how to programmatically get company websites or social URLs if your list doesn’t have them right off the bat. Luckily, because we’re starting with a Find Companies search, we already have everything we need to be successful data superheroes. But in case you’re ever feeling stuck on a specific data enrichment puzzle, just remember that all you really need to do is first find your corner pieces. Once you’ve found your corner pieces you can round out the edge with waterfalls, and then use AI Web Scraping (Claygent) to try and fill in the trickier center parts of the picture. For companies, your corner data pieces are going to be domain and company social URL . Once you have those two pieces, you can use any other company enrichment waterfall to get whatever data you need. For people, your corner data pieces are going to be full_name and contact social URL . But we’ll dig deeper into people in a later lesson. ‍ 🤔 How Do Waterfalls Work? Now that you know you can access almost any of the waterfall enrichments from your corner data pieces, it’s time to understand … what actually is a waterfall? ‍ In short, a waterfall is an intelligent way to get only the data that you need on a row by row basis from each provider. In the pre-waterfall era, it was common practice for a revenue team to have subscriptions to between 6-12 different data providers. When you’re paying that much money for data, you want to be as frugal as possible. The best sales teams would upload their lead lists CSVs to the first data provider, then download to a google sheet, and use VLOOKUP magic to filter down to only the percentage of the list that wasn’t found from the first provider. From there, they then re downloaded the new CSV from the google sheet, uploaded it to the second provider, got their results, and then rinsed and repeated for up to a dozen different providers. Waterfalls take that entire manual process (faulty, often inaccurate, and no matter what - time consuming) and automate each step along the way. Let’s say we’re trying to obtain Funding Stage from our list of companies. In the Funding Stage waterfall shown below, we’ll first try to get that data from Intellizence. If we find the data from Intellizence, the rest of the providers won’t run. If we don’t find the data from Intellizence, then we’ll try Dealroom. Then Harmonic. Then Owler. Then Pitchbook. Waterfalls help you maximize data coverage while minimizing data costs. You can have it all. 🤔 Understanding Waterfall Results Once we run the fundraising waterfall, we’ll see a beautiful cascade of our waterfall data across the 5 providers we ran it with. There are a few edge cases to waterfalls worth noting. First is that while the enrichment might be successful, if it doesn’t have the data point that we want – we’ll still waterfall to the next provider, as you can see happening in row 2 below. Looking at your provider columns is the quickest way to understand how a waterfall is working, but ultimately, all the providers will feed their data into one final result column for you to use in the rest of your clay table. ‍ With Intellizence alone, we would have 0% coverage. With Dealroom we get 70%. With Intellizence, Dealroom, and Harmonic, we reach the mythical 100% Now that we’ve got funding stage for these companies, we could repeat this process with any other data point that’s important to our strategy. Revenue, Tech Stack, Headcount, just to name a few. Once we’ve gotten the enriched company data that we need - it’s finally time to Find People. lesson 00:00 Enrich from Financial Filings Now that we&#x27;ve covered enriching images and screenshots, it&#x27;s time for one more AI enrichment lesson, this one focusing on financial filings . This is one of my favorite integrations, and it couldn&#x27;t be simpler to use. 🎯 Why You&#x27;d Enrich from Financial Filings Let&#x27;s say you&#x27;re reaching out to operations leaders at a public company. Instead of guessing what their pain points are, you can ask Oakie AI to pull recent insights from their 10-K or 10-Q—like mentions of cost-saving initiatives or upcoming tech investments. That gives you real material to tailor your message and start a meaningful conversation. You only need a few key data points from a 10-K or 10-Q to ground a conversation around what leadership actually cares about. 📝 Step-by-Step Process with Oakie AI Here&#x27;s how you would use Clay and the Oakie AI enrichment to gather insights from any public company&#x27;s financial statements: Start with your list of public companies Use the waterfall enrichment to get company domain names (pulls from Clearbit, Google, and other sources) Find each company&#x27;s stock ticker using Claygent : Go to Enrich and select Claygent Use the Meta prompter with this prompt: "Help me find the stock ticker for this company from this domain" Input the domain and run the enrichment Once you have the stock ticker, you can use the Oakie AI enrichment to analyze the financial documents: Set up the Oakie AI enrichment Input the stock ticker Specify the date range and filing type (10-K or 10-Q) Enter your questions about the company Run the enrichment 💪 Making the Data Actionable The initial output will be comprehensive but lengthy. To make it more actionable: Use AI to summarize the findings Use the Meta prompter to write your prompt Ask it to "Extract three key insights about challenges this company is facing" Map the key points to separate columns once you get the results Now you have three clear, focused insights about the company that you can use in executive meetings or outbound messaging. 🔄 Oakie AI vs. Claygent: When to Use Each A common question we get is: Can you just use Claygent to accomplish the same thing as Oakie AI? The answer is yes—but with some tradeoffs. If you need just a few high-confidence insights from a company&#x27;s 10-K or 10-Q, and you&#x27;re working with public companies, Oakie AI is usually the better option . It&#x27;s more reliable, faster, and doesn&#x27;t require finding the 10-K yourself. But if you want to ask multiple questions , pull data in a specific format, or get more control over how the output is structured, Claygent gives you that flexibility —as long as you&#x27;re okay with a little extra setup and the risk of not finding the 10-K every time with Claygent. 🎆 Conclusion To recap: Use Oakie AI for accuracy and simplicity Use Claygent for depth and customization Pick the tool that fits the workflow you&#x27;re building. 🔜 What&#x27;s Next That completes our coverage of the Enrich step in the FETC framework. In the next lesson, we&#x27;ll move onto the third piece of FETC ("fetch"): Transform. lesson 00:00 Enrich Images and Screenshots We just covered using Perplexity to enrich your data. Now, let&#x27;s look at how you can enrich from images and screenshots . Anytime you know who your target accounts work with—or who they serve—you have a serious edge in outbound. With the Analyze Image enrichment, you can instantly pull brand logos from a company&#x27;s homepage and turn that into actionable insights for outreach. In other words, you can pull insights from any visual content on the web that would be hard to get through scraping or would require manual work. 🔍 When to Use Analyze Image Enrichment You can use the Analyze Image enrichment when you need to: Pull logos or icons from a webpage Understand brand associations or customer lists Automate visual research that would normally require manual review 🎨 Example: Extracting Logos to Research Company Relationships Let&#x27;s say you&#x27;re targeting fast-growing SaaS companies and want to know which other brands they work with. You can take a screenshot of their homepage and use Analyze Image to extract all visible logos—giving you an instant read on their partners, customers, or integrations. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Process in Clay Here&#x27;s how you would do this in Clay with the Analyze Image enrichment: Start with a domain - We&#x27;ll use clay.com as an example. First, we&#x27;ll use the Analyze Image enrichment. Configure the Analyze Image prompt - Set it to say: "Analyze and return a comma-separated list of the company names for every logo you see on the page, prioritized by getting all the logos on the page. Scroll to the bottom of the page and make sure you get all the logos. Return only the list." Include the domain URL - Make sure to add the domain URL in the configuration box. Run the enrichment - After clicking Save, the enrichment will run and return a list of all logos found on the webpage. You can verify the results by comparing them to the original webpage. Convert to JSON format - Next, add another enrichment and select AI. Set the prompt to:"Return this comma-separated list as a JSON list" and make sure to select JSON schema as the output format. Configure the schema - Set up the schema to extract company logos properly. Write to a new table - Once you have the JSON schema, click into the JSON result, select "Take action on list," and choose "Write each item to a new row in another table." Create a table for the logos - Create a new table, select the list column, and specify the JSON conversion company logos field. After saving, you&#x27;ll have a new table with all the companies listed. Extract domains - Finally, use another Claygent prompt to extract the domain for each company. With these domains, you can then enrich the data further - looking up company news, information, or any other relevant research you need. 💎 Additional Use Cases The Analyze Image enrichment is useful in many other scenarios: Company research - Scan a screenshot of a customer&#x27;s homepage to understand what they do and how their site is designed Hiring signals - Check if a person&#x27;s LinkedIn profile has a "Hiring" badge by analyzing a screenshot with AI Technology detection - Use a screenshot + AI image analysis to detect if a site has a live chat widget or other tools 🎮 Pro Tip: Get Page Screenshot One last detail: Instead of using the domain directly, you can use the "Get Page Screenshot" enrichment, which takes a picture of a webpage based on the domain, and then use that to analyze that screenshot with the Analyze Image enrichment. 🌟 Why This Matters Visual data enrichment gives you access to information that might otherwise: Require manual research by your team Be missed entirely in text-based scraping Provide unique insights your competitors don&#x27;t have By automatically extracting visual information from websites, you can build a more complete picture of your target accounts and their ecosystem, leading to more effective and personalized outreach. Automated Outbound / Enrich People (Waterfalls) Lesson 3 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Enrich People (Waterfalls) 🫂 Supercharging Your People Data with Clay: Waterfalls Pt. 2 Note: this lesson also appears in Clay 101, Automated Inbound, and CRM Enrichment, so feel free to skim or skip if you&#x27;ve already seen it somewhere else ‍ Now that you’ve gotten your list of people, it’s time to pull out your waterfall skills again to enrich your contact data. Without basic contact information (at least social media profile and/or email), your contacts are essentially valueless. On top of that, you’ll need to go the extra mile when it comes to contact research if you really want to stand out in your messaging. In this guide, we’ll explore how to make the most of your contact data in Clay. ‍ 🏢 Pulling New Company Data into Your Table First things first, we want to access all that valuable company data we’ve already enriched. Maybe you want to personalize your messages based on tech stack, or recent employee growth. This process is simple. Whenever you add new company data to your company table, you’ll just rerun the lookup in your people table. This process pulls the enriched company data into your people table, ensuring you have a comprehensive view of each contact&#x27;s company contexts By taking this approach, you&#x27;re not only saving on data credits but also creating a more integrated dataset that combines individual and company information seamlessly. You can always rerun the second column linked to the company table to refresh 🌊 The Power of People Data Waterfalls Just like with companies, we’re now going to use Waterfalls to maximize our coverage while minimizing our cost across 10+ providers to get contact data. We’ll start with email data - one of the most powerful waterfalls in Clay. By default, you&#x27;ll have access to six providers in your email waterfall. But here&#x27;s where it gets interesting: you can customize your waterfall by adding more providers to maximize your email coverage. This flexibility allows you to tailor your data enrichment process to your specific needs and preferences. Remember the puzzle-building metaphor we discussed earlier? It applies here too. To access crucial information like work email, you&#x27;ll need your "corner pieces." For people data, these corner pieces are typically the full name and a social media URL. Once you have these, along with company domain and company social media URL, you&#x27;ve unlocked access to a treasure trove of integrations and data points. ‍ Example of setting up an email enrichment waterfall with multiple providers. ✉️ Email Validation: Ensuring Quality Data Clay’s email waterfalls go one step further by including email validation in the waterfall process. By default, we use ZeroBounce, a best-in-class validation service, but you have the flexibility to choose a different provider if you prefer. Understanding how Clay marks emails as valid or invalid is crucial. By default, catch-all emails are returned as valid. While these are often real emails, there&#x27;s some uncertainty about whether they belong to the specific individual or if they&#x27;re aliases. If you want to be more conservative in your approach, you can enable the "only mark safe to send" option, which will exclude catch-all emails from your valid email list. ‍ Configuring your email validation provider for your waterfall 🏊🏽‍♂️ Diving Deeper into Email Waterfalls As you run your email waterfall, you&#x27;ll see results populate from various providers. The final validated emails will appear in the last column of your table. It&#x27;s worth noting that while the validation columns aren&#x27;t displayed by default (to keep your table tidy), they do exist behind the scenes. If you&#x27;re curious about the validation process, you can unhide these columns to see how ZeroBounce (or your chosen validator) is working its magic. This transparency allows you to understand why certain emails make it to the final column while others don&#x27;t. In some cases, you might notice that the waterfall continues running even after finding an email. This usually indicates that an email was found by a data provider but failed the validation check. It&#x27;s this attention to detail that ensures you&#x27;re working with the highest quality data possible. ‍ The results of an email waterfall process. 🔢 Beyond Email: Expanding Your People Data While email is often the star of the show, Clay&#x27;s waterfalls can enrich your people data in numerous other ways. You can gather phone numbers, social media profiles, GitHub URLs, and much more. The possibilities are vast, allowing you to build a comprehensive profile of each contact in your database. For those looking to go even further, Clay offers additional tools like Claygent for web scraping and integrations with Google searches. These advanced features open up new avenues for data enrichment, helping you uncover those hard-to-find details that can make all the difference in your outreach efforts. We’ll cover those in some later lessons in this course - so don’t worry, it’s coming up! Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / / Enrich People (Waterfalls) Lesson 5 / Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Enrich People (Waterfalls) Enrich People (Email Waterfalls) In lesson four, you learned how to use Clay’s waterfall enrichment to enrich companies with firmographic and technographic data. Now we’re going to show you how to use waterfalls to enrich the people. And since contacts hold little value without basic contact information (at least LinkedIn profile and/or work email), in this lesson, we&#x27;ll show you how to enrich people with validated work emails. Prerequisites Before proceeding, ensure you have: A company list with domain names and LinkedIn profile URLs. If you haven’t imported companies yet, go back to the previous lesson: Finding Companies in Clay. An understanding of the Jigsaw framework, which helps you determine when your data is ready for enrichment. Review: Waterfall Enrichment If you remember from lesson four ( Enrich Companies ), a waterfall is a data enrichment method that pulls data from multiple providers in a specific order, eliminating the need for multiple manual uploads and lookups across different providers. Traditionally, revenue teams had to manage costly subscriptions to multiple data providers and manually filter results through spreadsheets. Waterfalls automate this process by sequentially querying providers—starting with the most cost-effective—until the required data is found, ensuring efficiency, accuracy, and cost savings. If one provider returns a valid data point, Clay stops further enrichments, saving you credits. Email Validation: Ensuring Quality Data Clay’s email waterfall not only finds emails, but validates them as well. By default, we use ZeroBounce, a best-in-class validation service, but you have the flexibility to choose a different provider if you prefer (e.g. if you know a different provider validates best or cheapest in your industry). 💡Tip: By default, Clay considers catch-all emails valid. You can toggle on the “Only mark ‘Safe to Send’ emails as valid” to exclude catch-all emails. How It Works: Watch The Guided Demo Just like with companies, we&#x27;ll use waterfalls to maximize coverage and minimize cost across 10+ data providers. This time, we’ll waterfall work emails—one of the most powerful waterfalls in Clay. How it works: Open the Enrichment Panel: Click on the “Add enrichment” button. Search for “Work Email” in the list of available enrichments. Configure Your Waterfall: You’ll see a pre-arranged order of email providers optimized for coverage. Add or reorder email providers as desired to maximize data coverage, as Clay refunds credits if a provider doesn&#x27;t return an email. Select Input Columns: The primary input required is the Company Domain. Ideally, also include Personal Linkedin URLs. If unavailable, use fallback combinations like Full Name + Company Name or Full Name + Personal Email. Choose Your Validation Provider: Clay defaults to ZeroBounce, known for high accuracy. You can select another validator if preferred. Set Catch-All Email Handling: By default, catch-all emails are treated as valid. To avoid potential deliverability issues, toggle to treat catch-alls as invalid if you’re uncertain. Run a Test on 10 Rows: Always start by testing 10 rows to review results before scaling. Click “Save & Run (10 Rows)” to initiate. Once the enrichment process starts, Clay dynamically moves through the waterfall: If a provider finds a valid email, the process stops for that contact. If no email is found, credits are refunded and Clay moves to the next provider. The process continues until an email is found or all providers are exhausted. 💡Tip: Validation columns are hidden by default. Open the Columns Panel and unhide these columns to inspect detailed validation steps. Enrich Beyond Emails Emails are the cornerstone of successful outreach, but Clay&#x27;s waterfalls can enrich your contact data far beyond just emails. Easily add phone numbers, Linkedin profiles, GitHub URLs, and other information to build a more complete picture of each prospect. And for those of you who need specialized, hard-to-find information, Claygent, Clay’s AI research agent , and our direct integration with Google , can help capture custom enrichment across the web. Congrats! That’s a wrap on finding validated work emails using Clay’s waterfall enrichment. Next up, we’ll explore prompt engineering best practices in Clay using the S.P.I.C.E.
