Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Transform with AI Formulas (and Optimize Credits) In the last lesson, we talked about the two ways you can use AI to transform data: deterministic and generative. Now we&#x27;re going to focus on the first one: deterministic transformations using AI Formulas in Clay. These are perfect for data cleanups, text extraction, and other repeatable operations where you want consistent, rule-based output. 🧮 When to Use AI Formulas Anytime you&#x27;re manipulating or calculating existing data in a structured way like: Totals Patterns Extractions Cleanups You should use AI Formulas . 🔍 Ideal Use Cases for Deterministic Tasks These are ideal for deterministic tasks when: You know exactly what kind of result you want You&#x27;re applying the same logic to every row You don&#x27;t need the AI to make a judgment call Here are a few classic examples. You want to: Extract all the companies someone has worked at into a comma-separated list Calculate the total years of work experience someone has Get the tenure in their last role , expressed in years and months This kind of transformation would normally take a bunch of custom formulas or scripting. AI Formulas make it simple. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Implementation Let&#x27;s walk through how to extract a CSV list of companies from someone&#x27;s work experience using AI Formulas: Start with data from social media Begin with a table containing social media domains Use the Enrich Person feature to get detailed profile information, including work experience Access Experience Data Open cell details for any person Scroll down to the "Experience" section You&#x27;ll see a list of all the companies they&#x27;ve worked for and roles they&#x27;ve held Create the AI Formula From the Experiences list, you can click "Take action on list" and then select "Formula" to open the AI Formula builder Write the Formula Enter a prompt like this: "Create a CSV of companies worked at, with these rules: Include company names only Exclude job titles and other details Skip placeholder companies (like “stealth&#x27;” or “new company”) Remove any duplicates" Review and Apply Generate the formula Check the output If it looks correct, accept and apply to all rows 📝 Additional Use Cases for AI Formulas That&#x27;s one simple use case for AI Formulas. You can also use it for: Formatting dates or numbers Extracting text patterns (like pulling a domain from an email) Cleaning up inconsistent inputs like job titles or locations Doing math, like adding up years of experience or calculating tenure If it&#x27;s structured and consistent, AI Formulas are your best bet. ⚡ Why AI Formulas Optimize Your Credits AI Formulas are particularly valuable because they: Don&#x27;t consume Clay credits; they&#x27;re free to use Process faster than API-based enrichments Maintain consistent output formats Can be reused across multiple tables and workflows By using AI Formulas for deterministic tasks instead of credit-consuming enrichments, you can reserve your credits for more complex operations that truly require generative AI. 🔮 What&#x27;s Coming Next In the next lesson, we&#x27;ll cover the other side of the Transform equation. We’ll use generative AI to take messy or unstructured inputs and turn them into clean categories or classifications. The combination of deterministic transformations (AI Formulas) and generative transformations gives you a complete toolkit for preparing your data for the final step in the FETC framework: Create. Welcome to lesson four of Inbound Automation with Clay! So far, we&#x27;ve walked through how to connect inbound lead sources with Clay and explored various ways to enrich lead data, empowering reps with the ability to find comprehensive information about their prospects. Now, we&#x27;re going to discuss how to manipulate and clean up all that enriched data to make it easily actionable. We want to ensure that messy data doesn&#x27;t stand in the way of clear lead scoring, a healthy CRM, or successful outbound efforts. Data cleaning isn&#x27;t just about hygiene—it&#x27;s about creating the foundation for intelligent automation. Raw enriched data often comes in inconsistent formats, contains extra characters, or includes variations that can break downstream logic. Proper cleaning transforms this messy data into standardized, reliable information that your scoring algorithms and automation can work with consistently. In this lesson, we&#x27;ll cover how to use Clay&#x27;s built-in normalization tools as well as AI formulas to prep and prime your data for effective lead scoring and routing. 🚿 Clay&#x27;s Native Cleaning Tools These built-in tools are your first line of defense against messy data, and the best part? They&#x27;re completely credit-free. These tools handle deterministic transformations: rule-based, predictable changes that follow consistent logic without requiring AI interpretation. To access these tools, navigate to the "Add enrichment" panel, select the "Normalize" option in the sub-navigation and choose from the pre-built normalization options. ‼️ Essential Normalization Functions Company Name Normalization addresses one of the most common data inconsistency issues. How often have you encountered company names cluttered with suffixes like "Inc.," "LLC," or "Corporation," or unnecessary prefixes that make company matching difficult? This function tackles that issue head-on. Select "Normalize Company Names" from the pre-built options, choose the appropriate input column containing your company names, and run the action across your rows. The result? Clean, consistent company names that are ready for your next campaign and significantly improve downstream copy and segment logic. Whitespace Normalization ensures consistent spacing across all your text data. This seemingly simple function eliminates extra spaces, tabs, and line breaks that can break automation rules or make data appear unprofessional in your outreach. Clean spacing is essential for reliable string matching and professional presentation. Phone Number Standardization creates uniform formatting by standardizing phone number formats, removing or adding parentheses and dashes as needed. This ensures your phone data works consistently across different systems and calling tools, preventing dial failures due to formatting inconsistencies. Location Normalization creates uniformity in how addresses and locations are represented across your dataset. This is particularly valuable if you&#x27;re doing geographic segmentation, routing leads based on territory, or analyzing market penetration by region. Clay&#x27;s native normalization tools cover most standardization needs efficiently and without consuming any credits, making them the ideal first step in any data cleaning workflow. 📐 Advanced Cleaning with AI Formulas What happens when you need more sophisticated data manipulation? Data cleaning and normalization isn&#x27;t just for hygiene&#x27;s sake—it can also be crucial for effective lead scoring and routing logic. Job Title Extraction Consider job titles as a practical example. Rather than working with full titles that might include detailed job functions or unnecessary organizational details, you might only want to know whether the person&#x27;s title includes seniority indicators like "Head," "VP," "Director," or "Lead." While you could use the "clean up job titles" function in Clay&#x27;s normalization tools and iterate from there, an efficient approach is using AI formulas for this type of extraction. Insert a formula column and describe what you&#x27;re looking for, mapping in your data column with all the collected job titles. AI will automatically generate the formula you need to extract exactly the information that matters for your scoring logic. Company Headcount Standardization Company headcount data presents another common challenge. When Clay enriches company information, it sometimes returns headcount ranges like "50-100 employees" rather than exact integer values, which can create inconsistencies in categorization and scoring algorithms. Using an AI formula, you can clean this data by removing hyphens and returning either the lower or higher number in the range, depending on your scoring methodology. This standardization ensures your lead scoring calculations work consistently across all records. 💡 Best Practices for AI-Powered Cleaning The best practice for these transformations is to select "Use AI" rather than Claygent since all the data you&#x27;re working with is already present in your table. This approach is more efficient and cost-effective for data manipulation tasks. As a rule of thumb , the default approach should always be to first try the tools that are free and low-effort, then decide whether you need additional cleanup afterward. Start with normalized job titles using Clay&#x27;s built-in tools, then if you need additional customization, try AI formulas to see if you can achieve your desired results. Only resort to more expensive AI categorization if the logic becomes too complex for regular expressions or simple AI formulas to handle effectively. 🎯 The Strategic Impact of Clean Data Clean, standardized data creates cascading benefits throughout your entire revenue operations workflow. the two ways you can use AI to transform data: deterministic and generative. Now we&#x27;re going to focus on the first one: deterministic transformations using AI Formulas in Clay. These are perfect for data cleanups, text extraction, and other repeatable operations where you want consistent, rule-based output. 🧮 When to Use AI Formulas Anytime you&#x27;re manipulating or calculating existing data in a structured way like: Totals Patterns Extractions Cleanups You should use AI Formulas . 🔍 Ideal Use Cases for Deterministic Tasks These are ideal for deterministic tasks when: You know exactly what kind of result you want You&#x27;re applying the same logic to every row You don&#x27;t need the AI to make a judgment call Here are a few classic examples. You want to: Extract all the companies someone has worked at into a comma-separated list Calculate the total years of work experience someone has Get the tenure in their last role , expressed in years and months This kind of transformation would normally take a bunch of custom formulas or scripting. AI Formulas make it simple. 📝 Use Cases for AI Formulas You can use AI formulas for: Formatting dates or numbers Extracting text patterns (like pulling a domain from an email) Cleaning up inconsistent inputs like job titles or locations Doing math, like adding up years of experience or calculating tenure If it&#x27;s structured and consistent, AI Formulas are your best bet. ⚡ Why AI Formulas Optimize Your Credits AI Formulas are particularly valuable because they: Don&#x27;t consume Clay credits; they&#x27;re free to use Process faster than API-based enrichments Maintain consistent output formats Can be reused across multiple tables and workflows By using AI Formulas for deterministic tasks instead of credit-consuming enrichments, you can reserve your credits for more complex operations that truly require generative AI. 🔮 What&#x27;s Coming Next In the next lesson, we&#x27;ll cover the other side of the Transform equation. We’ll use generative AI to take messy or unstructured inputs and turn them into clean categories or classifications. Progress Intro to Signals in Clay ✔ 1 Intro to Signals in Clay Types of Signals in Clay ✔ 2 Types of Signals in Clay Setting Up Signals in Clay ✔ 3 Setting Up Signals in Clay Building Custom Signals in Clay ✔ 4 Building Custom Signals in Clay Advanced Strategies with Signals ✔ 5 Advanced Strategies with Signals ClayBM: ABM in Clay ✔ 6 ClayBM: ABM in Clay ABM and Ad Intelligence in Clay ✔ 7 ABM and Ad Intelligence in Clay Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Signals & ABM / Types of Signals in Clay Lesson 2 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Types of Signals in Clay Introduction In our previous lesson, we introduced you to the world of signals in Clay and why they&#x27;re such a game-changer for modern GTM teams. Today, we&#x27;re diving deeper into the types of signals available in Clay: Default signals and Custom signals. By the end of this lesson, you&#x27;ll understand exactly which signal type to choose for any given use case, understand their technical capabilities and limitations, and feel confident building the right monitoring system for your specific GTM strategy. 🎯 Default Signals: Your GTM Intelligence on Autopilot Default signals are Clay&#x27;s greatest hits—the most valuable business events that trigger buying decisions, with monitoring systems built out of the box. Clay handles the data sources, refresh rates, and filtering logic so you get enterprise-grade monitoring without setup complexity. Career Movement Signals: Track VP-level job changes, new hires, promotions, layoffs, and relocations across your target accounts. When your champion moves companies or a key decision maker joins a prospect account, you&#x27;ll know within hours rather than discovering it weeks later through manual social media checks. News and Fundraising: Monitor funding rounds, mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, product launches, and leadership changes. These events create immediate opportunities—new budget from funding, tool evaluation during M&A integration, or fresh perspectives from new executives. Job Postings: Reveal expansion signals that predict buying behavior. Aggressive sales or marketing hiring indicates budget allocation and growth ambitions. Technical role postings show technology adoption plans and infrastructure investment. Clay analyzes job descriptions for urgency indicators and geographic expansion signals. Brand Mentions: Monitor competitor discussions, partnership opportunities, customer satisfaction signals, and thought leadership trends. This is social listening purpose-built for B2B sales intelligence, helping you identify prospects actively engaging with your category or expressing dissatisfaction with current solutions. Website Intent: Monitor page visits, content engagement, resource downloads, and pricing interactions for real-time buying signals. This reveals which accounts are actively researching solutions and how deep they are in their evaluation process. Customer Sentiment Analysis: Monitor reviews on G2, Capterra, and TrustRadius for competitive insights, feature requests in your category, and churn indicators from competitors&#x27; customers. This reveals prospects who might be open to switching solutions. Practical Example: Marketing Automation Let&#x27;s say you sell marketing automation software. You&#x27;d set up a Default signal for job postings, filtering for companies hiring Marketing Operations Managers or Demand Generation roles. When a company posts these positions, it often signals they&#x27;re scaling their marketing function and evaluating new tools. The signal fires, you get notified, and you can reach out with messaging about how your platform helps growing marketing teams scale efficiently. The timing is perfect because they&#x27;re actively thinking about their marketing infrastructure and likely evaluating technology to support their expansion. 🛠️ Custom Signals: Build Monitoring for Anything Custom signals combine scheduled sources, AI analysis, and conditional logic to monitor virtually anything that matters for your specific market. This is where you build proprietary intelligence systems that competitors can&#x27;t easily replicate. Example Monitoring Categories Tech Stack Changes : Detect adoption of any technology—CRM migrations, marketing automation implementations, security tool deployments, cloud platform switches. Each change represents an opportunity to offer complementary solutions or competitive alternatives. Compliance and Certifications : Monitor regulatory requirements, newly achieved certifications like SOC2 or HIPAA, and industry standards adoption. These events often trigger evaluation of related tools and services. Geographic Expansion : Identify new office openings, market entry signals, international hiring patterns, and localization efforts. Expansion creates needs for infrastructure, compliance, and operational tools. Website Content Monitoring: Track pricing modifications that suggest positioning changes, feature updates revealing product evolution, team page additions indicating growth, and blog themes showing strategic focus. These changes reveal company priorities and potential needs. Social Media Activity : Monitor executive social media posting patterns, company engagement levels with industry content, event participation showing active community involvement, and thought leadership themes revealing strategic priorities. Financial Filings Intelligence : Analyze SEC filings for revenue guidance changes, executive compensation patterns indicating strategic shifts, and strategic announcements about new markets or product lines. Public companies telegraph their priorities through regulatory filings. Engineering Density Metrics : Monitor GitHub activity levels, technical job postings, open source contributions, and developer community engagement. High engineering density often predicts technology adoption and infrastructure investment. These are just scratching the surface of what&#x27;s possible using custom signals. Any data source in Clay can become a signal . You&#x27;re not limited to pre-built options—if Clay can enrich for it, you can monitor for changes in it. This flexibility enables monitoring for highly specific criteria that matter uniquely to your business. Real-World Example: Vanta Vanta uses AI signals to identify companies actively seeking SOC2 certification, then reaches out with compliance automation messaging. They analyze website content, job descriptions, and social media to identify certification intent before it becomes obvious through public announcements. This early detection allows them to engage prospects during the research phase rather than the vendor evaluation phase, shaping the conversation and building relationships before competitors enter the picture. Progress Introduction to TAM Sourcing ✔ 1 Introduction to TAM Sourcing Understanding your ICP ✔ 2 Understanding your ICP TAM Sourcing Workflows in Clay ✔ 3 TAM Sourcing Workflows in Clay Advanced TAM Sourcing Techniques ✔ 4 Advanced TAM Sourcing Techniques Activating your TAM: From Intelligence to Revenue ✔ 5 Activating your TAM: From Intelligence to Revenue SMB TAM Sourcing ✔ 6 SMB TAM Sourcing Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers ✔ 7 Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / TAM Sourcing / Understanding your ICP Lesson 2 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Understanding your ICP 🎯 Building Your ICP & Data Foundation: Strategic Targeting Introduction In our last lesson, we explored Clay&#x27;s TAM sourcing capabilities and how they can completely transform your prospecting approach. Today, we&#x27;re diving into the foundation of all effective TAM sourcing: building your Ideal Customer Profile and establishing a solid data foundation. Without nailing down your ICP, even the most sophisticated Clay workflows will generate noise instead of qualified prospects. The most successful Clay users start with a clear, evidence-based understanding of who they&#x27;re trying to reach and why those prospects should care. 🚫 The Common ICP Mistake Most teams approach ICP development backwards, jumping straight to demographics without understanding the underlying business logic. Demographics-First Thinking When building an ICP, people immediately start listing criteria: company size between 100-500 employees, technology industry, North American headquarters, $10M+ revenue. While logical, this preemptive demographic filtering misses the fundamental question of why these characteristics matter. Pain-First Thinking The right starting point is understanding pain points and buying motivation. Before defining any demographic criteria, you need to answer fundamental questions that reveal who actually needs what you&#x27;re selling: Who feels this pain daily? Which roles or departments experience the problem your solution solves as a recurring frustration rather than an occasional inconvenience? Who has the budget to solve it? Which companies have the financial resources and willingness to invest in solutions to this problem? Who has authority to buy? Which individuals or teams have purchasing power or significant influence over buying decisions? Who is actively looking for solutions? Which prospects are currently researching alternatives rather than tolerating the status quo? What qualities do my top customers share? Which characteristics consistently appear across your most successful customer relationships? The Hypothesis Framework Remember that your initial answers are just your current best hypothesis based on limited data. You&#x27;ll continually refine them as you gather more market intelligence and customer insights through actual prospecting and sales conversations. This iterative approach means your ICP becomes more accurate over time rather than remaining a static guess about your market. 📊 The Problem Severity by Frequency Matrix Your answers to those fundamental questions help you construct the Problem Severity by Frequency Matrix, which provides clear guidance on prioritization and messaging strategy. Understanding the Axes The Y-axis represents problem severity —how much this issue actually hurts your prospect&#x27;s business in terms of lost revenue, wasted time, or operational inefficiency. The X-axis represents problem frequency —how often they encounter this problem in their daily operations, whether it&#x27;s a constant drain or an occasional frustration. The Sweet Spot: High Pain + High Frequency The optimal target is prospects experiencing both high pain and high frequency. These companies feel the problem acutely and encounter it constantly, making them desperate for solutions and willing to prioritize evaluation and purchase. Practical Example: Data Enrichment If you&#x27;re selling data enrichment solutions, consider two prospect profiles: High Priority Prospect : A company researching 500 prospects per week experiences high pain (massive time drain, bottleneck to pipeline growth) and high frequency (daily struggle). They feel the inefficiency constantly and it directly impacts their revenue generation capacity. Lower Priority Prospect : A company researching only 50 prospects per week might be interested in efficiency improvements, but they&#x27;re not desperate enough to prioritize finding and buying a solution. The pain exists but isn&#x27;t severe enough to drive urgent action. This matrix helps you prioritize who to target first and understand how urgently they need what you&#x27;re selling, informing both targeting decisions and messaging urgency. 🔍 Three Dimensions of ICP Definition Build your ICP across three interconnected dimensions that create a comprehensive prospect profile when layered together. Dimension 1: Firmographic Criteria These are basic company characteristics that provide demographic filtering: employee count ranges, revenue bands, industry classifications, and geographic locations. While essential for initial filtering, these are your table stakes criteria that define broad market segments. Firmographics alone don&#x27;t predict buying behavior or need—they simply define which companies could theoretically use your solution based on their basic characteristics. Dimension 2: Technographic Criteria Technographics reveal what tools and technologies prospects currently use, providing crucial context about their sophistication level and integration requirements. Are they using Salesforce or HubSpot for CRM? Outreach or SalesLoft for sales engagement? Marketing automation platforms or manual email? Their current tech stack tells you about their operational maturity, integration needs, budget allocation, and competitive displacement opportunities. This dimension transforms generic company profiles into specific opportunity assessments based on technology environment. Dimension 3: Behavioral Criteria Behavioral signals indicate timing and intent—the difference between companies that fit your demographic profile and those actually ready to buy right now. Are they hiring rapidly, suggesting growth that creates new needs? Did they just raise funding, indicating budget availability and growth ambitions? Are they posting jobs for go-to-market roles, signaling sales expansion? Have they recently changed executives, potentially triggering tool reevaluation? These behavioral signals identify the optimal timing for outreach when prospects are most receptive. The magic happens when you layer these three dimensions together. A company might fit your firmographic profile (right size, industry, geography) and have compatible technographics (using complementary tools), but without t

Automated Outbound / We Made 24 Prompts So You Don’t Have To Lesson 9 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 We Made 24 Prompts So You Don’t Have To 🧠 Unlocking the Power of AI in Clay: A Treasure Trove of Prompts At Clay, we&#x27;re always striving to empower our users with the most effective tools for data manipulation and analysis. Today, we&#x27;re excited to unveil a game-changing resource: our comprehensive collection of AI prompts designed to supercharge your Clay experience. These carefully crafted prompts are the result of extensive testing and real-world application, aimed at accelerating your AI-driven workflows within our platform. 🗂️ Three Pillars of AI Prompting Our prompts are thoughtfully organized into three main categories, each addressing a crucial aspect of data processing and content creation: Information Summarization: Distilling complex data into digestible insights Information Extraction: Categorizing and pulling specific data points from larger datasets Copywriting and Content Generation: Creating compelling, tailored content at scale Let&#x27;s dive deeper into each category and explore the myriad ways these prompts can transform your workflow. The three main categories of basic AI prompting in Clay 📊 Mastering Information Summarization In today&#x27;s data-rich environment, the ability to quickly synthesize information is invaluable. Our summarization prompts are designed to tackle a wide array of use cases. Imagine connecting your Gong or Fathom call recordings to Clay, then using AI to distill key points from lengthy transcripts. Or consider enriching social media data to surface unique insights about your prospects or customers. These prompts excel at condensing recent news articles, job listings, and company information into actionable intelligence for your sales team. They can even summarize third-party content like blog posts, interviews, or panel discussions, ensuring you stay on top of industry trends without drowning in information. Sample prompts for Summarization 🔍 The Art of Information Extraction Moving beyond summarization, our extraction prompts are designed to pull specific, high-value data points from your datasets. Whether you need to determine which job titles a company sells to, extract coordinates from addresses, or identify a company&#x27;s customer base from scraped data, we&#x27;ve got you covered. These prompts can uncover company missions, target markets, pricing structures, and even analyze job titles to understand role focuses. They can categorize companies as B2B or B2C, identify SaaS providers, assess Glassdoor reviews, and pinpoint the problems a company solves. From normalizing location data to determining time zones and seniority levels, these prompts offer a powerful toolkit for data refinement. Sample prompts for Extracting Information ✍️ Elevating Your Copywriting Game Last but certainly not least, our creative copywriting prompts are designed to add a spark of creativity to your content generation efforts. From the whimsical task of writing bios for animal shelter cats to the practical challenge of crafting compelling subject lines and outreach messages, these prompts cover a broad spectrum of copywriting needs. Need to find the perfect meme to illustrate a customer&#x27;s pain point? We&#x27;ve got a prompt for that. Looking to generate personalized plant recommendations? We&#x27;ve thought of that too. Our copywriting prompts are designed to inject creativity and personalization into your communications at scale. Sample prompts for AI copywriting 🚀 Your Launchpad for AI-Driven Success While we&#x27;ve provided a rich array of prompts to get you started, we encourage you to view these as a foundation rather than a limitation. Feel free to use them as-is, or better yet, adapt and modify them to suit your specific needs. The beauty of these prompts lies in their flexibility - they&#x27;re designed to be tweaked and tailored to your unique use cases. For instance, if you&#x27;re looking to summarize a specific type of content that isn&#x27;t covered in our existing prompts, use one of our summarization prompts as a starting point. Modify it to fit your needs, and you&#x27;ll be off to the races in no time. At Clay, we believe in the power of AI to transform business processes, and these prompts are our way of putting that power directly into your hands. We&#x27;re excited to see how you&#x27;ll use these prompts to drive innovation, streamline your workflows, and uncover new insights within your data. Remember, the world of AI is ever-evolving, and so too will our collection of prompts. We encourage you to experiment, iterate, and share your successes with the Clay community. Together, we&#x27;re pushing the boundaries of what&#x27;s possible with AI-driven data analysis and content creation. Happy prompting, and here&#x27;s to your AI-powered success! Lesson 1 / 10 Next lesson What is Clay in ChatGPT? This course explores what Clay in ChatGPT is, who it&#x27;s designed for, and the core capabilities that let you find people, enrich data, and draft personalized outreach within a single conversation. 🔧 The Current Prospecting Challenge Clay was built to solve the prospecting problem by consolidating 170+ data providers into one platform. But historically, Clay wasn&#x27;t positioned for SDRs and AEs—it&#x27;s a workflow tool that takes time to learn and makes it easy to burn through credits quickly. This ChatGPT integration is the first iteration of "rep tools" that lets sellers access Clay&#x27;s power without building full tables and systems. Instead of opening LinkedIn for contacts, ZoomInfo for emails, Crunchbase for funding data, a company website for tech stack info, your CRM to log everything, and Gmail to draft an email, Clay in ChatGPT collapses all of that into a single conversation. Type: "Find the marketing leaders at Notion and tell me about the last podcast they&#x27;ve been on" ...and get contact information, company data, and research insights without leaving ChatGPT. 🤖 What is Clay in ChatGPT? Clay&#x27;s data enrichment and research capabilities built directly into ChatGPT as a custom GPT: a research assistant that accesses Clay&#x27;s database of over 100 data providers and billions of contact records. It understands context and connects dots across multiple data points. When you ask it to find marketing leaders at a company, it returns names, titles, recent content, career progression, mutual connections, and drafts personalized outreach based on specific insights. 💪 Core Capabilities People Finding Search for contacts by company, role, location, or specific criteria like "find CTOs at Series B SaaS companies in Austin who previously worked at enterprise software companies." Data Enrichment For contacts: email addresses, phone numbers, LinkedIn profiles, social media handles For companies: revenue data, funding information, tech stack details, website traffic, headcount growth trends, job openings Research Through Claygent Research questions like: ‍ "What marketing challenges is this company likely facing based on their recent hiring and product launches?" or "Find recent news about this prospect&#x27;s initiatives." Personalized Message Drafting Craft tailored outreach messages that reference specific, relevant details about the prospect or their company. 👥 Who Is This Built For? Sales reps at SMBs and early-stage startups who need to move fast without heavy CRM processes or RevOps oversight. If you can research prospects and send outreach without multiple approval layers, this tool dramatically speeds up your workflow. Also valuable for: Recruiters identifying candidates VCs researching portfolio companies or investment targets Journalists looking for sources and story angles Marketers building targeted campaigns ‍ You need autonomy in your prospecting process. If every contact requires RevOps approval and Salesforce logging, Clay in ChatGPT might not fit your workflow yet (though it&#x27;s still useful for research). ⚡ What Makes This Different? Most sales tools require rigid workflows: search in one interface, export to another, enrich in a third system, then draft messages in a fourth platform. Clay in ChatGPT is conversational. Refine your search, ask follow-up questions, request additional research, and iterate on messaging in natural language within the same chat thread. It&#x27;s contextually aware. Instead of returning raw data, it synthesizes information and provides insights - noticing when a prospect changed jobs, their company announced a product launch, or they&#x27;ve been discussing specific challenges on LinkedIn. 🚀 What&#x27;s Coming Next We&#x27;re actively building new features: Enhanced Data : Phone number enrichment and first-party data connections Team Collaboration : Role-based access controls and unified organization signup System Integration : Direct CRM integration to automatically sync research and contacts ‍ The vision is making Clay in ChatGPT your central hub for all prospect research and outreach preparation. Next, we&#x27;ll walk through exactly how to set up Clay in ChatGPT. Progress What is HG Insights ✔ 1 What is HG Insights HG Insights in Action ✔ 2 HG Insights in Action Building Company Lists Based on Tech Stack ✔ 3 Building Company Lists Based on Tech Stack Mapping Company Relationships and Ownership ✔ 4 Mapping Company Relationships and Ownership Better Territory Management with Company Data ✔ 5 Better Territory Management with Company Data Forecasting with Parent Company Data ✔ 6 Forecasting with Parent Company Data Personalizing Outreach with Tech Stack Data ✔ 7 Personalizing Outreach with Tech Stack Data Wrapping Up with HG Insights ✔ 8 Wrapping Up with HG Insights Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / How to Use HG Insights in Clay / What is HG Insights Lesson 1 / 8 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 What is HG Insights In this course, we&#x27;re diving deep into one of the most powerful enrichment providers in Clay&#x27;s arsenal: HG Insights. Most technographic providers rely on web scraping and basic detection methods. They crawl websites looking for JavaScript snippets, tracking pixels, and other surface-level indicators. This gives you basic information like "Company X uses Salesforce" or "Company Y has Google Analytics installed." But here&#x27;s the problem: web scraping only captures what&#x27;s publicly visible on a company&#x27;s website. It misses the depth of their actual technology usage, spending patterns, and implementation details that really matter for sales and marketing. HG Insights takes a fundamentally different approach through document analysis. 📄 Document Analysis Methodology Instead of just scraping websites, HG Insights processes billions of business documents. We&#x27;re talking about SEC filings, press releases, contracts, RFPs, job postings, earnings calls, and other corporate documents that reveal the real story behind a company&#x27;s technology decisions. This document analysis methodology uncovers information that web scraping simply cannot access: actual spend amounts, contract terms, implementation timelines, and usage patterns. 🎯 The Difference in Practice Here&#x27;s the difference between basic technographics and HG Insights data: HG Insights tells you that Airbnb runs Salesforce Enterprise Edition plus Marketing Cloud, they&#x27;re spending approximately 180K annually across 50-plus licenses, they upgraded their implementation 8 months ago, and they&#x27;re currently evaluating additional Salesforce products based on recent job postings for Salesforce administrators. Or take a company like Stripe. A basic provider might detect that they use AWS. HG Insights reveals that Stripe has a multi-million dollar AWS contract, they&#x27;re using specific services like Lambda and RDS, they&#x27;ve expanded their usage by 40% in the last year, and they have dedicated AWS architects on staff. This level of detail transforms how you approach prospects because you understand not just what they use, but how they use it and what it means for their business priorities. 🏢 Corporate Structure Visibility HG Insights also provides corporate structure visibility that most providers miss entirely. Basic technographic tools typically focus on single domains or headquarters locations. But enterprise companies are complex - they have subsidiaries, regional offices, and different technology stacks across business units. HG Insights maps these relationships, showing you the complete technology footprint across an organization&#x27;s entire corporate structure. This means you can identify opportunities at subsidiary companies that other providers don&#x27;t even know exist, or understand how technology decisions flow between parent companies and their divisions. 📊 Enterprise Adoption 90% of Fortune 500 technology companies rely on HG Insights data for their go-to-market strategies. And 75% of Fortune 100 companies use their insights for competitive intelligence and market research. 💡 Clay <> HG Insights Integration But here&#x27;s where Clay changes the game for smaller teams and individual users. Traditionally, accessing HG Insights data required expensive annual contracts, often starting at $50,000+ per year with lengthy procurement processes. Clay&#x27;s integration eliminates these barriers entirely. You get the same enterprise-grade technographic data through Clay credits, meaning you get access to Fortune 500-level intelligence without the budget or procurement headaches. 🤔 When to Use HG Insights So when should you use HG Insights versus other technographic providers? Use HG Insights when you need depth over breadth. If you&#x27;re doing high-touch sales with longer deal cycles, the detailed spend and contract information can be the difference between a generic pitch and a conversation that resonates. Use it when you&#x27;re targeting enterprise accounts with complex corporate structures. The subsidiary mapping and organizational visibility helps you identify the right entry points and decision-makers. And use it when timing matters. The contract renewal dates and implementation timelines help you reach prospects when they&#x27;re actually in buying mode, not just when they happen to visit your website. 🚀 What&#x27;s Next In our next lesson, we&#x27;ll walk through exactly how to set up HG Insights enrichment in Clay, including the specific data points you can access and how to structure your tables for maximum efficiency. ‍ Table of contents TOC Heading TOC Heading Related resources Next lesson Next up How to Use HG Insights in Clay HG Insights in Action View next lesson View next lesson Explore, practice and master Clay Powered education Linkedin Youtube Slack community Explore Clay Visit Clay.com Integrations Multi-provider data enrichment Sculptor AI Claygent Audiences Sequencer Pricing Changelog Get started here Get started lesson Clay 101 Enroll in Clay cohorts Engage Find a Clay experts Hire a GTME talent GTM job board Community Join Slack FAQ Legal Privacy policy Terms of service Do not sell my data © Clay 2025 – Born in Brooklyn. Progress Intro to Inbound Automation ✔ 1 Intro to Inbound Automation Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow ✔ 2 Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow Connecting Inbound Lead Sources ✔ 3 Connecting Inbound Lead Sources Your Inbound Enrichment Stack ✔ 4 Your Inbound Enrichment Stack Transforming Data for Inbound ✔ 5 Transforming Data for Inbound Lead Scoring for Inbound ✔ 6 Lead Scoring for Inbound Lead Routing ✔ 7 Lead Routing Personalized Messaging for Inbound ✔ 8 Personalized Messaging for Inbound Deep Dive: Web Intent ✔ 9 Deep Dive: Web Intent Responding to Inbound Leads (Exporting Data) ✔ 9 Responding to Inbound Leads (Exporting Data) Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Automated Inbound / Your Inbound Enrichment Stack Lesson 4 / 9 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Your Inbound Enrichment Stack 🔎 Smart Inbound Lead Enrichment: From Basic Info to Sales Intelligence Today, we&#x27;re diving into the enrichment step of your inbound engine—the process that transforms basic lead information into comprehensive prospect intelligence. Enrichment is the difference between knowing a lead&#x27;s name and knowing whether that lead is worthy of a rep&#x27;s full attention right now. In this lesson, we’ll break down how to enrich smarter and efficiently, showing you how to think creatively strategically about what really matters for your team. 📄 Why Shorter Forms Win in Inbound The unique thing about inbound is that you get to decide how much to ask customers upfront. Spoiler alert: less is more. While more fields allow you to collect more customer data, the longer the form, the higher the friction is for leads. Research shows that just adding two extra form fields - from 3 to 5 - slashes average completing rates by nearly one half. Before Clay, there was an inescapable trade-off between form length and lead quality. Shorter forms led to better conversions but left reps scrambling to manually research basic information on leads just to qualify them. With longer lead forms, companies sought to pre-qualify leads in an attempt to minimize manual research. It’s why so many B2B software demo forms still ask questions like “What is your company size?” With Clay, you don’t need to ask those questions anymore. You can have the best of both worlds: short forms that maximize conversions and minimize speed to lead, without sacrificing the data you need for context-rich follow-up. In a post-Clay world, your inbound forms really only need to ask for one or two critical pieces of info: Name Email address or LinkedIn profile URL From just those data points, we can easily enrich our way to personal info like job title, years of experience, educational background, as well as company data like headcount, industry, description, tech stack, and anything else you might want to learn about. It’s same Jigsaw framework we discussed in Clay 101: we always want to start with those corner pieces before filling in the center. 🧠 Thinking Strategically about Inbound Enrichment Another key difference between enriching inbound leads versus outbound is how you prioritize what data to gather. With outbound, you often want a broad, complete picture of potential prospects in order to identify new targets. With inbound, that script flips: you’re working backwards from bare minimum data points, figuring out just how much data you need to confidently score and prioritize leads while maximizing speed to lead. To put it simply, it’s not about collecting every possible data point— it’s about doubling down on the essential signals that tell you whether or not a lead is worth immediate action. With Clay, you can get incredibly creative about what firmographic, demographic, and behavioral traits represent best fit custom data signals for your company. If you don’t know where to start, you can start by asking: What traits and behaviors do we see consistently in our best customers? At Clay, we know that some key data points for our own segmentation and scoring strategy are company size, which determines which internal team at Clay handles the lead, the lead’s seniority and title, which helps us know whether we’re speaking with a key decision maker, and industry - we tend to sell well to software companies because they usually have RevOps and marketing leaders who are comfortable working with tools like Clay and more open to experimentation. By defining these key must-have signals, we make sure that our enrichment process is focused and directly tied to our revenue motion. 🚿 Waterfall Enrichments: Contact Enrichment As you might remember from 101, all good enrichment starts with Waterfalls. Waterfalls help maximize data coverage and accuracy across our 100+ providers. Let’s start with contact enrichment. You can leverage waterfall enrichments to validate and find data, starting with email address and Linkedin URL. After collecting those corner pieces, you can continue using waterfalls to fill in useful contact data like phone number and social media profiles. With those bits of info, you can quickly extract tons of detailed information about a contact’s work experience and education that can help you understand someone’s background to determine their fit as a prospect or to craft personalized messaging. 💼 Job Change To inform personalized messaging, you might be interested in detecting whether an inbound lead recently changed jobs. The best way to do this is to use the “Job Start Date” enrichment. After identifying when a lead started their most recent role, you can add a formula column to generate a boolean response based on whether the start date falls within the last six months, or whatever time frame you select. Maybe you want to find mutual social media connections between your team and that of your new lead. You can leverage Clay’s integration with The Swarm to find those warm intros that you can mention later in outreach. 🤖 Claygent: Find job title and company Beyond native enrichments and integrations, AI formulas or Claygent are a great way to find nuanced info. Let’s say you want to find a person’s current title and company. While that might seem simple, people might have primary and secondary positions, in addition to advisory or board roles you might want to filter out. Here’s an example of a prompt that let’s you do just that: **You are a job title analyzer. Your task is to identify a person&#x27;s PRIMARY professional role and filter out secondary, advisory, or board positions. **CLASSIFICATION RULES:** **PRIMARY POSITIONS (Include these):** - Full-time executive roles: CEO, CTO, CMO, CFO, COO - Department heads: VP of Sales, Director of Marketing, Head of Engineering - Operational management: General Manager, Operations Manager, Regional Manager - Functional specialists: Senior Developer, Account Executive, Product Manager **SECONDARY/

University All courses / Clay 101: GTM Automation / Your First GTM Use Case Lesson 2 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Your First GTM Use Case This lesson is a small preview into the art of what&#x27;s possible in Clay. We&#x27;re going to quickly look at three different workflows that demonstrate Clay&#x27;s power. Don&#x27;t worry about memorizing every step or understanding all the technical details right now. The purpose here is to show you what kinds of business outcomes become possible once you start to grasp the basics of Clay. 💪 What Makes Clay Truly Powerful What makes Clay truly powerful isn&#x27;t any single feature—it&#x27;s how all these features combine into end-to-end workflows that automate what used to take hours or days of manual work. These workflows create real business outcomes: higher conversion rates, better targeting, more personalized outreach, and access to prospects your competitors can&#x27;t reach. Remember, we&#x27;re showing you possibilities here. The detailed "how to" on building these workflows are coming in the lessons ahead. 📈 Use Case 1: B2B Outbound Campaign Let&#x27;s start with a classic B2B outbound campaign, but supercharged with Clay&#x27;s capabilities. Here&#x27;s how this workflow unfolds: First, we find companies using Clay&#x27;s native dataset, filtering for specific criteria like industry, headcount, and location to match our ideal customer profile. Next, we enrich those companies with firmographic data—things like funding stage, revenue estimates, and technology stack. Then we filter the list down to our most promising prospects. Now we find people at those companies, targeting specific job titles and seniority levels that match our buyer personas. We enrich those people with contact information using Clay&#x27;s email waterfalls. Here&#x27;s where it gets interesting: we use AI formulas to extract the unique companies each person has worked at Finally, we export everything to our CRM and email sequencing tool, complete with personalized subject lines for each prospect. The business outcome? A highly targeted outbound campaign where every email includes genuine, personalized insights. Instead of generic "I saw you work at Company X" messages, you&#x27;re referencing their specific background and experiences. Compare this to the manual approach: what used to take a team of researchers weeks to compile, you can now build in hours. 🗺️ Use Case 2: Local Business Prospecting Now let&#x27;s look at something completely different—targeting local businesses that most B2B tools completely miss. This workflow starts with finding local businesses using Google Maps integration. We&#x27;re not limited to companies with strong online presences or LinkedIn pages. We can find every dentist in Austin, every restaurant in Brooklyn, or every auto repair shop in Phoenix. Then we use Claygent to gather specific business insights that matter to our offering. For example, if we&#x27;re selling to restaurants, Claygent can check if they offer delivery, what their specialties are, or whether they mention specific challenges on their website. We enrich with contact information and business details, including number of reviews and average rating. When we&#x27;re ready, we can export to our outreach tools with highly relevant, location-specific personalization. The business outcome is accessing markets your competitors can&#x27;t reach. While they&#x27;re all fighting over the same companies in traditional B2B databases, you&#x27;re building relationships with local businesses that have real needs but limited online visibility. This gives you a real advantage over competitors—you&#x27;re finding new business opportunities in untapped markets while others chase the same crowded prospects. 🔬 Use Case 3: Advanced Research and Personalization For our third example, let&#x27;s look at the advanced research capabilities that create truly differentiated outreach. This workflow leverages everything we&#x27;ll cover in Clay 101 to conduct deep research on leads and their companies by gathering insights from social mediaprofiles, company websites, and AI-powered web searches. You&#x27;ll discover non-traditional data points that matter, then use all this intelligence to create highly personalized outreach that actually resonates with your prospects. Here&#x27;s how it works: Start by importing your lead data, capturing key information like social mediaprofile URLs from sources like Typeform responses Gather detailed information about each lead&#x27;s experience, skills, and current company situation from social media profiles Enrich company data using social media company URLs to understand company size, industry, and other relevant firmographics Use AI-powered tools like Claygent and ChatGPT to analyze all this data and identify unique insights that others would miss Create personalized outreach materials including tailored messages, research briefs, and even custom memes that speak directly to each prospect&#x27;s situation The result? Sophisticated personalization that creates genuine connections. Instead of surface-level personalization, you&#x27;re reaching out with insights like "I noticed your company just posted three new engineering roles and mentioned AI transformation on your careers page" or "I saw your recent blog post about scaling customer success—we&#x27;ve helped similar companies in your situation." The business outcome is outreach that feels genuinely researched and relevant, leading to much higher response rates and better conversations. You&#x27;re not just another vendor—you&#x27;re someone who clearly understands their business and challenges. 🧩 The Framework Connection Here&#x27;s the best part of these three workflows—they all follow the exact same underlying frameworks we&#x27;re goin

Learn more about cohorts Learn more about cohorts Learn more about cohorts Talents Hire GTME Talent Find and connect with GTM talent who&#x27;ve demonstrated expertise in building advanced workflows Explore GTME talents Explore GTME talents Explore GTME talents FAQ Why are certifications paused? ​ GTM engineering and Clay are evolving quickly. We want to make sure the certification program keeps pace and that being Clay Certified continues to hold weight with employers, partners, and the broader community. We&#x27;re using this time to rethink assessment design, skill validation, and what mastery looks like. What if I currently hold a Clay Certification? ​ Your certification stands. Nothing changes. If you earned it, it&#x27;s yours. I was about to submit. What should I do? ​ Hang tight. Join the waitlist and you&#x27;ll be first to know when we reopen. Any submissions received before the pause are still being reviewed. When will certifications come back? ​ We don&#x27;t have a specific date yet, but it will be soon. We&#x27;ll share an update once we have a clearer timeline. Join the waitlist to make sure you hear about it. I need certification for a Clay partner requirement. What do I do? ​ The certifications program is paused for general applicants, but if you need a certification as part of becoming a Solutions Partner, the process is still open for you. Start by applying through the Solutions Partner application linked from our directory , where you&#x27;ll get access to rubrics, evaluation guidelines, and submission links. Will the same four tracks come back? ​ We&#x27;re rethinking the full program structure, so the tracks may look different when we return. That&#x27;s part of why we paused: we want to make sure the next version reflects where GTM engineering is headed, not just where it&#x27;s been. Can I give input on what the new program might look like? ​ We&#x27;d love to hear from you. Contact Aly Slater, our certifications program lead, directly at aly.slater@clay.com - or share your thoughts when you sign up for the waitlist. We&#x27;re building this with our community, not just for it. Who do I reach out to if I need help with my certifications submission and/or results? (previous program) ​ Please reach out to aly.slater@clay.com ! ‍ Does Clay offer team or organizational certifications? (previous program) ​ No. Certifications are individual credentials. Our system verifies that you created the table you&#x27;re submitting to make sure that it reflects your individual skills, not collaborative work or tables built by others. How many times can I resubmit? (previous program) ​ There is no limit to the number of times you can resubmit! ‍ Do I need a paid account to be awarded a clay certification? (previous program) ​ You should be able to complete the requirements for the Outbound and Inbound Certifications without needing a paid plan. However, for the CRM enrichment plan, Pro features are required. ## https://university.clay.com/claybooks/automate-financial-insights-for-enterprise-accounts

Automate financial insights for enterprise accounts - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / Automate financial insights for enterprise accounts Automate financial insights for enterprise accounts Use Clay and Oakie.ai to unlock 10-K, 10-Q, and earnings call intelligence in seconds, without lifting a finger. Start building now with No items found. Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to use Claygent and Oakie to find and summarize 10-Ks, 10-Qs, and earnings calls Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin If you’re part of an enterprise sales team, there’s a good chance you’re under-leveraging one of the richest sources of account insight available: 10-Ks, 10-Qs, and earnings calls. The problem? It’s a manual, time-consuming process. At best, you might load a 10-K into GPT once in a while, but there’s no easy system to stay updated. That’s why we built this Claybook: to show you how to automate financial insights using Clay + Oakie.ai (a platform for custom financial agents inside Clay). First, let’s set the stage: If you’re selling into Enterprise accounts right now (Q2 2025), you would need all three of the following: The company’s 2024 10-K The company’s Q1 2025 10-Q Insights from their latest earnings call One document alone isn’t enough. The 10-K covers last year but misses current updates. The 10-Q covers this quarter but isn’t as detailed as the 10-K. And earnings calls give you future-looking insights that neither document can capture. Tracking all three — across every account on different fiscal calendars — quickly becomes impossible to manage manually. That’s where Oakie.ai inside Clay changes the game. Oakie.ai lets you build custom agents. In this case, Israel Zalmanov (co-founder) built a financial agent that works directly inside Clay. With it, you can: Upload a list of accounts Add Oakie.ai as an enrichment Define the key financial questions you care about Instantly pull answers from the latest 10-K or 10-Q (with earnings call transcripts coming soon) And we’re not stopping there. By adding scheduled runs inside Clay, you can set your table to update automatically—daily, weekly, or monthly. The system will pull the latest filings, run your custom financial analysis, and deliver fresh insights into your CRM, Slack channel, or wherever your sales team works. With this setup, you’ll create a fully automated pipeline of backward-and forward-looking financial intelligence for every target account—without lifting a finger after setup. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 3 Step 2: Customize prompts and run table Good news: This table is so dialed in that all you need to do is drop the name of a publicly-traded enterprise company (e.g. Atlassian) in the first column and the rest will work its magic, automatically. But since every business and category is different, take this time to analyze the AI prompts (both Claygent and Oakie) in case you need to customize them to your needs. For example, Claygent, Clay’s AI web research agent , summarizes earning call transcripts—if there’s something specific you want to add to the summary, adjust the prompt accordingly. And Oakie.ai analyzes growth objectives and operational challenges—if there’s something specific you want to find, adjust the prompt now. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Community engagement is essential, but recognizing and rewarding your most active members usually takes a lot of manual effort. So we created this Claybook to help our team at Clay automate awards (in the form of Clay credits) to our most rabid Slack community upvoters. How? By using Tightknit , Typeform (optional), and, of course, Clay. How it works: We create an award in Tightknit for users who upvote Slack threads the most If you win, Tightknit sends you a Slack DM congratulating you on your victory Using a Tightknit webhook, we then send the winners information to a Clay table Since we want to award our users with Clay credits, we then automate a Slack DM with a Typeform link asking for their workspace email Once we receive it, we look up their workspace ID in Snowflake, and use an HTTP API call to distribute their credits automatically Want to award power users in your Slack community with credits to your platform? The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Set up a reference table First things first, you’ll want to create and customize a Clay table that lists all your awards, the award ID from Tightknit, their credit amounts, and any other relevant information. You’ll use this table as an internal record and reference table so you can standardize your credit gifts to users. For example, in our reference table, we include the Tightknit award ID (required), award name, credit amount, and award notes. We’ll reference this information in another table in order to distribute the right credit amounts. ‍ 3 Step 3: Send data to Clay via a Tightknit webhook Next, set up your Tightknit webhook (Table: Send Tightknit Typeform) so you can automatically send award information to Clay as soon as it’s announced through Slack. To do that, copy the Clay webhook URL in column one and paste it back in Tightknit. For more information on setting up your webhook in Tightknit, follow their documentation here . Once a new award gets announced via Slack, this table will send a unique Typeform link (optional) to the award winner via a Slack direct message using an HTTP API call. Why? At Clay, we need the user&#x27;s workspace email so we know which account to distribute credits to—Typeform asks for the email. ‍ 4 Step 4: Send data to Clay via a Typeform webook (optional) Next, if applicable, set up a Typeform webhook (Table: Tightknit Typeform Outputs). Here’s how it works: Once the user submits their Typeform, the Typeform webhook will send their workspace email back to Clay where we can look them up in our Snowflake database, find their workspace ID, and distribute the awarded credits. Then we’ll trigger an automated direct message via Slack notifying them that we’ve added credits. ‍ 5 Step 5: Set up an HTTP API call to send credits to your users Next, we’re going to use HTTP API to connect to our Clay API so we can automate the distribution of credits. Customize this step by connecting to your own HTTP API. Last, using the same type of HTTP API call we used previously to send a direct message via Slack, we&#x27;re going to send two different messages: one for successful credit distributions and one for failed distributions. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin When a trial gets extended, your AEs need to know and your CRM needs to reflect it. This Claybook helps you automate the entire trial extension workflow: pull account data from Snowflake when a free trial extension initiates, lookup the account’s AE in Salesforce, send them a real-time Slack alert, and log the extension in CRM—all without lifting a finger. No more chasing down trial status or forgetting to follow up. Your AEs stay in the loop, and your data stays clean. How it works: Import account-level data from Snowflake (or any data source) Lookup each account’s opportunity and owner in Salesforce Use Slack IDs to send real-time alerts to the right AE Create a new trial extension record in Salesforce to close the loop ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Import account data from Snowflake (or data warehouse) The table template you copy to your workspace won’t come with data in it. To import account data from Snowflake, just click on the “+” icon in the first column, log in to your Snowflake account, select your Snowflake database, and submit. Once imported, map each respective data point to its own column in the table. For us, we’re importing the following from accounts that just got a free trial extension: email and company URL, their Clay workspace ID, their account executives information, and their opportunity ID that we’ll use to lookup their record in Salesforce. Not using Snowflake? You can delete this column and import account data from any other data warehouse or source. ‍ 3 Step 3: Lookup account and AE in Salesforce (or CRM) Next, we’re going to use the opportunity ID we just pulled in from Snowflake to lookup the account’s record in Salesforce and import that data into the table. Then we’re going to use the owner ID attached to the account’s record to import the account executives&#x27; Slack user ID so we can automate trial extension alerts. Customize the “Get Owner” and “Get Opp” CRM lookups to do the same. ‍ 3 Step 3: Lookup account and AE in Salesforce (or CRM) Next, we’re going to use the opportunity ID we just pulled in from Snowflake to lookup the account’s record in Salesforce and import that data into the table. Then we’re going to use the owner ID attached to the account’s record to import the account executives&#x27; Slack user ID so we can automate trial extension alerts. Customize the “Get Owner” and “Get Opp” CRM lookups to do the same. ‍ 4 Step 4: Customize your Slack message Next, using data we pulled in from Snowflake and Salesforce, we’re going to automate a Slack message to our account executives every time a new trial extension gets added to one of their accounts. Customize the Slack message to fit your style and preferences. ‍ 5 Step 5: Create a free trial record in Salesforce (or CRM) Last, we’re going to close the loop by creating a new record in Salesforce that details the account’s recent free trial extension. Now, moving forward, every time a new trial extension gets triggered in Snowflake, each account’s respective AE will get a Slack alert and Salesforce will get updated with a new record. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to automate account reviews using AI ‍ Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Most customer experience leaders run regular account reviews: monthly or quarterly deep dives into the health and trajectory of strategic and enterprise accounts. These reviews are critical for driving renewals, identifying expansion opportunities, and preventing churn. But too often, they rely on scattered spreadsheets, manual data pulls, and last-minute scrambles to piece together a clear picture of each customer. That’s where Clay comes in. This Claybook shows you how to automate account reviews using Clay, pulling in up-to-date data from CRMs, product usage tools, support systems, and more to generate a living, breathing snapshot of each account. Instead of chasing down context, your team gets a single view that includes: Health rating + reasoning Current use cases and feature adoption Product feedback and support history Risks to renewal Opportunities for expansion How it works: Import account data from anywhere: CRM, data warehouse, support tool, billing software, Gong, etc. Customize account review inputs: create columns for every relevant data point your import Use AI to automate reviews: plug those account inputs into an AI prompt that summarizes and scores account health ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Import account data You can import account data from anywhere: your CRM, a data warehouse, Gong, billing tools, support platforms (e.g. Intercom), or directly from Clay’s out-of-the-box enrichment. For example, we’re importing data from Salesforce, which stores most of our account information like subscription data, product usage stats, and Gong calls, and Snowflake. Need help figuring out what data to import for your account reviews? Here’s some inspiration: Commercial summary: contract value (ARR/MRR), renewal date, expansion or contraction history, payment status or billing issues Product usage & engagement: logins / active users vs. licenses, key feature adoption (what are they actually using?), usage trends (flat, growing, or declining), last activity date or period of inactivity Support & satisfaction: support ticket volume / time to resolution, open/closed tickets, NPS / CSAT scores, escalations or major issues flagged Stakeholder health: who the key decision-makers and power users are, whether those people are still at the company, level of engagement (meeting attendance, feedback loops) Customer goals & success plans : what outcomes were promised or expected, progress toward those goals, documented success metrics (and whether they’re being hit) Renewal & expansion signals: license utilization (over or under), cross-sell / upsell opportunities, org changes, funding events, or tech stack shifts, intent data or buying signals (if available) ‍ Account notes & relationship context: internal notes from AMs/CSMs/sales, meeting summaries, previous challenges, wins, or executive sponsors 3 Step 3: Customize account review inputs Just because you import it, doesn’t mean you need to use it. For example, in this table, we import loads of account data from our CRM and Snowflake, but we only use the following: Basic CRM record data : account name, record ID, account manager, etc. Product usage: subscription plan, credit usage and pacing, ARR, days left on contract, one year credit limit, last 7-day usage, top use cases (extracted using an AI prompt) Product feedback: feedback, concerns, or suggestions extracted from Gong call transcripts Decide which inputs you want to use in your account review and which you don’t. In the next step, you’ll feed those inputs into ‍ 4 Step 4: Customize account review AI prompt Next, customize the account review AI prompt to fit your business and needs. Currently, it’s using the inputs mentioned above to report on the overall health of the account, identify risks and opportunities, and spotlight product use cases and feedback. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin As our customer support team grows at Clay, maintaining consistent, qualitative feedback regarding support effectiveness has gotten much harder. While individual support ticket reviews were helpful, they were also time-consuming. So we built a QA engine in Clay to automate feedback on customer support tickets. This Claybook sends closed tickets from Intercom to Clay where ChatGPT runs them through four qualitative checks: understanding and clarity, problem solving and resolution, communication and tone, setting expectations. We then send summaries and feedback to the team through Slack for review (see below). I’m morally against using AI to measure the success of our support team. So we use this system to find areas of opportunity, not to measure how well each individual is doing. If we get a low QA score, we can see where in the support conversation we could have improved and what to do better next time. All in real time. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 4 Step 4: Customize GPT prompts Customize any of the OpenAI prompts to better fit your needs. Certain prompts include reference to Clay.com, for example. Update with your business name and adjust as needed. Currently, ChatGPT runs four prompts to analyze four separate customer support call criteria: Understanding and clarity (column 9) Problem solving and resolution (column 11) Communication and tone (column 14) Setting expectations (column 17) 5 Step 5: Connect to Slack Last, if your Slack account isn’t already connected to your Clay account, add it now, along with the ID of the channel you want to send feedback to.
