## https://university.clay.com/claybooks/classify-ticket-complexity-to-prioritize-route-and-improve-support

Classify ticket complexity to prioritize, route, and improve support - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Customer experience / Classify ticket complexity to prioritize, route, and improve support Classify ticket complexity to prioritize, route, and improve support How to import support tickets from Intercom and classify difficulty on a scale from “very easy” to “very hard.” Start building now with Intercom Download the template What we used Clay ( Explorer ): to import Intercom support tickets, clean data, and rate ticket difficulty Intercom (Paid): to push support tickets to Clay for analysis Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Support tickets are chock full of valuable information that you can use across every department in your business. For example, we use support tickets to catalog bugs, reference recurring issues, find support article topics, and identify Fin AI (Intercom’s AI agent) success rate. But in this specific Claybook, we’re going to show you how to import support conversations and classify the complexity of a ticket as “very easy,” “easy,” “medium,” “hard,” or “very hard.” Scoring support tickets by difficulty might sound like overkill—but it’s actually a game-changer. When you classify tickets from very easy to very hard , three big things happen: You work smarter. Harder tickets get routed to senior agents, simple ones get handled (or deflected) faster, and your team’s time is better spent. You spot patterns. Repeated bugs, complex features, and low-AI-deflection areas become easier to flag and fix. You track what matters. CSAT means more when you know how hard the ticket was. And performance benchmarks finally have context. In short: it’s not just about labeling tickets—it’s about leveling up your entire support operation. How it works : Import Intercom support conversations via webhook and HTTP API Clean support tickets of any irrelevant content that may cause AI to hallucinate Analyze customer support conversations for specific criteria Use AI (and our customer support inputs) to score ticket difficulty ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Import Intercom conversations into Clay This happens in two phases: first, connect to Intercom via webhook (column one) and import conversation IDs from Intercom; second, using HTTP API and the conversation IDs, import all support ticket transcripts into Clay too. ‍ 3 Step 3: Clean support responses of any irrelevant information (blue columns) Next, we analyze all support responses and clean them of any irrelevant information that doesn’t directly address the customer’s issue, like “Happy to help!” or “Can you send the table link?” This leaves you with a “Cleaned Support Response” column focused only on useful, issue-solving content. It helps reduce noise and avoid AI hallucinations later on. Next, we use formulas to calculate: How many cleaned messages there are Where that count ranks (percentile-wise) vs. other tickets Total word count of the convo Word count percentile Add, delete, or customize the formulas and AI prompts in this step (all blue-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ 4 Step 4: Analyze customer responses (yellow columns) Next, we extracted client messages into CLIENT_RESPONSE, counted them, and ranked their volume—more messages often meant higher complexity. We then flagged frustrations, troubleshooting attempts, and topic count to identify harder tickets. Last, we used AI to infer client experience and receptiveness, which impact resolution time. Add, delete, or customize the formulas and AI prompts in this step (all yellow-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ 5 Step 5: Look for any bugs (green columns) Next, we used only the support agent’s messages (SUPPORT_AGENT_RESPONSE) to detect bugs, avoiding false flags from clients mislabeling issues. The Bug Detection column flags the bug and shows the triggering message. If flagged, Bug Functionality reads the full convo to identify the broken enrichment and summarize what the client was doing. Splitting this into two steps reduced hallucinations and improved accuracy. Customize the AI prompt and outputs in this step (all green-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ 6 Step 6: Score ticket difficulty (violet columns) Last, we used ChatGPT-4 and Claude 3.7 to rate ticket difficulty (Ticket Complexity 1 and 2). If their ratings were close, we averaged them. If they differed by 2+ levels—or disagreed on “medium”—we flagged it. Binary Response Complexity forced a choice between the two. If confidence was low, Ticket Difficulty Reasoning Model reviewed both explanations and chose the stronger one. Add, delete, or customize the formulas and AI prompts in this step (all violet-colored columns) to fit your business and industry. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Start building now with APIVoid Apify Download the template What we used Clay (Explorer+) to research and enrich companies and identify M&A APIVoid (Paid) to check website status of companies who were acquired Apify (Optional) fallback to find employee headcount if needed ‍ Free resources Copy the Clay table template Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . I&#x27;m also personally available to help troubleshoot. You can send me, Jacob Tuwiner , a message on LinkedIn, or schedule a meeting with my Claygency, Sculpted , to learn how we can help. ‍ Get started Before you begin Most go-to-market workflows break down before they even begin because the data at the top of the funnel is already flawed. Inaccurate company names, stale headcounts, and unresolved M&A records lead to bad routing, missed opportunities, and bloated CRMs. For Nooks.ai (one of our Sculpted.agency clients), the problem was no different. So we created this Claybook that introduces a structured data workflow purpose-built to solve the problem. It’s a modular workflow that transforms messy company inputs into clean, enriched records ready for routing, enrichment, and reporting. Here&#x27;s how it works: Intake & Normalization: It starts by cleaning raw company names and domains—removing URL junk, fixing casing, and standardizing formats. B2B SaaS Classification: Next, it determines whether the company is both B2B and SaaS, so you can filter out irrelevant records early. M&A Detection: It checks for acquisitions, identifies the acquiring and acquired companies, and corrects name/domain mismatches. Acquisition Status Check: If a company was acquired, it flags whether the brand is still active (sells independently) or inactive (fully absorbed). Headcount Enrichment: Finally, it pulls accurate employee counts from LinkedIn with two fallbacks—ensuring >95% coverage and 99% accuracy. With this Claybook, you can tackle three of the most common go-to-market data issues: M&A Chaos: Acquisitions often leave duplicate records and misnamed brands that confuse routing logic. Headcount Errors: Reps get SMB accounts routed as Enterprise—or the reverse—due to stale or misattributed employee counts. CRM Bloat: Inactive brands clutter reporting and confuse account ownership. Watch the full guided demo below, or skip ahead for a step by step breakdown: Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 2 Step 2: ‍ Add company names and domains to the first table To start this workflow, manually enter record IDs (optional, but recommended), company names, and company domains into the first three columns, respectively. From there, Clay will automatically normalize company names and domains, then write that data to a second table for further enrichment. To learn how to write data to a different table, take the Clay 101 lesson: Mastering Write to Table. ‍ 3 Step 3: Edit AI prompts to fit your category and business The second table “B2B SaaS Check” uses a series of Claygent and ChatGPT prompts (six total) to identify whether or the company is a SaaS company in B2B: SaaS Research (3 prompts): Company description What they sell Pricing model B2B Research: Single Claygent prompt to analyze target customers. Decision prompts: Two separate evaluations: SaaS check: Reviews 3 SaaS Research summaries → returns is_saas B2B check: Analyzes target custom summary→ returns is_b2b Replace the six prompts with your own category definitions to tailor the table to your needs. After the table determines whether or not the company fits your stated criteria (in our example, B2B SaaS), it writes those companies to a new table for further enrichment. To learn how to master AI prompting, take the Clay 101 lesson: The S.P.I.C.E Framework 5 Step 5: Enrich companies with employee headcount Next, we’re going to enrich companies with employee headcount. To do that, we enrich companies with their LinkedIn company data. If a company doesn’t exist in Clay’s database (rare, but it happens), you can use Apify (natively integrated with Clay but you need your own account to run it) to find additional company headcount. 6 Step 6: Update CRM records Last, it’s time to update your CRM with clean company names, domains, and employee headcount, and create a company-to-company association if a company was acquired by another company. This final table includes all of the data we collected in the previous tables that you need to push to your CRM to update, organized into one pane of glass. Simply add a CRM lookup column, or create/update object column. You can push data to any CRM or export via CSV as well. To learn how to create or update objects in CRM, take the Clay 101 lesson: Mastering CRM data export. Start building now with Beauhurst Download the template What we used Clay (Paid): Powers the full CRM enrichment workflow — pulls in existing account data, runs Beauhurst&#x27;s enrichment actions across every row, applies scoring and routing logic, and syncs enriched records back to your CRM automatically. Beauhurst: Provides three core actions — Enrich Company, Find Company Funding, and Find Company Corporate Structure — that fill gaps in company records, surface funding signals, and map corporate hierarchies. You&#x27;ll need to bring your own Beauhurst API key to connect the integration inside Clay. Your CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, or other): The source of your existing account data and the destination for enriched records once the workflow runs. ‍ Free resources Download the template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert Get started Dirty CRM data is one of the biggest blockers to effective outbound and account management — missing fields, outdated funding information, and unclear corporate structures mean reps are working with incomplete context and routing decisions are made on bad data. This Claybook solves that by applying Beauhurst&#x27;s three core actions to your existing CRM accounts. Enrich Company fills in missing firmographic details like company registration numbers and LinkedIn URLs so every account is actually actionable. Find Company Funding adds funding data at scale — grants, total fundraising, and investment history — so you can build routing logic, identify growth signals, and trigger re-engagement at the right moment. Find Company Corporate Structure maps parent-subsidiary relationships so you can merge duplicates, route complex accounts to strategic sales, and disqualify records whose parent company puts them outside your ICP. Once enriched, everything syncs automatically back to your CRM on whatever cadence you set. ‍ How it works: Pull in your CRM data from Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other CRM integration to populate your Clay table with the accounts you want to clean and enrich. Run Enrich Company to fill gaps in your company records — pulling registration numbers, LinkedIn URLs, and other missing firmographic data directly from Beauhurst&#x27;s dataset. Run Find Company Funding to layer in funding history at scale — number of grants, total fundraising, and investment rounds — so you can build routing logic, flag growth signals, and trigger re-engagement workflows. Run Find Company Corporate Structure to map parent-subsidiary relationships for every account — giving reps clarity on true buying centers, surfacing duplicate records, and flagging accounts whose parent company falls outside your ICP.. Sync enriched data back to your CRM using an Update action to keep Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other CRM automatically up to date on whatever cadence you set. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Copy this template First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Pull in your CRM data Use your CRM integration to import existing account records into Clay as the starting point for enrichment. Customize your import using the following available inputs: CRM source (Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other connected CRM) Account filters (e.g. only pull accounts missing key fields, or accounts within a specific segment or ownership tier) Fields to import (company name, domain, existing firmographic data, owner, and any other relevant CRM fields) ‍ 3 Step 3: Run Enrich Company Use the Beauhurst: Enrich Company action to fill gaps in your company records with Beauhurst&#x27;s dataset. Customize your enrichment by mapping the following available identifiers and outputs: Company name or domain as the identifier Company registration number LinkedIn URL Firmographic details (industry, headcount, location, and more) ‍ 4 Step 4: Run Find Company Funding Use the Beauhurst: Find Company Funding action to layer detailed funding history onto each account. Customize your funding data capture using the following available outputs: Number of grants received Total fundraising amount Individual funding rounds (round type, date, amount, and investors) Use as a routing trigger — e.g. flag accounts that have raised a Series A or above for enterprise routing Use as a re-engagement signal — e.g. trigger outreach when a new funding round is detected ‍ 5 Step 5: Run Find Company Corporate Structure Use the Beauhurst: Find Company Corporate Structure action to map parent-subsidiary relationships for each account. Customize your structure mapping using the following available outputs: Parent company identification Subsidiary list Use to merge duplicate records (e.g. same parent company appearing multiple times in your CRM) Use to route complex accounts to strategic sales based on parent company size or tier Use to disqualify records whose parent company falls outside your ICP ‍ 6 Step 6: Sync enriched data back to your CRM Use the Update CRM action to automatically push all enriched fields back to your Salesforce, HubSpot, or other CRM instance. Customize your sync using the following available inputs: Fields to update (registration number, LinkedIn URL, funding data, corporate structure, ICP score) Update cadence (set the table to rerun on a schedule to keep records continuously up to date) Conditional update logic (only overwrite empty fields, or overwrite all with latest Beauhurst data) CRM destination (Salesforce, HubSpot, or any other connected CRM) ‍ Get Started Start cleaning and enriching your CRM accounts with Beauhurst to fill data gaps, layer in funding signals, and map corporate structures — then sync everything back to your CRM automatically. And now you can use Clay to scale thousands of personalized Arcade demos in seconds. For example, say you just launched a new product feature and want to send personalized product demos to potential buyers that fit your ICP. Traditionally, you’d have to personalize a new demo for every potential customer, or send one generic demo to everyone. Nevermind the process you’d have to perform to actually find ideal companies worth reaching out to in the first place. Now, using Clay and Arcade, you can find target companies in seconds and insert personalized snippets into Arcade demos using their custom variables feature—automatically. Using Arcade’s custom variables feature , select which steps you’ll personalize with Clay’s AI-generated snippets. 3 Customize AI prompts in Clay Next, before running the table, customize AI prompts to fit your business. There’s three prompts in the second table. The first one likely doesn’t need customization. The other prompts create snippets for specific custom variables in Arcade (currently two different variables). Note: If your Arcade includes more than two variables, add an additional prompt column for each additional variable. 4 Paste Arcade URL into Clay This Clay table doesn’t require any HTTP API connections. Instead, it uses custom variable URL strings. Clay’s AI will find your company description, create an ideal customer profile (ICP), and define your feature set in seconds. We’ll use this information in the second table to tailor your Arcade demo variables. 6 Step 6: Import companies and run the table Last, select your targeting criteria and import companies and the table will run automatically. ## https://university.clay.com/claybooks/domain-deliverability-check

Domain Deliverability Check - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Other / Domain Deliverability Check Domain Deliverability Check Stop hurting your deliverability — flag risky domains before you hit send Start building now with No items found. Download the template What we used Clay account to manage and automate domain analysis workflows Domain list or emails with extractable domains API keys (optional, for custom WHOIS or DNS tools) ‍ Free resources ‍ https://app.clay.com/shared-table/share_6VpwoE7yKyUj Need help? Ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before you begin Cold email deliverability issues don’t usually come from bad messaging—they come from bad data. Risky domains with no inboxes, recent registrations, or spam traps can quietly wreck your sender reputation before your campaign even gets off the ground. This Claybook helps you stop that at the source. ‍ But first, here’s a quick refresher on some key technical terms you’ll see throughout this workflow: MX Records (Mail Exchange): These DNS records determine if a domain is capable of receiving emails. No MX = no inbox. TTL (Time to Live): A DNS metric that can indicate how secure or stable a domain’s setup is. Very low TTLs can be a red flag. WHOIS Data: Public records about domain registration—like when a domain was created, who owns it, and when it expires. Trap Domains: Domains set up specifically to catch and block spammers. Emailing them hurts your reputation. Catch-All Domains: Domains that accept emails sent to any address (even invalid ones). They’re risky because they hide bounces. ‍ For RevOps, Demand Gen, and Deliverability teams, the challenge is always the same: how do you catch these risks before the damage is done? So we created this Claybook to automate domain risk detection before you press send. It’s a modular workflow that transforms raw domain lists into clean, enriched, and fully risk-assessed records—so you can protect your sender score and filter with confidence. ‍ Here’s how it works: 1. Domain Intake: Start with any list of emails or domains—Clay parses and normalizes them automatically. 2. Email Config Check: Confirm valid MX records and assess TTL to gauge email readiness and potential red flags. 3. WHOIS Metadata: Pull domain age, expiration timing, and change history to spot sketchy or disposable domains. 4. Risk Detection: Use tools like Hunter.io to flag trap domains, catch-alls, and other high-risk patterns. 5. Aggregated Scoring: Combine all risk signals into a simple “Domain Red Flags” column to make fast decisions. ‍ With this Claybook, you can avoid three of the most common outbound killers: Silent Deliverability Decay: Catch dangerous domains early—before they degrade your sender reputation. Mystery Bounce Spikes: Know which domains are likely to fail before launch. Wasted Effort: Stop chasing unreachable leads that never had valid inboxes to begin with. Watch the full walkthrough below, or skip to the step-by-step setup. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Base Table Setup Make a Copy of this template Create a new Clay table Add / Upload your list of company domains as the primary column 2 Step 2: Add Email Configuration Enrichment Use the Google MX Records enrichment to check for: Whether the domain has email inboxes configured (MX records) TTL (Time to Live), which loosely reflects email security processing time ‍ 3 Step 3: Add WHOIS or domain metadata enrichments Add WHOIS or domain metadata enrichments to pull: Days since domain registration Days until domain expiration Days since last update or change Enrich domain security events (e.g., clientDeleteProhibited, clientTransferProhibited) 4 Step 4: Add Email Risk Enrichment Use Hunter.io (or similar) to check for: Catch-all domains Trap domains 5 Step 5: Output or Sync Filter your table to show only domains without red flags Export or sync clean contacts into your CRM or outbound tool For flagged domains, optionally create a second flow (e.g., waterfall validation for catch-alls) Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Get started Before we begin ‍ Using Typeform and need to enrich, classify, and distribute leads evenly to the right SDRs? ‍ Let Clay do it for you. ‍ This Claybook imports leads from Typeform, enriches them with personal and company data, classifies them into urgent, enterprise, and regular, then distributes those leads evenly amongst SDRs. Currently, it ranks lead seniority from "A" to "C": "A" for founder/CEO/leadership roles, "B" for mid-level roles, and "C" for junior positions. If data is insufficient to assign a rank, it outputs "Unranked". To customize ranking, edit the “Level Ranking” Claygent prompt. 3 Step 3: Customize lead ranking criteria (optional) The purpose of this Claybook is to help you feed the right leads to the right SDRs. Currently, it ranks lead seniority from "A" to "C": "A" for founder/CEO/leadership roles, "B" for mid-level roles, and "C" for junior positions. If data is insufficient to assign a rank, it outputs "Unranked". To customize ranking, edit the “Level Ranking” Claygent prompt. 4 Step 4: Customize lead classification formula This table classifies leads into three categories based on employee count and days since submission: urgent, enterprise, and regular. Specific SDRs will then get assigned those leads in a round robin fashion. To customize lead classification, edit the “Output Classification” formula. 5 Step 5: Customize round robin assignment names Last, customize your round robin assignment names and quantity. In this table, we’ve labeled assignment names using numbers (1-6), but we recommended labeling them with your SDRs or AEs names. Start building now with Lusha Download the template What we used Clay (Paid): Powers the enrichment workflow — connects your people sources, runs the Lusha Enrich Person action across every contact row, applies filtering logic, and routes enriched contacts to your CRM, sequencer, or inbound motion. Lusha (API key required): Provides the Enrich Person action that returns verified emails with confidence scores and direct dials with Do Not Call indicators — with ~85% phone accuracy and non-scraped data for European compliance coverage. You&#x27;ll need to bring your own Lusha API key to connect the integration inside Clay. Free resources Download the template here ‍ Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ ‍ Get started Contact enrichment is only as good as the data it returns — and many providers struggle with accuracy, coverage, or compliance, particularly across European markets. Bad emails hurt deliverability. Unverified phone numbers waste rep time. And scraped data exposes your team to compliance risk on every dial. This Claybook solves that by adding Lusha&#x27;s Enrich Person action to your existing contact enrichment chains. With ~85% phone accuracy and non-scraped data, Lusha surfaces verified emails with confidence scores and direct dials with Do Not Call list indicators — so your reps stay compliant and your outreach actually connects. It works across every major motion: inbound enrichment, outbound list building, and CRM hygiene. ‍ HOW IT WORKS: Bring in your contact list from any people source — a Clay Find People search, a Lusha lookalike result, a CRM export, or any other integration that populates a Clay table with contact rows. Run Lusha&#x27;s Enrich Person action using a few key identifiers per contact — LinkedIn URL, email, full name and company domain, or full name and company name — to retrieve verified contact data at scale. Pull verified emails with confidence scores to trust your deliverability metrics before contacts ever hit a sequence. Pull direct dials with Do Not Call indicators so your reps know exactly who they can legally call before picking up the phone. Feed enriched contacts downstream into your inbound routing, outbound sequencer, or CRM sync — with cleaner data and fewer bounces across every motion. ‍ Note: Lusha requires you to connect your own API key inside Clay to activate the Enrich Person action. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Copy this template First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Bring in your contact list Use any people source as your starting point to populate your Clay table with contact rows. Customize your input using any of the following sources: Clay&#x27;s native Find People action Lusha&#x27;s Find People Lookalikes action A CRM export (HubSpot, Salesforce, or other) Any other Clay integration that returns contact-level rows ‍ 3 Step 3: Run Lusha&#x27;s Enrich Person action Use the Lusha: Enrich Person action to retrieve verified contact data for each row in your table. Customize your enrichment by mapping any of the following available identifiers: LinkedIn URL / professional profile URL Email Full name and company domain Full name and company name ‍ 4 Step 4: Pull verified emails with confidence scores Use the Include Emails toggle within the Enrich Person action to return email data for each contact. Customize what you capture using the following available outputs: Verified email address Email confidence score (to filter by deliverability threshold before contacts hit your sequencer) ‍ 5 Step 5: Pull direct dials with Do Not Call indicators Use the Include Phone Numbers toggle within the Enrich Person action to return phone data for each contact. Customize what you capture using the following available outputs: Direct dial phone number Do Not Call list status (to automatically flag contacts your reps cannot legally call) ‍ 6 Step 6: Feed enriched contacts downstream Use a Filter , Push to CRM , or Send to Sequencer action to route your enriched contacts into the appropriate downstream motion. Customize your routing logic using criteria such as: Email confidence score threshold (only route contacts above a set deliverability score) Do Not Call status (exclude flagged contacts from call-based sequences) Enrichment match status (only push fully enriched rows) Motion type — inbound routing, outbound sequencer, or CRM hygiene sync ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Extract data from paginated databases in seconds - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / Extract data from paginated databases in seconds Extract data from paginated databases in seconds Don’t let pagination stop you from extracting the custom data you need to fuel your marketing and sales. Extract it with Clay instead. Start building now with ZenRows Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ) to scrape and clean paginated data Free resources Download the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Manually scraping data from large, paginated databases takes forever. And many web scrapers simply can’t navigate pagination easily to do it automatically. Good news: this Claybook uses Zenrow and Clay’s custom formulas to scrape paginated databases in seconds. How it works: Create thousands of paginated database URLs using Clay formulas, automatically Use Zenrows (natively integrated in Clay) to scrape each page, one by one Use scraped data for enrichment, personalization, outbound, and more Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. 2 Step 2: Add paginated page numbers How many pages exist in the paginated database you want to scrape? Add them to the first column, giving each page its own row. We’ll use these page numbers in the next step to create dynamic URLs. 3 Step 3: Create pagination URLs using Clay formulas Next, so you don’t have to manually paste URLs into Clay, we’ll use a formula to add the page number to the database URL string automatically. Simply paste the URL of the database in the formula and insert the page number cell in the proper spot. Once finished, run the Zenrow data scrape column. 4 Step 4: Edit AI data cleaning prompt to fit your needs Next, to ensure we’re pulling usable data from often complex databases, use ChatGPT to clean the dataset. 5 Step 5: Write data to another table for further enrichment Last, write your newly scraped database data to a new table. Why? We want to get all the datapoints into their own columns. The only way to do that is to write to a new table. In the new table, you can use this data for anything, like further enrichment or for outbound messaging. If you don’t use Salesforce, replace this column with a lookup column for your CRM (e.g. Hubspot, Pipedrive, etc.). 4 Step 4: Write to second table Next, we’re going to move account contacts and additional column data to a second table to write and send personalized emails. In the last column, customize the contact and table data you want to move to the second table. 5 Step 5: Customize formulas and prompts Next, tailor any formulas or message prompts to fit your business needs. Promotion category (column 15, table 1): This formula labels accounts as either joint customers (us and our partner), high-intent Clay accounts who are customers of our partner, or high-intent partner accounts who are Clay customers Email subject line (column 14, table 2): The subject line of your outbound email Email body (column 15, table 2): The body content of the email, including conditional messaging 6 Step 6: Connect to Outreach (or other sequencer) Last, to push data to Outreach and send emails, connect the following columns in table 2: Lookup prospect (column 16): Find out if the contact exists in Outreach already Update prospect (column 18): Update the contact with email subject line and body fields Lookup mailbox (column 19): Find the reps mailbox who owns the account so you can send emails from the correct rep Add to sequence (column 21): Select the sequence in Outreach to add contacts and messages to Note: Don’t use Outreach? You can run the same workflow with a different sequencer like Salesloft, too. Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin Influencer marketing is one of the most effective ways to reach new audiences, but finding the right influencers, qualifying them, and reaching out at scale can be a challenge. This Claybook will walk you through a streamlined process using Clay, MoDash , and Twain to automate influencer discovery, enrichment, and outreach, saving you hours of manual work. What is MoDash? MoDash.io is a powerful influencer discovery and analytics platform that helps brands and marketers find the right influencers across YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok. With advanced filtering options such as audience demographics, engagement metrics, and credibility scores, MoDash makes it easy to identify influencers who align with your brand’s goals. It also provides enriched influencer data, including contact details and audience insights. How it works: Find influencers that match your criteria (e.g., platform, audience size, interests) Enrich influencer data with contact details and audience insights Filter and qualify influencers based on engagement and authenticity Automate outbound email sequences using Twain’s AI-powered messaging ‍ By the end, you’ll have a fully automated workflow to find, qualify, and contact influencers so you can focus on building relationships instead of manually researching profiles. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. ‍ If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. To do this, customize your search criteria from the list of available options, including: ‍ Social platform (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube) Bio key phrases Mentions Lookalike of a specific influencer Min. followers Max. followers Language Brands Audience location Audience age Advanced filters (e.g. credibility score, growth rate) ‍ 3 Step 3: Enrich influencers with emails and more Next, using the MoDash enrichment integration, enrich your newly imported influencers now. To do this, open the enrichment column and map the Profile URL column to the “Username / Profile Url / User ID” field. Then save and run. ‍ Enriched data includes: Email addresses Bio City/State Gender States User ID Audience age group LIkes/comments/hashtags Post count Recent posts Sponsored posts And more ‍ 4 Step 4: Adjust influencer qualification criteria Drawing from our enriched data, this table qualifies influencers for outbound email campaigns based on audience age group, influencer audience interests, and real audience weight (percentage of audience who are not bots). But you can customize your qualifying criteria to include any combination of datapoints from the table. ‍ 5 Step 5: Customize outbound messaging AI prompt Using Clay’s native integration with Twain, an AI outbound messaging tool that specializes in outbound sequences, this Claybook uses the influencers most recent posts (along with some other enriched data) to write a two-email outbound sequence with unique messaging for every influencer. Customize the Twain inputs and prompts to fit your business and needs. ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. ## https://university.clay.com/claybooks/how-connectwise-uses-clay-to-keep-their-account-database-clean

How ConnectWise uses Clay to keep their account database clean - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / How ConnectWise uses Clay to keep their account database clean How ConnectWise uses Clay to keep their account database clean See how ConnectWise keeps their account database updated with live website URLs, accurate headcount and addresses, and custom segmentation and account scoring Start building now with APIVoid Download the template What we used Clay ( Explorer ): to clean, segment, score, and tier accounts APIVoid (Paid): to check website status of accounts Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? I&#x27;m also personally available to help troubleshoot. You can send me, Jacob Tuwiner , a message on LinkedIn, or schedule a meeting with my Claygency, Sculpted , to learn how we can help. ‍ ‍ ‍ Get started ‍ Before we begin Keeping your account database clean is the foundation of any successful outbound strategy. But for teams like ConnectWise, it&#x27;s also a massive operational challenge. Dead domains: 10–20 % of CRM records point to sites that no longer resolve. Generic industry tags: Vendors lump SaaS and MSPs into one “IT” bucket—reps waste time disqualifying. Manual segmentation drag: 250 k site-checks by hand (or offshore) is slow, pricey, inaccurate. So our team at Sculpted helped ConnectWise build a smarter workflow with Clay that updates their database with live website URLs, up-to-date address and headcount, account segmentation, scoring and tiering. How it works: Intake / Normalization Cleans raw company names and domains (e.g., strips LLC/LTD, fixes casing) Website Status Check Pings domains (via APIVoid) to flag 404s, server errors, or redirects Address & Headcount Enrichment Pulls company location and employee count from LinkedIn (fallbacks to Claygent or Apify if blank) AI Segmentation Uses GPT-4o summaries and prompts to classify business type and market (e.g., SaaS vs Traditional, B2B vs B2C) Scoring & Tiering Weighs factors like URL health, LinkedIn presence, industry fit, and headcount to assign account scores and tiers ‍ Watch the guided demo (or scroll down for a step-by-step breakdown) to learn how to customize this workflow for your business. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Set up APIVoid HTTP API call to check website status First, connect to APIVoid via HTTP API in the first table. You’ll need your own APIVoid account (credits are dirt-cheap; one key covers 1M hits), along with the API key, for this step to work. 3 Step 3: Import records with names and domains Next, import records into the first table by filling out the first three columns: record ID (optional), company name, and company website domain. You can add records by typing them in yourself, uploading them via a CSV file , or automating it via a webhook . Once you insert records, manually run the “Normalize Domain” column to kickoff the rest of the table. We keep this column on manual so bulk imports don’t fire the whole workflow by accident. Note: Only working URLs designated by APIVoid will get sent to the second table for further enrichment (and credit usage). 4 Step 4: Customize AI segmentation (table 2) Next, in the second table, customize the account segmentation AI prompts (highlighted in gren). There’s two types of prompts: research prompts and decisions prompts. The research prompts find the company’s summary, its services, and target customers.The decision prompts use that information to segment accounts. In our example, we’re using ChatGPT to help us segment accounts in three ways: SaaS vs. Brick-and-mortar Managed service provider (MSP) vs. Managed security service provider (MSSP) B2B vs. B2C Customize both research and decision prompts to fit your industry and business. Once customized, run the “Enrich Companies” column. This action uses Clay credits, so we set it to manual so you don’t waste money on poor-fit accounts. Additionally, we added a conditional formula so LinkedIn enrichment runs only when industry category is relevant. 5 Step 5: Customize account scoring and tiering (table 2) Next, in the second table, customize the account scoring (0-100) and account tiering (1, 2, 3) criteria to fit your business (account scoring is a native feature in Clay). In our example, we’re weighing five criteria: URL health, LinkedIn presence, industry fit, country, and employees to surface scores and tiers. ‍ 6 Step 6: Update CRM (optional) Last, push updated and enriched data back to your CRM. Just add a Create/Update Object column for HubSpot or SFDC (or a different CRM), or just export to a CSV. To learn more about pushing data to your CRM, check out the Clay 101 lesson: Mastering CRM data exports. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ ‍ Get started Before we begin Identifying and utilizing intent and firmographic data for high-touch outreach is a significant challenge, as access to actionable, localized gifting data is often limited. Without clarity on which stakeholders are showing interest—and which gifts are actually available in their region—targeting becomes inefficient and physical mailers often go to waste. ‍ This Claybook resolves this issue by leveraging real-time intent signals and firmographic data to build a prioritized buying committee. When paired with Sendoso , it enables the automated selection of personalized, budget-compliant gift recommendations, empowering fast and effective high-touch campaigns that break through the noise. What is Sendoso? Sendoso is the leading platform for launching gifting and direct mail programs at scale, with the same ease as a digital campaign. We handle everything from sourcing and logistics to integrations with your GTM tech stack, so B2B teams can cut through digital fatigue and connect with buyers in more personal, thoughtful ways. With options across global a marketplace and AI-powered personalized gift recommendations, Sendoso is trusted by industry leaders like Gong, Verkada, and Meta, Sendoso helps GTM teams double win rates, drive 6x higher second-call rates, and close deals 29% faster. How it works: Build your target list using Clay’s native firmographic data to identify high-fit companies. Score and qualify each prospect by layering in real-time intent signals to prioritize accounts with the highest propensity to buy. Map prospect budget tiers to ensure every gift recommendation is automatically aligned with your ROI and spend limits per persona. Generate personalized gift recommendations for each prospect by querying the live Sendoso catalog based on their specific country and seniority. Trigger gift fulfillment directly from Clay, sending the order to your Sendoso account for final approval and shipping. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. To do this, customize your scoring criteria using these available options: ‍ Claygent to identify the number of physical locations each company has Chatgpt to identify the category of leadership each prospect belongs to Use Find active job openings action to see if the company is employing for related roles ‍ 4 Next, use a Formula Column or AI Column to assign a budget tier to each prospect based on their profile. This ensures your high-touch gifting is reserved for the highest-value opportunities. Customize your logic using criteria such as: Leadership category Number of physical locations they have Number of active job openings available ‍ 5 Next, use the Sendoso: Get Gift Recommendations action to automatically pull relevant gift ideas from their live catalog. Instantly enrich Intercom support tickets, directly in your chat thread, in real time - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Customer experience / Instantly enrich Intercom support tickets, directly in your chat thread, in real time Instantly enrich Intercom support tickets, directly in your chat thread, in real time Deliver better customer support by using Clay to enrich Intercom support tickets with custom contact and company data, in real time. Start building now with Intercom Download the template What we used Clay ( Explorer ) to enrich support tickets and access Intercoms API Intercom ( Advanced ) to manage support tickets and post enriched data Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin ‍ What’s one of the most common challenges support teams face every day? ‍ Identifying which person and company has opened a support ticket in the first place. ‍ At Clay, ten support specialists handle over 6,000 support tickets every month. By quickly identifying who’s on the other line (and their history with our product), we can make each response more relevant and helpful. ‍ So we created a system for it. ‍ Each time a ticket opens, an Intercom workflow triggers a webhook to Clay. In Clay, we: ‍ Enrich user data with our people/company information. Pull relevant data from Salesforce. Use the Intercom API to post this information as a note on the ticket. ‍ Why not just connect our CRM to Intercom? ‍ We do, but here’s two reasons why this works better: ‍ Coverage : Sometimes users reach out before creating a Clay account, so this method helps us recognize who they are even if they haven’t reached Salesforce. ‍ Visibility : Intercom sidebar data is overwhelming, so adding this info directly in the ticket keeps it front and center for our specialists. Plus, we can adjust the info to align with our goals. For example, we can see how many enrichments a customer has run in Clay which helps with activation goals. Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Create a webhook and workflow in Intercom Set up your webhook and workflow in Intercom so it can send data to Clay when new support tickets open. 3 Step 3: Set up your HTTP API call Next, so Clay can send enriched data back to Intercom in the form of notes, customize your HTTP API column with your Intercom API key and admin ID. To find your Intercom API key, follow the instructions here . To find your admin ID in Intercom: settings > workspace > teammates > click on the teammate you want > copy the ID at the end of the URL of the page. For example: intercom.com/a/apps/w14l1kwz/admins/ 1633147 (in this URL, “1633147” is the admin ID). 4 Step 4: Set up CRM Lookup Last, so Clay can check if someone exists in Salesforce (and pull information if they do), update both Salesforce lookup columns with your credentials. Using a different CRM? Replace lookups with your respective CRM by navigating to add enrichment > integrations > find your CRM > select contact or company lookup. ## https://university.clay.com/claybooks/monitor-and-act-on-linkedin-brand-mentions

Signals: Capture and activate brand mention signals, natively in Clay - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / Sales / Signals: Capture and activate brand mention signals, natively in Clay Signals: Capture and activate brand mention signals, natively in Clay How to automate LinkedIn brand mention monitoring in Clay Start building now with No items found. Download the template What we used Clay ( Free ): to import social posts from LinkedIn that mention your company name, and enrich people who comment Free resources Copy the free template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Before we begin Whether it’s a shoutout, a question, a critique, or a casual name-drop, every public mention is an opportunity to engage, qualify, or learn. But most companies let these signals slip by unnoticed, buried in the feed or locked inside a team member’s notifications. Missed opportunity. This is where brand mention signals come in. By automatically tracking and enriching mentions of your brand across LinkedIn posts, you can turn passive noise into actionable insight: Spot buyers in the wild without waiting for a form fill Route warm leads to sales or CS in real time Understand how people are framing and interpreting your product Prioritize advocates and influencers in your network Respond quickly to negative or confused mentions before they snowball In this Claybook, we’ll show you how to automate brand mention alerts using Clay’s out-of-the-box brand mention signals. It pulls in LinkedIn posts, enriches the data with author and sentiment info, writes to your contact table, and even sends alerts to Slack so your team never misses a moment that matters. How it works : Find and enrich posts: use "find social posts" to pull linkedin posts (e.g. mentioning “clay”) and enrich them with metadata (author, content, comment count) using "enrich social post". Extract core post data: create fields to extract key details like post text, url, creation date, and update time. Enrich author info: use "enrich person" to pull the author’s name, title, and organization from their linkedin profile. Analyze and classify content: use "clay category & sentiment" to assess sentiment and categorize the post’s mention of clay; extract those values into fields. Capture and route comments: use "get comments on a social post" and write those, along with the original post data, to the "all social post reactors" table. Notify via slack: send a message to a slack channel when a post about clay is detected, including author info, sentiment, category, and post link. Prioritize Outreach with Buying Intent Signals via Lusha - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other Roles index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Claybooks Role ​ Customer experience ​ Events ​ Marketing ​ Partnerships ​ RevOps ​ Sales ​ Other All claybooks / RevOps / Prioritize Outreach with Buying Intent Signals via Lusha Prioritize Outreach with Buying Intent Signals via Lusha Layer Lusha&#x27;s contact and company signal actions into any Clay workflow to reprioritize account lists, give reps a timely reason to reach out, and trigger sequences based on real buying momentum — not just firmographic fit. Start building now with Lusha Download the template What we used Clay (Paid): Powers the signal enrichment workflow — connects your people and company sources, runs Lusha&#x27;s signal actions across every row, applies scoring and filtering logic, and routes prioritized records to your sequencer or CRM. Lusha: Provides signal actions — that surface timely buying intent at both the contact and company level. Note that signal actions are charged on a per-result basis, so configuring your inputs carefully before running is important. ‍ Free resources Download the template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Most enrichment workflows treat every contact and account equally — but timing is everything in outbound. A perfectly enriched contact means little if there&#x27;s no trigger to act on. The signal is often already there; it&#x27;s just not being captured. This Claybook solves that by layering Lusha&#x27;s four signal actions into your existing Clay workflows. At the contact level, Find Person Signals detects promotions and company changes — two of the strongest indicators that a buyer&#x27;s priorities have shifted. At the company level, Find Company News surfaces funding rounds, acquisitions, and leadership changes, while Find Company Headcount Growth and Find Company Jobs Growth track hiring momentum by department over time. Together, they give you the context to reprioritize lists, score accounts dynamically, and trigger personalized outreach at exactly the right moment. ‍ HOW IT WORKS: Bring in your contact or account list from any Clay people or company source — a CRM export, a lookalike result, a Find People search, or any existing Clay table you want to reprioritize. Run Find Person Signals at the contact level to detect promotions and company changes for each contact, and use the results as run conditions to filter or trigger downstream steps. Run Find Company News Signal to surface funding rounds, acquisitions, and leadership changes at the account level — with article highlights, titles, event dates, and source URLs you can feed directly into AI columns for personalization. Run Find Company Jobs Growth Signal to track hiring surges by department, capturing historical averages, change rates, and new job postings from the last month to identify accounts in active growth mode. Run Find Company Website Traffic Signal to monitor web traffic trends at the account level. Score and reprioritize your list using a Formula or AI column that weighs signal recency and strength — then route high-signal accounts and contacts to your sequencer or rep queue for timely, context-rich outreach. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Copy this template First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Bring in your contact list Use any people or company source to populate your Clay table. Customize your input using any of the following sources: CRM export (HubSpot, Salesforce, or other) Lusha&#x27;s Find Company or People Lookalikes Clay&#x27;s native Find People or Find Companies action Any existing Clay table you want to reprioritize with signal data ‍ 3 Step 3: Run Find Person Signals Use the Lusha: Find Person Signals action to detect recent career activity for each contact in your table. Customize your enrichment using the following available inputs and outputs: LinkedIn URL or email as the contact identifier Monitoring date (how far back to look for signal activity) Promotion detected (boolean — use as a run condition to trigger downstream steps) Company change detected (boolean — use as a run condition to filter or re-route contacts) ‍ 4 Step 4: Run Find Company News Signals Use the Lusha: Find Company News Signals action to surface timely account-level events. Customize your signal capture using the following available inputs and outputs: Company domain or name as the identifier News topic filters (specify before running as this action charges per result) Article title and highlights (feed into AI columns for outreach personalization) Event effective date (use to filter for recency) Article URL (for rep context and source verification) ‍ 5 Step 5: Run Find Company Jobs Growth by Department Signal Use the Lusha: Find Company Jobs growth by department signal action to track hiring momentum by department. Customize your signal capture using the following available inputs and outputs: Company domain or name as the identifier Max departments to return (specify before running as this action charges per result) Department-level hiring surge indicator Historical average and change rate New job postings in the last month ‍ 6 Step 6: Run Find company website traffic signal Use the Lusha: Find Company Website Traffic Signal action to monitor web traffic trends at the account level. Customize your signal capture using the following available inputs and outputs: Company domain or name as the identifier Signal type selection (increase or decrease in traffic — choose based on whether you&#x27;re targeting growth or churn risk) Signal date (to filter for recency) Historical average visits ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . ‍ Get started Before we begin ‍ How does GoNimbly streamline multi-threading and next steps after sales calls? ‍ By automating the entire process using Gong, Hubspot, and Clay. ‍ This Claybook helps sales reps efficiently multi-thread by automatically capturing meeting attendees&#x27; emails, enriching their profiles, sending them directly to the CRM, and messaging them at the right time. ‍ Here’s how it works: ‍ Capture meeting attendees emails Enrich their profiles in Clay Send enriched contact data back to your CRM Receive Gong call summaries in Slack Automate multi-threaded outbound via Gong Flows Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 First, copy both templates in Clay: Gong HTTP/API Calls and enrichment If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. Then paste your Gong API token in the marked spot. Clay will store all calls within the timeframe—directly in the table. No data warehouse needed. This table uses the “Basic Authorization” HTTP header. You can also retrieve calls through Oauth using the Bearer token. Learn how to create both here: Gong API , retrieve call data . 3 Step 3: Set up “Write to other table” Next, send call data to your second table (Calls and enrichment) where we’ll pull in all details, enrich contacts, find emails, and draft quick, informed follow ups. 4 Step 4: Configure “Transcripts” HTTP/API To get transcripts for calls in the “Calls and enrichment” table, open the “Transcripts” column and paste your API token in the marked spot. Learn more about Gong’s “transcript” documentation here . To get detailed call data from Gong records, open the “Get call details” column and paste your API token in the marked spot. In order to change what call details you want to retrieve, edit the body (optional). Currently, the main call details include: brief, topics, parties on the call, outline, keywords tracked, highlights, and points of interest. Learn more about Gong’s “extensive” documentation here . 5 Step 5: Set up HubSpot lookups and add to Gong “Flow Next, add your HubSpot account so you can “lookup” contacts in your CRM and update or create a deal. This table repeats this step seven 7 times, so add your Hubspot account to each of the seven columns. If you don’t use HubSpot, you can delete these columns and replace them with your CRM. Last, add your enriched prospects to your Gong “Flow” (their version of an automated outbound sequence) for multi-threaded outreach. ## https://university.clay.com/claybooks/turn-closed-won-accounts-into-net-new-pipeline-with-lusha-lookalikes

Turn Closed-Won Accounts into Net-New Pipeline with Lusha Lookalikes - Claybooks Skip to main Review your year with Clay on Clayback.clay.com University home page Search University or ask AI. Start building now with Lusha Download the template What we used Clay (Paid): Powers the full lookalike workflow — runs Lusha&#x27;s table source actions to generate net-new rows, stacks enrichment actions at the company and contact level, applies ICP scoring logic, and routes qualified records to your CRM or sequencer. Lusha: Provides the Find Company Lookalikes and Find People Lookalikes source actions that surface net-new accounts and contacts matched to your best customers by firmographic profile, title, seniority, and company context. ‍ Free resources Download the template here Need help? If you have any issue, you can ask for help in Slack or schedule time with a Clay expert . Get started Finding net-new accounts and contacts that fit your ICP is one of the hardest parts of outbound — most teams either rely on static lists or manually hunt for companies that "feel similar" to their best customers. The signal is already in your CRM; it&#x27;s just not being used. This Claybook solves that by using Lusha&#x27;s Find Company Lookalikes and Find People Lookalikes — two table source actions that generate net-new rows from your seed inputs. Feed in 5–100 of your best customer domains or top-converting contacts&#x27; LinkedIn URLs or emails, and Lusha&#x27;s proprietary algorithm returns similar companies matched by firmographic profile, or similar people aligned by title, seniority, and company context. From there, Clay enriches the results, scores them against your ICP, and pushes them to your sequencer — or Clay&#x27;s own — for personalized outreach. ‍ How it works: Seed your lookalike search with 5–100 of your best customer domains (for account-level prospecting) or your top-converting contacts&#x27; LinkedIn URLs or emails (for people-level prospecting). Generate net-new lookalike rows using Lusha&#x27;s Find Company Lookalikes or Find People Lookalikes — both are table source actions, meaning they create new records matched by firmographic profile, title, seniority, and company context rather than enriching existing ones. Enrich the results by running Lusha&#x27;s Enrich Company or Enrich Person actions — or any other Clay enrichment provider — to layer in full firmographic and contact data on every returned record. Score each record against your ICP using a formula or AI column to rank accounts and contacts by fit — filtering out noise before anything hits your sequencer. Push to outreach by routing qualified accounts and contacts to your sequencer of choice — or directly into Clay&#x27;s built-in sequencer — for personalized, high-relevance campaigns. ‍ Information Follow the step by steps here in Clay Download the free template 1 Step 1: Copy this template First, copy this template in Clay. If you’re already a user, you’ll be directed to your workspace. If not, you’ll be prompted to create a free Clay account. The interactive demos on the right will walk you through each step of this Claybook. ‍ 2 Step 2: Seed your search and generate net-new lookalike rows Use the Lusha: Find Company Lookalikes or Lusha: Find People Lookalikes action as your table source, inputting your best customers and top-converting contacts as seeds to generate net-new rows. Customize your lookalike search using the following available inputs: Find Company Lookalikes: Seed company domains (minimum 5, maximum 100) Exclusion list (domains to exclude from results — use to filter out existing customers or previously contacted accounts) Max results to return per seed Find People Lookalikes: Seed LinkedIn URLs, professional profile URLs, or emails (minimum 5, maximum 100) Exclusion list (profiles or emails to exclude from results) Max results to return per seed ‍ 3 Step 3: Enrich the results Use Lusha: Enrich Company , Lusha: Enrich Person (both require API key) , or any other Clay enrichment provider to layer full firmographic and contact data onto every lookalike record returned. Customize your enrichment by mapping the following available identifiers: Enrich Company: Company domain Company name Returns: employee count, annual revenue, follower count, industry, and more Enrich Person: Professional Profile URL Email Full name and company domain Returns: verified email, direct dial, title, seniority, and more ‍ 4 Step 4: Score each record against your ICP Use a Formula Column or AI Column to assign a fit score to each returned record before anything moves to outreach. Customize your scoring logic using criteria such as: Industry or vertical Employee count or annual revenue range Seniority level or job title Geography or region Technology stack (e.g. CRM type from waterfall enrichment) Keywords from enriched firmographic data ‍ 5 Step 5: Find and enrich contacts at matched companies Use Clay&#x27;s Find People action to identify relevant contacts at your highest-scoring lookalike companies, then stack contact-level enrichments to fill in outreach details. Customize using the following available inputs: Company domain (pulled from enriched lookalike rows) Job title or function filter Seniority filter Find Work Email or Enrich Person to retrieve verified contact information ‍ 6 Step 6: Push to outreach Use the Clay&#x27;s built-in sequencer or any other sequencer to route qualified records into a personalized outreach campaign. Customize your outreach logic using the following available inputs: Recipient email First and last name Personalization fields drawn from enriched company or contact data Sequence or campaign assignment Filter conditions to ensure only records above your ICP score threshold are pushed Destination — CRM, third-party sequencer, or Clay&#x27;s native sequencer ‍ Other popular resources Experts Find a Clay Expert Explore our network of Clay experts and agencies. Day 01 Kickoff Day 02 Foundations of AI-Powered GTM Day 03 GTM Automation with AI Formulas Day 04 Prompting Masterclass Day 05 Limitless Research with Claygent Day 06 Graduation & Alumni Community FAQ Is it mandatory to join the Clay Slack community? ​ Yes! All cohort communication takes place in a private channel in the Clay Slack community. You must join the community before submitting a cohort application. What is the time commitment? ​ All cohorts run for 1 week. You should expect to set aside 3-4 hours each day to go through the content and build workflows. It is an intensive and involved learning experience so keep that in mind before you apply! How many live sessions take place during a cohort? ​ While the cohort is designed to help you learn at your own pace async, we offer several optiona l live sessions alongside to help you meet other learners, ask questions about the Cohort content, and dive deeper into GTM Engineering related topics outside of the immediate lessons! You can find all live sessions on the course calendar on Uplimit once you’re enrolled. Remember - these optional live sessions are offered to complement the async learning + peer-to-peer discussions happening on your private Cohort Slack. As you complete each assignment, you will get additional credits based on your performance. (*this does not apply to Clay Enterprise Cohort) This is done only once per workspace for the same cohort type in your lifetime – and will be issued automatically following the Kickoff call. Even if you have multiple users joining a cohort, the joining credits will remain the same. Please note that the joining credit does not expire for 1 year. If you’re seeing that your joining credits are gone, it’s likely that you or someone else in your workspace has already used them so please check before inquiring. ‍ When should I submit my cohort application after creating a new Clay account? ​ You must wait at least 24 hours after creating a new Clay account before submitting your cohort application. Do I need to be on a paid plan to join a cohort? Do I need to pay to enroll in a cohort? ​ Cohorts are free to join. For AI Skills Cohort, you can be on any plan to apply. For Enterprise Cohort, you must be on an enterprise plan to enroll. What do I get if I graduate from a cohort? ​ Graduation perks change from time to time. Currently, we provide access to our exclusive graduates community as well as additional credits that you earn along the way! Please Note: Clay reserves the right to change cohort perks without prior communication. The terms communicated during the cohort in the private channel are applicable. ‍ What should I know about credit expiration? ​ For free accounts, credits earned during a cohort will expire at the end of each month. Plan your cohort applications accordingly. For paid accounts, refer to the info on this page . What if I run out of credits during the cohort? ​ While additional credits aren&#x27;t normally offered for cohort purposes, you can open a support ticket to explain your case if you run out during your cohort. Please use this template for the support ticket. How can I switch to a different cohort? ​ To switch cohorts, submit the Cohort Application Update form . This can be done during a cohort or after it ends (if you haven&#x27;t graduated). How do I change my Clay Email or Workspace ID? ​ If you need to update the Clay Email or Clay Workspace ID you submitted in your application form, please contact Support ( support@clay.com ). Include both your original Email and Workspace ID, as well as the new ones you’d like to use. What should I expect after applying? ​ Cohorts are exclusive and submitting an application doesn&#x27;t guarantee acceptance.
