Now we&#x27;re doing a deep dive into custom signals, the secret weapon that truly helps you build GTM Alpha. While your competitors track the same default signals like job postings and funding announcements, custom signals let you monitor the unique data points that actually predict buying behavior in your specific market. 🎯 What Are Custom Signals? Custom signals are user-defined monitoring systems that track any data point relevant to your business, turning unique insights into automated buying signals. You can turn anything—any integration, any source in Clay—into a signal, as long as it&#x27;s digitally accessible. 🚀 Why Custom Signals Transform GTM Identify Opportunities Competitors Miss Custom signals let you spot opportunities competitors either completely overlook or have no structured way of monitoring at scale. While they rely on standard intent data everyone can buy, you&#x27;re detecting signals unique to your understanding of the market. Unlock industry-Specific Insights Monitor data points that only matter in your vertical—compliance certifications, regulatory changes, industry-specific events that generic signal providers would never track because they serve broad markets. Track Your Unique Buying Patterns Instead of relying on generic intent signals based on aggregate data, monitor the specific behaviors that predict purchases in your business based on your actual closed-won analysis and customer research. 📊 Categories of Custom Signals 1. Social Listening Signals X/Twitter : Monitor hashtag conversations, sentiment analysis around your category, and executive activity showing thought leadership or strategic focus. Reddit : Access subreddit discussions, pain point mentions in relevant communities, and product comparisons revealing consideration behavior. 2. First-Party Data Signals Turn your own operational data into buying signals by monitoring internal systems: Product Usage : Connect Snowflake or your data warehouse to track usage patterns, feature adoption rates, and engagement declines that predict churn or expansion. Gong Conversations : Analyze call topics, specific pain points mentioned repeatedly, and competitor mentions revealing consideration of alternatives. 3. Tech Stack Change Signals Track technology adoption and migration that creates immediate integration and replacement opportunities: New tool adoptions showing budget allocation and infrastructure investment Platform migrations like CRM changes creating tool evaluation cycles Competitor tool removals opening displacement opportunities Stack expansions when companies add entire new technology categories 4. Web Content Change Signals Monitor website updates that reveal strategic shifts and priorities: Homepage messaging changes showing repositioning Pricing page updates indicating market strategy shifts Team page additions when new executives join Product page feature additions revealing roadmap priorities Blog content themes showing strategic focus areas Case study publications indicating target market evolution 5. Compliance and Certification Signals Track regulatory and security achievements that often trigger related technology purchases: New security certifications like SOC2, ISO, or PCI compliance Compliance badges added to websites signaling achievement Regulatory filings revealing compliance investments Industry-specific accreditations opening new market opportunities 6. RSS Feed and News Monitoring Systematically track public announcements and news: Industry news publications for category-wide trends Regional news at county level for local businesses (construction, real estate) Regulatory announcements affecting your target market Patent filings showing innovation investment Conference announcements revealing industry participation Press releases about partnerships, products, or expansions 7. Unique Industry Signals These are vertical-specific signals that only make sense in your context. Here are some examples: Trucking Safety : One customer tracks truck incidents like jackknifes across the US on an hourly basis, using real-time data to immediately reach out to companies needing safety solutions right after incidents occur. Warehouse Staffing : Another customer discovered their number one predictive data point was "how many parking spaces a warehouse has"—which correlates directly with staffing needs and facility size. These create un-replicable competitive advantages because they&#x27;re based on deep domain expertise competitors don&#x27;t have. 🛠️ Building Custom Signals Step 1: Identify Your Signal Opportunity Ask your sales and customer success teams four key questions that reveal what actually predicts buying: What data points do you manually research before outreach? What changes at accounts trigger buying conversations? What patterns do you see consistently in closed-won deals? What information makes you say "we should reach out now"? Signal Validation Checklist Before building a custom signal, validate the opportunity: Is this data publicly available or in our systems? Does this change frequently enough to be actionable? Does this correlate with buying intent or churn risk? Can we act on this signal within 24-48 hours? Is this unique to our business and not tracked by competitors? If you answer yes to all five, you&#x27;ve identified a strong custom signal candidate. Step 2: Choose Your Data Source Select the right technical approach based on your data type and structure: Web Scraping with Claygent : Best for website content, public data, and unstructured information that requires interpretation. API Integrations : Optimal for structured data from platforms like HG Insights, TrustRadius, or any service with documented APIs. RSS Feeds : Perfect for news, blogs, regulatory filings, and press releases that publish via standard feeds. First-Party Data : Connect your Snowflake or data warehouse (Enterprise plans) for product usage, engagement metrics, and support data. Social Listening : Use native Clay integrations for brand mentions, competitor discussions, and sentiment analysis across social platforms. Progress Intro to Inbound Automation ✔ 1 Intro to Inbound Automation Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow ✔ 2 Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow Connecting Inbound Lead Sources ✔ 3 Connecting Inbound Lead Sources Your Inbound Enrichment Stack ✔ 4 Your Inbound Enrichment Stack Transforming Data for Inbound ✔ 5 Transforming Data for Inbound Lead Scoring for Inbound ✔ 6 Lead Scoring for Inbound Lead Routing ✔ 7 Lead Routing Personalized Messaging for Inbound ✔ 8 Personalized Messaging for Inbound Deep Dive: Web Intent ✔ 9 Deep Dive: Web Intent Responding to Inbound Leads (Exporting Data) ✔ 9 Responding to Inbound Leads (Exporting Data) Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Automated Inbound / Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow Lesson 2 / 9 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow ⚒️ Building End-to-End Inbound Workflows: The Complete Revenue Engine We&#x27;re diving into a real-world example of how Clay allows you to build a powerful inbound engine that transforms form submissions into qualified, enriched leads ready for your sales team. We&#x27;ll walk through a high-level overview of an end-to-end inbound workflow and then discuss how to reverse-engineer it so you can see the big picture. Don&#x27;t worry if this seems overwhelming right now. In each lesson of this course, we&#x27;ll go over every step of this workflow in detail. ✍🏻 Example Workflow: First, an inbound lead comes in via Typeform - in this form, the lead just has to fill in their name and email address These leads are then sent to a table via Webhook in Clay - we’ll cover over how to set this up in detail in our next lesson Next, we begin filling in the missing data. The first enrichment fills in those corner pieces, scraping using those identifiers we collected (lead name and email) to find information like company domain that we can use to unlock more enrichments Then, we go deep, finding relevant firmographic data that might help us determine whether a lead is a good fit - data points like employee headcount across departments, tech stack, company description, funding stage — all the stuff you’d usually have to Google As another key part of determining fit and lead scoring, we then enrich the contacts with data (title, past experiences, time at the company) All that enriched data is cleaned and normalized for use Based on all this helpful data, the leads are scored based on custom criteria If they pass the bar, personalized AI copy is generated based on data we’ve already collected Using our native lead routing capability, leads are routed to the correct AEs with custom weightings Lastly, data is exported out to the CRM or directly to your sequencing tools. fully enriched and ready to go 💭 Key Takeaways You don’t need to collect tons of first-party data from leads with long forms anymore - Clay helps you fill in the gaps and go the extra mile to find any information imaginable. While the possibilities are endless, the key is learning how to think backwards and reverse engineer what data you actually need. In inbound, the ultimate objective is fairly straightforward: reach your best fit leads as soon as possible. Speed to lead is the top priority and layering on personalization is the cherry on top that helps you further stand out from the crowd. 🧠 Computational Thinking with an Inbound Lens To build more intelligent inbound workflows, apply a computational thinking approach to systematize your logic. First, decompose the problem. What qualifies whether this inbound lead is a good prospect for your software? Is it the size of the company, its growth rate, the industry it’s in, technology adoption patterns? Then, you look for patterns. What trends have you seen in your customer and conversion data? Maybe marketing leaders at enterprise-size companies operating across multiple regions are your ideal buyer personas. Perhaps fast-growing SaaS startups with remote teams are three times more likely to choose your platform. Next, you synthesize these insights into reusable logic. Your goal is to create a dynamic process that can run automatically and improve over time. Your inbound workflow becomes a systematic approach to identifying and qualifying inbound prospects flowing in from any channel at scale. This is computational thinking applied to inbound. You&#x27;re not just collecting data on inbound leads but building an intelligent system that allows you to get to every lead faster with the most relevant, timely context. 🔜 What&#x27;s Next You’ve now seen how Clay transforms scattered lead generation activities into a cohesive revenue engine. This end-to-end approach forms the foundation for building sophisticated inbound engines that consistently deliver qualified prospects to your sales team. In our next lesson, we&#x27;ll begin constructing this workflow step by step, starting with connecting your lead sources and establishing the data foundation that makes everything else possible. Remember, the key to effective inbound automation is not just in the individual pieces, but in how you orchestrate it all together within your Clay workspace. Happy building, and here&#x27;s to transforming your manual inbound process into a deal-closing machine! Progress Intro to CRM Enrichment ✔ 1 Intro to CRM Enrichment Importing from your CRM ✔ 2 Importing from your CRM Clay x HubSpot Actions ✔ 3 Clay x HubSpot Actions Clay x Salesforce Actions ✔ 4 Clay x Salesforce Actions Enriching your CRM Data ✔ 5 Enriching your CRM Data Keeping your CRM data fresh ✔ 6 Keeping your CRM data fresh Taking action on enriched CRM data ✔ 7 Taking action on enriched CRM data Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / CRM Enrichment / Clay x HubSpot Actions Lesson 3 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Clay x HubSpot Actions Introduction In our previous lesson, we covered the technical foundations of CRM enrichment: connecting Clay to HubSpot and Salesforce, importing your contacts, and setting up proper field architecture. Now we&#x27;re diving into Clay&#x27;s HubSpot actions, which are the core building blocks for actually working with your HubSpot data inside Clay. This lesson focuses specifically on HubSpot actions. In the next lesson, we&#x27;ll cover Salesforce-specific actions, so feel free to focus on whichever CRM your team uses. 📚 Understanding HubSpot Actions Read-Only vs. Write Operations First, you have Lookup actions. These pull data FROM HubSpot INTO Clay without changing anything in your CRM. Think of these as read-only operations—you&#x27;re simply viewing and importing existing data for analysis or enrichment purposes. Your HubSpot database remains completely unchanged regardless of how many times you run these actions. With Lookup actions, you can experiment freely—there&#x27;s no risk of damaging your CRM data or disrupting your sales team&#x27;s workflow. You can run tests, try different queries, and iterate on your approach without any consequences to your production data. Then you have Create and Update actions. These push data FROM Clay TO HubSpot and actually modify your CRM records. These are write operations that make real, permanent changes to your database that affect every user in your organization. With Create and Update actions, you need to be more careful and methodical. These actions have real business consequences because they modify data that your entire revenue team relies on for their daily operations. Think of it this way: Lookup is like reading a book—you&#x27;re not changing the content, just consuming information. Update and Create are like editing the book or adding new pages—you&#x27;re making permanent changes that affect everyone who reads it afterward. 🔍 Lookup Actions Primary Use Cases Contact and Company Lookup allows you to pull existing contact records, company profiles, and all their associated data into Clay for further enrichment or analysis. This creates a foundation layer of existing CRM data that you can then enhance with external sources. Duplicate Checking represents another powerful use case that prevents CRM pollution. Before creating new records, you can lookup existing contacts by email or company domain to avoid creating duplicates in your CRM. This proactive approach maintains data hygiene and prevents the confusion that comes from multiple records for the same prospect. Data Verification allows you to cross-reference information between Clay and HubSpot to identify inconsistencies or outdated records that need attention. You might discover that contact job titles in HubSpot don&#x27;t match current LinkedIn information, creating opportunities for targeted updates. ✏️ Create and Update Actions These actions are where Clay becomes truly powerful for CRM enrichment, but they also require careful planning and execution because they make permanent changes to your HubSpot database. Create Actions Create actions let you add completely new contacts, companies, or deals to HubSpot directly from Clay. This capability is perfect for adding enriched prospects from your outbound research, importing leads from external sources, or creating records for companies discovered through signal monitoring. The key with Create actions is ensuring you&#x27;re not accidentally creating duplicate records. This requires combining Create actions with Lookup actions to check for existing records before attempting to create new ones. Update Actions Update actions modify existing HubSpot records with new data from Clay. You might update contact records with enriched job titles, add company funding information, append research notes, or populate custom fields with insights gathered from external sources. ⚙️ Setting Up Conditional Logic for Updates When setting up Update actions, you must specify conditions for when the update should run. This prevents accidental overwrites and ensures you&#x27;re only updating records when it makes strategic sense. Common Conditional Patterns Consider implementing conditions like: Empty Fields : Only update if the current field is empty. This prevents overwriting existing, potentially valuable data with automated enrichment. Recency Validation : Only update if the new data is more recent than existing information. This ensures you&#x27;re not replacing fresh data with stale information. Confidence Thresholds : Only update if the confidence score or data quality meets a certain threshold. This prevents low-quality enrichment from polluting your CRM. Source Prioritization : Only update if the new data comes from a higher-priority source than the existing information. This creates a hierarchy of data quality that protects your most reliable information. Without proper conditions, you could accidentally overwrite good data with incomplete or outdated information, creating more problems than you solve. Create Action 101 For Create actions, you want to use conditional formulas to only create new records if nothing was found during your Lookup phase. This prevents duplicate creation while ensuring you capture all net-new prospects from your enrichment workflows. 🧪 Safe Experimentation Practices Here&#x27;s a best practice that will save you significant headaches during development: turn off auto-update when you&#x27;re experimenting with Create or Update workflows. Instead of automatic execution, you can manually trigger updates on small batches of records once you&#x27;ve verified everything looks correct in Clay. This allows you to review the intended changes, spot potential issues, and make corrections before they affect your production CRM data. Once you&#x27;re confident in your workflow and have tested it thoroughly on small datasets, you can re-enable auto-update for seamless automation. 🔄 Combining Actions for Powerful Workflows As you start building more sophisticated enrichment systems, you&#x27;ll often combine these actions into comprehensive workflows that handle the complete enrichment lifecycle. Progress Intro to CRM Enrichment ✔ 1 Intro to CRM Enrichment Importing from your CRM ✔ 2 Importing from your CRM Clay x HubSpot Actions ✔ 3 Clay x HubSpot Actions Clay x Salesforce Actions ✔ 4 Clay x Salesforce Actions Enriching your CRM Data ✔ 5 Enriching your CRM Data Keeping your CRM data fresh ✔ 6 Keeping your CRM data fresh Taking action on enriched CRM data ✔ 7 Taking action on enriched CRM data Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / CRM Enrichment / Clay x Salesforce Actions Lesson 4 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Clay x Salesforce Actions Introduction In our previous lesson, we covered Clay HubSpot Actions. Now we&#x27;re diving into Clay SFDC Actions, where we&#x27;ll explore Salesforce-specific functionality. While some actions are quite similar to HubSpot, Salesforce has unique features and quirks that require a slightly different approach. Most importantly, we&#x27;ll show you how to work safely with sandbox environments so you can test everything before deploying to your production Salesforce instance. 🧪 Safe Testing with Sandbox Environments When starting out, always use a Salesforce sandbox environment when testing Clay actions. This is perhaps the most important best practice for any Salesforce automation work. Think of a sandbox like a practice room for musicians. You wouldn&#x27;t perform a complex piece in front of an audience without rehearsing it first. Similarly, you don&#x27;t want to test Clay automations directly in your production Salesforce instance where real customer data lives and active sales processes depend on data integrity. Setting Up Your Sandbox Connection Here&#x27;s how to establish your safe testing environment: Navigate to Settings in Clay, then go to Connections and look for the Salesforce test environment option. Connect your sandbox instance using the same authentication process you used for your production environment. This creates a completely separate connection that mirrors your production setup without affecting live data. Once you&#x27;ve validated everything works correctly in sandbox, you can confidently deploy to production. 🔍 Understanding Salesforce Data Visibility Once you&#x27;ve imported your Salesforce data into Clay, you might notice something unexpected compared to HubSpot. All your Salesforce objects don&#x27;t automatically show up in the cell details view. This difference stems from Salesforce&#x27;s more complex data architecture and permission system. To see complete record information, you need to explicitly lookup your records using the CRM ID as an identifier. This tells Clay to fetch the full record details from Salesforce rather than just displaying the imported fields. The Lookup and Display Process Here&#x27;s the step-by-step process to access complete Salesforce data: Add a new enrichment column and select Salesforce Lookup. Use your CRM ID column as the identifier and run the lookup to populate full record details. This additional step fetches all available fields and related data for each record. To display specific Salesforce objects in your Clay table as separate columns, click on the data point you want to display in the cell details, then select "Add as column." This creates a new column with that specific field, giving you granular control over your data presentation. ⚙️ Core Salesforce Actions The core Salesforce actions in Clay operate on similar principles to HubSpot, but with important differences that reflect Salesforce&#x27;s enterprise architecture. Lookup and Create/Update functions work on the same fundamental principles you learned in the HubSpot lesson. You&#x27;re either retrieving existing records for analysis or creating new records and updating existing ones with enriched data. Upsert Salesforce includes a special action called Upsert that&#x27;s essentially a combination of Create and Update in one intelligent operation. This is one of Salesforce&#x27;s most powerful features for data management. Here&#x27;s how it works: If a record with the specified external ID exists, Salesforce updates it with your new data. If no record exists with that external ID, Salesforce creates a new record automatically. This dual functionality requires you to have an external ID field configured in your Salesforce setup, but it eliminates the need for separate existence checking and conditional logic. 📊 Advanced Data Retrieval with SOQL For more complex data relationships and enterprise-level automation, you can retrieve exactly what you need using SOQL (Salesforce Object Query Language). This is Salesforce&#x27;s specialized data retrieval language designed for complex enterprise data structures. SOQL becomes especially valuable when you&#x27;re dealing with one-to-many relationships that are common in enterprise sales processes: Finding all opportunities associated with a specific account to understand deal pipeline Retrieving all activities related to a contact to understand engagement history Pulling custom object data that relates to standard Salesforce objects This SOQL query pulls account records and their related opportunities/activities for multiple domains at once to help identify which account should be the "primary" when duplicates exist. If SOQL syntax seems daunting, Claude is excellent at generating these queries for you. Instead of learning SOQL syntax from scratch, you can describe what you want to retrieve in plain English, and Claude will generate the proper SOQL query with correct syntax and best practices. This approach allows you to leverage Salesforce&#x27;s powerful querying capabilities without becoming a SOQL expert, making enterprise-level automation accessible to revenue operations professionals. 🔄 Lead Conversion Automation Another one of Salesforce&#x27;s unique features is the Convert Lead action, which automates a fundamental part of the Salesforce lead management process. This action converts a lead record into the standard Salesforce account and contact structure. When you run Convert Lead through Clay, several things happen automatically: The lead record gets converted to a contact with all relevant information transferred. A new account gets created (or the contact gets associated with an existing account if there&#x27;s a match). Optionally, an opportunity record gets created if there&#x27;s a potential deal identified during the conversion process. This automation is particularly valuable for inbound workflows where you want to move qualified leads from your lead queue into your standard account and contact structure without manual intervention. It maintains data consistency while enabling automated lead processing at scale. 🎯 Understanding Salesforce Object Relationships Understanding the difference between Leads and Contacts in Salesforce is crucial for effective Clay automation because it affects how you structure your workflows and data management strat

Progress Intro to Signals in Clay ✔ 1 Intro to Signals in Clay Types of Signals in Clay ✔ 2 Types of Signals in Clay Setting Up Signals in Clay ✔ 3 Setting Up Signals in Clay Building Custom Signals in Clay ✔ 4 Building Custom Signals in Clay Advanced Strategies with Signals ✔ 5 Advanced Strategies with Signals ClayBM: ABM in Clay ✔ 6 ClayBM: ABM in Clay ABM and Ad Intelligence in Clay ✔ 7 ABM and Ad Intelligence in Clay Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Signals & ABM / ClayBM: ABM in Clay Lesson 6 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 ClayBM: ABM in Clay Introduction to ABM in Clay Today, we&#x27;re diving into Account-Based Marketing (ABM) in Clay—where we take everything you&#x27;ve learned about signals and audiences and apply it to your most valuable accounts. This is where Clay really shines: helping you deeply penetrate high-value accounts with precision targeting and real-time intelligence. ABM isn&#x27;t just another prospecting strategy but a fundamental shift in how you approach your market. 🐟 What Makes ABM Different Account-Based Marketing is fundamentally about precision over volume. Instead of casting a wide net hoping to catch anything, ABM is like spear fishing. You identify which fish you want, study their behavior, and strike with precision. This means targeting 100 to 2,000 accounts maximum, with a few thousand total contacts per year. Compare that to traditional prospecting where you might contact thousands of prospects daily. For high-value accounts, generic messaging doesn&#x27;t just fail—it actively damages relationships before they even begin. 🧠 Clay as Your ABM Central Nervous System Clay serves as the unified data layer that makes modern ABM possible. Think of it as the central nervous system connecting your first-party data, enrichment providers, intent signals, and CRM. It&#x27;s where all your account intelligence comes together in one place. Modern ABM requires accurate, real-time data at two levels: At the company level, you need to understand how priorities are shifting. Is the company expanding? Did they raise funding? Are they posting jobs that signal new initiatives? These signals tell you when accounts are ready to engage. At the people level, you need to identify the right person to reach at the right moment. Did someone new join the buying committee? Did your champion move roles? Understanding personnel changes prevents outreach from falling into a black hole. 🔄 The Unified ABM Motion The ABM motion in Clay ties together demand generation, sales development, expansion, and customer success. Instead of operating in silos, ABM creates a unified approach to penetrate your most valuable prospects. You start with real-time data monitoring—tracking job changes, company news, and intent signals. Then you progress accounts through defined stages based on engagement. You orchestrate multi-channel touchpoints including ads, events, personalized content, and direct outreach. Finally, you maintain human-in-the-loop execution where ops teams continuously improve automation based on results. 📊 The Three Core ABM Stages Understanding how accounts move through your ABM funnel is critical. Each stage requires different data, messaging, and tactics. Stage 1: Aware Accounts enter through social media connections, social engagement, website visits, event attendance, or investor introductions. At this stage, they know you exist but haven&#x27;t shown meaningful interest yet. Your tactics include social media auto-connect sequences, paid advertising, personalized landing pages, warm introductions, and event invitations. The goal is building awareness and establishing initial relationships. Stage 2: Interested Accounts move here when they create a workspace, visit pricing pages, send positive replies, or attend high-intent events. This is where curiosity transforms into genuine interest. Tactics shift to retargeting ads, signal-based outbound sequences, webinars, and case studies. You&#x27;re now nurturing active interest and demonstrating value specific to their situation. Stage 3: Evaluating This stage is triggered by contact sales form submissions or discovery meetings. The account is actively considering whether to buy, and every interaction matters. Tactics become executive dinners, referrals, multi-threading across the organization, and pre-call research briefs. You&#x27;re removing friction and building conviction across multiple stakeholders. 🤝 Converting Accounts to Aware Stage Systematic relationship building is key to getting accounts into your ABM motion. For events and dinners, filter your target list by location and contact grade, then auto-send invites to relevant events. Geography-based targeting ensures you can meet prospects face-to-face when they&#x27;re ready. For warm introductions, upload your executives&#x27; social media connections, cross-reference with target accounts, and identify mutual connections who can make introductions. Warm intros convert at dramatically higher rates than cold outreach. Social media auto-connect works well when triggered by engagement. Set up workflows that send connection requests when prospects engage with content or visit landing pages—they&#x27;re already showing interest. Clay excels at social listening. Monitor relevant keywords and get alerts when prospects post about topics related to your solution. This gives you perfect conversation starters grounded in their actual priorities. 💡 Moving Accounts to Interested Stage Moving accounts from aware to interested requires deeper intelligence and personalization. Use Claygent to scrape company websites, recent news, and SEC filings to identify their top three business and technology priorities. Then create personalized landing pages that reference these specific priorities. Generic messaging won&#x27;t cut it at this stage. Track product signals if they&#x27;re using your product. Monitor feature usage and trigger personalized help offers when they hit milestones. This positions you as helpful rather than pushy. Web intent tracking becomes critical. Monitor not just page visits, but time on site and multiple visits that indicate growing interest. Someone spending 8 minutes on your pricing page is telling you something important. 🎯 Deploying High-Touch Tactics in Evaluating Stage The evaluating stage is where you deploy your highest-touch tactics to close deals. Auto-generate pre-call research briefs that include company summaries, recent funding information, potential partnership ideas, and relevant news. This arms your sales team with conversation starters that demonstrate you&#x27;ve done your homework. First impressions matter enormously at this stage. Multi-threading becomes essential. Use conversation intelligence tools like Gong to identify stakeholders mentioned in calls, then reach both economic buyers and end users. Single

this lesson also appears in Clay 101, Limitless Research, and CRM Enrichment, so feel free to skim or skip if you&#x27;ve already seen it somewhere else ‍ Now that you&#x27;re a prompting expert, it&#x27;s time to dive into Clay&#x27;s most powerful AI integration - Claygent. At it&#x27;s core, Claygent is an AI based web scraper perfectly designed for retrieving unstructured data in non-repeatable locations (think staff/people pages on various company websites as an example). ‍ 🌐 Understanding Claygent: Your All-Knowing Digital Assistant Imagine having a tireless, incredibly knowledgeable assistant at your fingertips, ready to scour the web for any information you need. That&#x27;s Claygent in a nutshell. It&#x27;s designed to access and retrieve virtually any publicly available data point on the internet, with the exception of information hidden behind paywalls or password-protected areas. What makes Claygent truly unique is its ability to harness both the vast expanse of web data and the analytical power of AI. However, it&#x27;s important to remember that while Claygent has access to an enormous amount of information, its effectiveness relies heavily on the context and instructions you provide. Mastering the art of prompting is key to unlocking Claygent&#x27;s full potential. Selecting Claygent from the Enrichment Panel ‍ 🚀 Getting Started with Claygent To begin your Claygent journey, navigate to the enrichment panel in your Clay workspace and look for the Tools section. Under AI, you&#x27;ll find Claygent among other powerful options. We&#x27;ve made it easy to hit the ground running by providing a library of preset templates for common tasks. These templates are an excellent starting point, especially if you&#x27;re new to working with AI agents. For instance, if you need to locate a company&#x27;s 10K report, you can simply input the company name from your table, and our pre-written prompt will guide Claygent in finding the relevant URL. This template approach not only saves time but also helps you understand how to structure effective prompts for various tasks. Using Claygent to find Company 10-Ks and Extract Information from them 🧠 Choosing the Right Model: Neon, GPT-4, or Claude When using Claygent, you have the flexibility to choose from different AI models, each with its strengths: Claygent Neon: Our flagship model, specially designed for agent tasks. While it may not have the same level of reasoning capabilities as some other models, it excels in answer formatting and data extraction. Neon allows you to format results into multiple columns or outputs, making it incredibly powerful for extracting various data points from a single Claygent run. GPT-4 and Claude Opus: These models offer enhanced reasoning capabilities. While they don&#x27;t provide the same level of answer formatting as Neon, they can be useful for testing data accuracy or handling more complex analytical tasks. Selecting the right model is more of an art than a science, and we encourage you to experiment to find the best fit for your specific needs. 🔮 The Future of AI-Powered Research Claygent represents a significant leap forward in how we approach data gathering and analysis. By combining the vast resources of the web with the intelligence of AI, we&#x27;re opening up new possibilities for personalization, research, and outreach. We&#x27;re thrilled to see how you will leverage Claygent in creative and exciting ways. Whether you&#x27;re in sales, marketing, research, or any field that requires deep, personalized insights, Claygent is poised to become an indispensable tool in your arsenal. As we continue to refine and expand Claygent&#x27;s capabilities, we encourage you to explore, experiment, and push the boundaries of what&#x27;s possible. The future of AI-powered research is here, and it&#x27;s more accessible than ever before. Setting up Clay in ChatGPT ✔ 2 Setting up Clay in ChatGPT Best practices for Clay in ChatGPT ✔ 3 Best practices for Clay in ChatGPT Finding & Enriching Contacts in ChatGPT ✔ 4 Finding & Enriching Contacts in ChatGPT Company Research in ChatGPT ✔ 5 Company Research in ChatGPT Outreach in ChatGPT ✔ 6 Outreach in ChatGPT An SDR Workflow in ChatGPT ✔ 7 An SDR Workflow in ChatGPT An Account Planning Workflow in ChatGPT ✔ 8 An Account Planning Workflow in ChatGPT Creating Your Own Use Cases in ChatGPT with AI ✔ 9 Creating Your Own Use Cases in ChatGPT with AI Troubleshooting Clay in ChatGPT ✔ 10 Troubleshooting Clay in ChatGPT Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Clay in ChatGPT / Company Research in ChatGPT Lesson 5 / 10 Next lesson Company Research in ChatGPT Before we jump into the different research capabilities, let&#x27;s review some best practices that will help you get cleaner, more accurate results every time. ✅ Best Practices for Company Research Following these two simple practices will dramatically improve the quality of your research results: 1️⃣ Use the company&#x27;s domain instead of just the company name. Instead of typing "Stripe," use " stripe.com ." This ensures Clay pulls the correct company data without any ambiguity. 2️⃣ Do one company at a time. Don&#x27;t research multiple companies in the same chat. If you need to research a new company, start a fresh chat. This keeps your context clean and your results focused. There are exceptions to this rule, and we&#x27;ll show you one below where comparing companies makes sense. 🥊 Use Case: Competitive Research When you need to understand how two competitors stack up against each other, you can research them together in the same chat. Here&#x27;s an example prompt: @Clay research and compare the hiring trends of OpenAI.com and Anthropic.com ; summarize what they&#x27;re focused on comparatively. This type of comparative analysis helps you understand where competitors are investing, what roles they&#x27;re prioritizing, and how their strategic focus differs. Instead of researching each company separately and manually comparing notes, Clay pulls the data and synthesizes the comparison for you. 🎯 Use Case: Multi-Dimensional Analysis Sometimes you need a comprehensive view of a single company across multiple dimensions - hiring, technology, and product strategy all at once. Here&#x27;s how to request that: @Clay please research Notion.com &#x27;s overall hiring trends, tech stack, and any new product announcements This gives you a holistic picture of what&#x27;s happening at the company. You&#x27;ll see where they&#x27;re hiring (indicating growth areas), what technologies they&#x27;re using (revealing their technical infrastructure), and what new products they&#x27;re launching (showing strategic direction). All of this intelligence in one consolidated research request. 📄 Use Case: Using Claygent for Deep Research For the most sophisticated research - like analyzing SEC filings or other complex documents - you can leverage Claygent directly from ChatGPT. Here&#x27;s an example: @Clay use Claygent to review Intuit.com &#x27;s latest 10-K and summarize priorities, leadership changes, and headcount trends Claygent will actually review the company&#x27;s 10-K filing and extract the specific insights you&#x27;re looking for. This saves you from manually reading through hundreds of pages of financial documents to find the strategic signals that matter for your sales or research process. 🎬 What&#x27;s Next That&#x27;s it for company research using Clay in ChatGPT. Next, we&#x27;ll look at how you can even do outreach work directly in ChatGPT, taking your workflow from research all the way through to prospect communication. Leads can trickle in from anywhere. Website visitors, chatbots, webinars, newsletter signups, even Linkedin DMs. Inbound leads are some of your highest-intent signals so it’s crucial to engage quickly. In this lesson, we’ll cover some of the most common inbound lead automations our customers use. Keep in mind that your approach might vary slightly based on your inbound lead sources. 📄 🧺 Collecting leads from Typeform Typeform is a popular tool for capturing inbound leads. Forms can be easily embedded in websites, newsletters, or surfaced on social media. Clay has a native integration that allows you to import directly from Typeform when creating a new table. All you do is go to “Import” under the Actions tab, click on “Import Typeform form responses,” link up with your org’s Typeform account, and the table will automatically populate with Typeform responses as they come in. 🔗 Introduction to Webhooks While Clay is natively integrated with platforms like Typeform, we know that leads can come in from anywhere and we want to make sure you can capture all of them. That’s where Webhooks come in. You can think of them as little messengers that can seamlessly transmit info from one source to another, in real time. To get started in Clay, select “Import” then “Pull in data from a Webhook.” Copy the Webhook URL and then go over to the tool you’re looking to collect inbound leads from. There, you can add a new Webhook and paste the Clay URL. This will instantly send data from that source to the Clay table. Webhooks open up nearly limitless possibilities for collecting and consolidating inbound leads. For example, if you’re running Zoom webinars, you could set up a webhook to automatically send attendee or registrant data into Clay as soon as someone signs up instead of manually exporting and importing CSVs. Webhooks are also perfect for capturing high-intent signals like trial signups. Multiple signups coming from the same company could indicate strong team interest that’s definitely worth acting on quickly. Do note that Webhook sources are limited to 50,000 submissions; you’ll need to create new tables if you’d like to process more. 🌊 Opening the Data Floodgates To spark your creativity, here are a few more examples of sources that Clay users link up: Conversations via Intercom, Zendesk, or Drift chats: We feed all our support tickets from Intercom into Clay tables to help us analyze responses with AI, improve our documentation, and suggest new docs to be created Content Engagement: You can capture new blog subscribers or track website interactions like downloading a whitepaper or clicking on certain CTAs (Segment Session Integration) Many companies are used to sending inbound signals directly into their CRM. However, routing signals straight into your CRM first can actually compromise your speed-to-lead due to synchronization delays and processing bottlenecks. By bringing signals into Clay first, you can instantly enrich lead data, prioritize, and decide what truly belongs in your CRM - ensuring faster, more targeted outreach. Inbound is a huge web of signals. Clay lets you weave together all those threads into one intelligent, actionable system. 🤔 What’s next? By establishing these lead source connections, you&#x27;re creating the critical foundation that enables everything else in your inbound automation system. This real-time data transfer is just scratching the surface of what Clay can do for inbound automation. In our upcoming lessons, we&#x27;ll explore how to leverage Clay&#x27;s powerful enrichment capabilities to instantly gather deep company and contact data, implement intelligent scoring mechanisms that prioritize your highest-value prospects, and build sophisticated routing systems that ensure every lead receives the context-rich attention they deserve as quickly as possible. Effective inbound automation starts with reliable data capture but its true power emerges when you strategically enrich and efficiently act on that information. You&#x27;ve now laid the groundwork for building an inbound engine that consistently delivers qualified, well-researched prospects to your sales team. Happy importing! About this lesson 00:00 Create: AI-Driven Effortless Output We just wrapped up the Transform section of this AI-Powered GTM course, where you learned how to use AI to clean, structure, and prepare your data for action. Now let&#x27;s move to the final step in the FETC ("fetch") framework: Create . 🚀 This is Where Your Data Turns Into Action Once your data is enriched and transformed, it&#x27;s time to do something with it. That&#x27;s where AI creation comes in. In most workflows, this starts with copy. Think: subject lines, intros, CTAs, PS lines. But the Create step goes far beyond outbound messaging. With AI in Clay, you can also use your data to: Generate AI sales copilot documents for AEs Produce video and voice content using tools like ElevenLabs Create Google Slides and internal reports Build location-based content or geo-targeted campaigns Source influencers based on niche criteria And even generate images and visual assets for campaigns AI is about turning data into deliverables that drive go-to-market. 📝 Starting with Copy: The Foundation of Creation That&#x27;s where most teams start. And it is still one of the highest-leverage use cases. In Clay, the most effective way to do this is through AI Snippets . Instead of generating long paragraphs or entire emails, we use AI to create one focused piece of copy at a time. That could be: A subject line based on a job change An intro sentence that references a recent podcast Or a closing line that mentions a shared connection or industry trend This modular approach gives you control, makes your messaging feel real, and improves accuracy, since we&#x27;re generating less text with each call to our LLMs. 💭 The Philosophy Behind Create When we talk about creating with AI, we&#x27;re not just talking about producing more . We&#x27;re talking about producing better . The real goal is distillation . In a world where we have access to 10 times more data, the challenge isn&#x27;t gathering information. Information is easy. But filtering it down for signal? THAT&#x27;S what&#x27;s hard now. Whether you&#x27;re writing a subject line, summarizing a customer&#x27;s product roadmap, or building a deck for your AE, the most valuable thing you can do is boil it down to what actually matters . That&#x27;s what Create is really about: turning rich, structured data into high-quality content, insights, and assets that people can use. And that shows up in lots of ways: Creating a snippet of personalized outreach Writing a short, focused summary for a sales copilot doc Generating a value prop slide from a company&#x27;s feature set Highlighting the top three things a CSM needs to know before a QBR Each of those examples starts with data, but the output only works if it&#x27;s clear, targeted, and easy to act on. 🧩 AI Snippets: The Building Blocks of Personalization The creative, or human, part of the copywriting process is coming up with the personalization ideas you want to use. Once you develop a tactic, executing it has been historically manual and time-consuming. That&#x27;s where AI snippets come into play. Let&#x27;s use a quick example from my BDR days: When I was prospecting for clients, if I saw that a lead spoke another language fluently on social media, I&#x27;d translate the subject line of my email into that language... Just the subject line! Then I&#x27;d add a short PS to the email body, along the lines of: "P.S. I don&#x27;t speak Arabic fluently, but I saw you did. Thought it was cool and figured it might help this email stand out." This worked really well. Now, AI can create these kinds of formulaic snippets for us at scale, so you can run the same play across your whole list without having to do it manually. That&#x27;s the magic of AI: You come up with the tactic. AI helps you experiment and execute in a fraction of the time, while setting you up to scale instantly. 🔮 What&#x27;s Coming Next In the next lessons, we&#x27;ll show you how to use AI to: Create personalized content at scale using modular AI Snippets And draft full emails faster with tools like Twain Then we&#x27;ll come back to other creation workflows, e.g. video, slides, and more, in future lessons. 💡 Why The Create Step Matters The Create step is what transforms all your hard work gathering, enriching, and transforming data into tangible results. Without effective creation: Your insights remain locked in spreadsheets instead of driving action Your personalization feels generic because it&#x27;s applied inconsistently Your team spends too much time writing instead of engaging with prospects By leveraging AI for creation, you not only save time but also ensure that every piece of content you produce is data-driven, personalized, and optimized for conversion. Remember: The goal isn&#x27;t to replace human creativity, but to amplify it. You identify the signals that matter and the tactics that work, and AI helps you execute them at scale. lesson About this lesson 00:00 Create Multi-Step Sequence Messaging with Twain In the last lesson we covered AI Snippets . These are a modular, high-control approach to generating content where you can customize every part of a message. But what if you don&#x27;t want or need to customize every step? What if you&#x27;re looking for a lower-friction way to start your outbound sequences… and just want the AI to generate full email copy for you? That&#x27;s exactly what the Twain enrichment is for. 🧩 How Twain Structures Your Messaging Instead of asking AI to generate a single block of text, Twain walks the model through a multi-step process , typically including: Subject Line Intro Line Body or Value Prop Call to Action (CTA) PS or Signature (optional) And it can automatically use the enriched data in your Clay table, like: Company name and description Job title Recent funding Tech stack Or any other signals you&#x27;ve pulled in All that data gets plugged into a structured template behind the scenes. ✅ When to Use Twain Twain is a good solution when: You want full email copy, not just snippets You need to ensure you&#x27;re not overloading AI with too much unstructured data You still need to customize tone, length, or structure You want outputs that are clean, modular, and easy to edit 🔄 Using Twain with Your Research Data Let&#x27;s go back to our previous example. We&#x27;ve got our leads and we&#x27;ve done some research. Now we want to start sending personalized outbound messages. Using the same leads we want to contact, let&#x27;s look at what this looks like with Twain. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Setup Process Here&#x27;s how to set up your sequence: Choose your sequence type: Select a pre-defined sequence (1-4 steps) from the dropdown menu If you have a Twain account, you can use your own sequence by selecting your Twain account and entering a sequence ID Configure your prompt parameters: Add your prospect description Define your outreach signal Describe your ideal customer profile State the problem you&#x27;re solving And more… Add your prospect information: Enter first name, last name, and social media profile URL for each prospect Don&#x27;t have social media profile URLs? Use Claygent to find them using prospect emails Map and execute: Map Twain&#x27;s multi-step messages to your Clay columns Run the table to generate your sequences 🤔 AI Snippets vs. Twain: When to Use Each This might leave you wondering – when should you use AI snippets vs Twain? Use AI Snippets when you want full control and flexibility at the sentence level Use Twain when you want a faster , more structured way to generate outbound messaging at scale Both are powerful. Choose the one that best fits your workflow. Experiment with both. Scale what works. 💼 Benefits of a Multi-Step Approach The multi-step approach that Twain uses offers several key advantages: Better structure : By breaking the generation process into discrete steps, the AI focuses on one task at a time, producing more coherent results Improved personalization : Each step can incorporate different aspects of your prospect data Easier editing : If you don&#x27;t like a particular part of the message, you can regenerate just that section Sequence consistency : Ensures your follow-up messages maintain a consistent voice and approach 🌟 Real-World Applications Beyond basic outbound sequences, you can use Twain for: Multi-touch campaigns that gradually build on previous messages Post-event follow-up sequences Re-engagement campaigns for dormant prospects Content distribution sequences that share different resources over time 🔮 What&#x27;s Coming Next We&#x27;ve covered effortless output when it comes to writing copy. There&#x27;s still a number of creation workflows, like video, slides, and more. We&#x27;ll cover those in future lessons. As you move forward with your AI-powered GTM automation, remember that the tools and techniques we&#x27;ve covered in the FETC framework work together as a system. The Find, Enrich, and Transform steps all feed into your Create step, giving you the data and structure you need to generate high-quality, personalized content at scale. About this lesson 00:00 Create Personalized Content at Scale We talked about the philosophy behind Create, how AI helps distill large amounts of data into high-quality, focused content. Now it&#x27;s time to put that into practice. In this lesson, we&#x27;ll show you how to create personalized content at scale using modular AI Snippets in Clay. 🌐 Applications of Create Across Your GTM Motion We can create personalized content across your entire GTM motion: Ad copy for account-based marketing campaigns Direct messages across social media platforms Content for blog posts, landing pages, or social media posts And of course, highly tailored sales emails The most common use case is outbound messaging. And with Clay, you can take a deep personalization table and create dynamic snippets tailored not just to the person, but to the hypothesis you&#x27;re running. 📈 The Evolution of Personalization In the past, personalization meant using simple variables like: "I see you&#x27;re working at {{company}}" Now, the personalization is richer, more dynamic — and powered by AI: {{subj line}} : "Congrats on the new GTM hire" {{body}} : "Saw you closed out Q1 with a 2x jump in pipeline. Curious how the team&#x27;s prioritizing RevOps this quarter?" You&#x27;re still using a template. You&#x27;ll have sections like intro, body, close, ask… but now each variable can contain an entire AI-generated sentence or phrase. You can even change tone and voice using dynamic prompting. This means adjusting copy depending on whether you&#x27;re writing to a VP or an individual contributor. 💪 Benefits of AI-Powered Snippets This approach helps you: Enhance email deliverability Adjust tone and voice per persona Increase message quality without writing every word yourself 🧠 Scaling Strategy, Not Just Messages The real power of AI Snippets is how they reflect your hypotheses , not just your data. For example: If you think a company values innovation, you can generate a subject line that highlights that If you&#x27;re targeting accounts with closed/won pipeline growth, your intro can reference their velocity If someone&#x27;s on the ASU board and you&#x27;re a fellow alum, your CTA can reflect shared context Each variable becomes a reflection of why this person was selected in the first place. 🔬 Example: Personalized Email Intros at Scale Let&#x27;s say you&#x27;re reaching out to 100 marketing leaders at recently funded SaaS startups. You&#x27;ve pulled in: Company descriptions Job changes Funding round details Personal bios Using AI Snippets, you can generate: A subject line based on their funding news A personalized intro based on their latest hire A CTA that reflects the growth stage of their team All without writing a single line of copy by hand. 📋 Implementation in Clay Let&#x27;s see what this looks like in Clay: Start with a deep personalization table Begin with your list of prospects Enrich with social profiles to get detailed information Use AI formulas to transform the enriched data Apply Claygent to find additional context (thought leadership, blogs, interviews) Create modular AI Snippets Generate subject lines that reference specific insights Craft personalized intros based on research findings Develop custom P.S. lines that connect on a personal level Combine into complete messages Use formula columns to combine snippets into cohesive messages Maintain consistent core messaging where appropriate Preview and refine your results 🚀 The Power of Scaling What Works With Clay, you&#x27;re not writing 100 emails. You&#x27;re writing one great play — and then letting AI turn it into 100 unique, relevant messages. That&#x27;s what scaling personalization looks like. You identify what works, and then apply it systematically across your entire prospect list. 🔮 What&#x27;s Coming Next In the next lesson we&#x27;ll show you how to take these snippets and stitch them into complete emails, faster and with better copy, using tools like Twain . 💡 Conclusion Traditional personalization has always faced a fundamental tradeoff between scale and depth. With AI Snippets, you get both and more: Deeper personalization : Each message can reference specific, nuanced details about your prospect Greater scale : You can reach more people without sacrificing quality Consistent messaging : Your core value proposition remains clear and focused Testable hypotheses : You can systematically track which personalization approaches work best By breaking messages into modular components, you gain both flexibility and control, allowing you to maintain your brand voice while adapting to each prospect&#x27;s unique context. Setting up Clay in ChatGPT ✔ 2 Setting up Clay in ChatGPT Best practices for Clay in ChatGPT ✔ 3 Best practices for Clay in ChatGPT Finding & Enriching Contacts in ChatGPT ✔ 4 Finding & Enriching Contacts in ChatGPT Company Research in ChatGPT ✔ 5 Company Research in ChatGPT Outreach in ChatGPT ✔ 6 Outreach in ChatGPT An SDR Workflow in ChatGPT ✔ 7 An SDR Workflow in ChatGPT An Account Planning Workflow in ChatGPT ✔ 8 An Account Planning Workflow in ChatGPT Creating Your Own Use Cases in ChatGPT with AI ✔ 9 Creating Your Own Use Cases in ChatGPT with AI Troubleshooting Clay in ChatGPT ✔ 10 Troubleshooting Clay in ChatGPT Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Clay in ChatGPT / Creating Your Own Use Cases in ChatGPT with AI Lesson 9 / 10 Next lesson Creating Your Own Use Cases in ChatGPT with AI In this lesson, you&#x27;ll use AI to generate creative prompts and workflows tailored to your role. Then, run the best ideas through Clay in ChatGPT. 📝 Step 1: Set Your Role and Goal First, go to ChatGPT and clearly define who you are and what you&#x27;re trying to accomplish. For example: I&#x27;m a Head of Growth at Gusto. Help me think through creative research strategies for prospecting into mid-market companies. This gives the AI context about your specific situation so it can generate relevant, actionable ideas for your use case. 💡 Step 2: Generate Data Points and Prompt Templates Next, ask the AI to brainstorm specific data points and prompt templates you can use. For example: Give me 10 creative data points I should gather about target accounts and 5 prompt templates I can use with Clay in ChatGPT. The AI will generate a list of creative research angles and ready-to-use prompts tailored to your role and goals. 🧪 Step 3: Test the Best Ideas Pick 2 promising data points or prompts from the AI&#x27;s suggestions and run them in Clay in ChatGPT to see what results you get. For example: @Clay find companies in the healthcare space with 200-500 employees that recently raised Series B funding OR @Clay research which HR software they currently use and identify the decision maker for HR operations Test different approaches to see which ones surface the most valuable insights for your specific needs. 🔄 The Migration Rule: When to Move from ChatGPT to Clay Tables Here&#x27;s the key principle: If you find yourself typing the same prompt repeatedly, that is your signal to migrate the workflow into Clay. Repeating prompts means you have found a repeatable workflow. When you notice this pattern, it&#x27;s time to move it from ChatGPT into Clay tables for: Automation at scale - Run the workflow across hundreds or thousands of records automatically CRM integration - Connect your enriched data directly to your sales tools Team collaboration - Share the workflow with your entire team Credit efficiency - Optimize how you use your Clay credits across larger datasets ‍ The ChatGPT interface is perfect for experimentation and testing ideas. But once you&#x27;ve validated a workflow that delivers results, Clay tables give you the infrastructure to scale it across your entire go-to-market motion. We got one more lesson for you. See you there. Now we&#x27;re getting into the strategic execution: how to actually build enrichment workflows that transform your raw contact data into actionable intelligence. By the end of this lesson, you&#x27;ll have a comprehensive playbook for turning basic contact information into the rich, contextual data your sales team needs to have meaningful conversations and drive better sales outcomes. 🔑 The Power of CRM Contact ID You can unlock tremendous enrichment value just by using the CRM contact ID as your starting point. This single identifier acts as a master key that unlocks a treasure trove of data about both the contact and their company, making it incredibly efficient to build comprehensive profiles from minimal starting information. The contact ID connects to your CRM&#x27;s existing data while enabling you to layer on external intelligence from multiple sources. This approach ensures you&#x27;re building on your existing data foundation rather than starting from scratch, which maximizes efficiency and maintains data consistency. Let&#x27;s walk through some of the most valuable and common enrichment use cases that GTM teams use to drive revenue results. 📈 Use Case 1: Enriching New Inbound Leads When inbound leads enter your CRM, you often know very little beyond their name and email address. This minimal information creates challenges for effective qualification and routing, making enrichment crucial for converting inbound interest into qualified opportunities. Note: This use case is covered in depth in our Inbound Automation course, where you can learn the complete workflow and advanced techniques. The Foundation Identifiers Contact Email and LinkedIn URLs serve as the golden identifiers that unlock most other enrichment possibilities. These two data points provide reliable connections to external databases and social profiles that contain comprehensive professional information. Use waterfall enrichment strategies to maximize coverage across multiple data providers. If one source doesn&#x27;t have complete information, the waterfall automatically tries additional sources until you get comprehensive data or exhaust all options. You can extract the company domain directly from the email address to enable company-level enrichments that provide organizational context for individual contacts. The domain data then allows you to enrich company size, industry, technology stack, and other firmographic data that influences qualification and messaging. 🔄 Use Case 2: Updating Existing Contacts with Enriched Data Updating existing contacts with new enriched data requires more sophisticated workflow logic to prevent data conflicts and maintain CRM integrity. The Safe Update Process First, run the Lookup action to identify contacts that already exist in your CRM. Then, create a conditional run formula for Create or Update actions so you&#x27;re not executing both operations unnecessarily. Only Create a new record if the Lookup doesn&#x27;t return anything, and only Update if specific conditions are met. Critical Scenarios to Avoid There are two main problems that can derail update workflows: Credit Waste and Data Overwriting : If conditionals aren&#x27;t configured correctly, you might end up overwriting valid existing data while unnecessarily spending enrichment credits on records that don&#x27;t need updates. Manual Data Conflicts : Be careful about updating fields that are manually maintained by your sales team. Accidentally overwriting manually-entered notes, custom scores, or relationship information can delete valuable institutional knowledge stored in your CRM. Implementation Best Practices Before setting up any update workflow, take time to understand why and how each field is being used by different team members. Document which fields are automatically managed versus manually maintained, and create update rules that respect these distinctions. Consider implementing confidence scoring for enriched data, only updating fields when new information has higher confidence than existing data. This prevents low-quality automated data from overwriting high-quality manual entries. 🚨 Use Case 3: Detecting Contact Job Changes This represents one of the most powerful signal-based enrichment workflows you can implement, providing real-time intelligence about prospect and customer career movements that create new opportunities. The Job Change Detection Process The systematic process for identifying job changes looks like this: Pull existing contacts from your CRM along with their social media URLs. If you don&#x27;t already have social media URLs stored, Clay offers waterfall enrichments that can find these easily using just email addresses or names. Enrich each person using their email and social media profile to get current company information, job title, and employment status. Compare the current company domain from social media with the company domain stored in your CRM to identify discrepancies. Flag mismatches as potential job changes and route these flagged contacts to your sales team for immediate follow-up. Update contacts in your CRM with new emails and job titles as needed to maintain data accuracy. You can use similar logic to detect internal role changes within the same company, identifying contacts who&#x27;ve been promoted to decision-making roles or moved to departments that might need your solution. Job change detection creates natural conversation starters for re-engagement and helps you identify new opportunities at both the contact&#x27;s previous company and new company. 🏢 Company-Level Enrichment Strategies Company enrichment enables sophisticated account-based marketing and sales strategies by providing comprehensive organizational intelligence that informs targeting and messaging decisions. This systematic approach ensures consistent evaluation across all prospects and customers. this lesson also appears in Clay 101, Automated Inbound, and CRM Enrichment, so feel free to skim or skip if you&#x27;ve already seen it somewhere else ‍ Now that you’ve gathered a wealth of company and contact data, it’s time to clean it all up. Getting data is just the first part of the journey. But if you’ve worked with data in the past, then you know that “garbage in leads to garbage out”. Luckily, with some clever native integrations we’ve built into Clay - you can turn “garbage” data into “golden” data. Let&#x27;s explore how these tools can transform your workflow. ‍ 🛠️ Our Data Cleaning Arsenal ‍ Nestled within our enrichment panel, under the "Tools" section, you&#x27;ll find a treasure trove of functions designed to manipulate and clean your data. These tools go beyond what AI formulas alone can offer, providing specialized solutions for common data challenges. View all your cleaning data functions in the tools modal 🏷️ Normalizing Company Names: A Game-Changer One of our most popular cleaning tools addresses a common pain point: inconsistent company names. How often have you encountered company names cluttered with legal suffixes or unnecessary prefixes? Our normalize company names function tackles this issue head-on. For instance, "Panamax Inc." becomes simply "Panamax," and "Cora, a company of blank" is streamlined to "Cora." This clean-up not only makes your data more uniform but also prepares it for seamless use in email copy or other communications. Utilizing the “Normalize company names” function to clean up company data 📞 Beyond Company Names: Versatile Normalization Our normalization tools extend far beyond company names: Text Whitespace : Ensure consistent spacing across all your text data. Phone Numbers : Standardize formats, removing or adding parentheses as needed. Locations : Create uniformity in how addresses and locations are represented. These are just a few examples – we encourage you to explore the full range of normalization options available in Clay. ‍ 🚀 Putting It Into Practice Let&#x27;s walk through a quick example of how to use our normalize company names function: Navigate to the enrichment panel and locate the "Tools" section. Scroll past the AI options to find our pre-built functions. Select "Normalize Company Names." Choose the appropriate input column (in this case, the company name from your companies table). Optionally, you can normalize the case and add additional fields as needed. Run the action across your rows. The result? Clean, consistent company names ready for your next campaign or analysis. ‍ 🌟 Unlocking the Potential of Clean Data By leveraging Clay&#x27;s data cleaning and normalization tools, you&#x27;re setting yourself up for success. Clean data leads to more accurate analyses, more effective outreach, and ultimately, better business outcomes. Remember, while we&#x27;ve highlighted some key features here, there&#x27;s always more to explore. We encourage you to dive into our various normalization options and discover how they can enhance your specific workflows. Data cleaning might not be the most glamorous part of data management, but with Clay&#x27;s tools, it can be surprisingly straightforward – and even enjoyable. Happy data cleaning! Progress Introduction to TAM Sourcing ✔ 1 Introduction to TAM Sourcing Understanding your ICP ✔ 2 Understanding your ICP TAM Sourcing Workflows in Clay ✔ 3 TAM Sourcing Workflows in Clay Advanced TAM Sourcing Techniques ✔ 4 Advanced TAM Sourcing Techniques Activating your TAM: From Intelligence to Revenue ✔ 5 Activating your TAM: From Intelligence to Revenue SMB TAM Sourcing ✔ 6 SMB TAM Sourcing Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers ✔ 7 Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / TAM Sourcing / Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers Lesson 7 / 7 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Data Collection with Third-Party Scrapers 🔍 Third-Party Scrapers: Accessing Hidden Market Intelligence Introduction Previously, we covered advanced TAM sourcing techniques using Clay&#x27;s native capabilities. Today, we&#x27;re expanding your toolkit with third-party scrapers like Apify and Phantombuster to access data sources that traditional B2B providers simply can&#x27;t reach. By the end of this lesson, you&#x27;ll know exactly when and how to use these powerful tools to build comprehensive TAM databases from virtually any corner of the internet, creating competitive advantages through unique market intelligence. 🔍 The Gaps in Traditional B2B Data Traditional B2B data providers like ZoomInfo and Apollo excel at capturing enterprise companies with strong digital footprints, active social media presence, and structured business profiles. But they systematically miss entire market segments that could be goldmines for your business. Think about local businesses like restaurants, medical practices, and retail stores. These companies often have minimal social media presence but significant revenue potential. They&#x27;re running successful operations with real budgets but remain invisible in standard B2B databases. Consider niche industries with specialized directories, geographic markets with region-specific business listings, and real-time signals like job postings, product launches, or pricing changes that indicate immediate buying opportunities. Traditional providers update quarterly or monthly, far too slow to capitalize on these timing-sensitive signals. 🌐 The Untapped Data Universe The internet contains far more business data than any single provider can capture or commercialize. Every industry has its own ecosystem of information sources that traditional aggregators don&#x27;t touch. Review sites like Yelp, G2, and Capterra contain thousands of businesses with rich behavioral data that traditional firmographic databases can&#x27;t provide. The challenge isn&#x27;t necessarily finding this data but collecting it systematically and at scale. Manual copying from websites doesn&#x27;t scale beyond a handful of prospects. That&#x27;s where tools like Apify, Phantombuster, and Chrome scrapers provide the infrastructure for systematic data collection. ⚡ Apify: Systematic Web Data Collection Apify is the most powerful option for systematic data collection from virtually any website, turning unstructured web pages into structured datasets you can analyze and enrich. The Actor Library Apify&#x27;s library contains over 2,000 pre-built actors, ready-made scrapers optimized for popular platforms. Want to scrape Instagram business profiles for follower counts and engagement rates? There&#x27;s an actor for that. Need company data from social media including employee counts and recent posts? There&#x27;s an actor for that too. This extensive library means you rarely need to build scrapers from scratch. Practical Restaurant POS Example Here&#x27;s a concrete example demonstrating Apify&#x27;s TAM expansion power. Say you&#x27;re targeting local restaurants for point-of-sale software. Traditional B2B providers might give you 20% market coverage because most independent restaurants don&#x27;t appear in business databases. With Apify, you can scrape Yelp for restaurants in specific zip codes, extract contact information, revenue estimates based on review volume and pricing, and review sentiment data revealing operational pain points. This approach provides 90% market coverage with rich behavioral data showing which restaurants struggle with service speed or order accuracy—perfect indicators they need better POS systems. Apify: Setup and Configuration Here&#x27;s the step-by-step setup process: Step 1: Create Your Apify Account and browse their actor library to find scrapers matching your data needs. Each actor targets specific platforms—Instagram Business Scraper, Google Maps Scraper, and hundreds more specialized options. Step 2: Configure Your Actor by clicking "Create Task" to add it to your library of actors, which Clay will be able to access directly. Switch the input format from Manual to JSON mode and copy the body text—this becomes your input data structure in Clay. Step 3: Connect to Clay by navigating to Actions → Run Apify Actor. Select the task you just created in Apify and paste the JSON configuration under "Input Data" to define what the scraper should collect. 🎯 Building GTM Alpha Through Creative Data Collection Let&#x27;s examine how creative scraping strategies create genuine competitive advantages that traditional prospecting can&#x27;t match. The E-Commerce Marketing Agency Example Say you&#x27;re a marketing agency trying to target e-commerce brands. The standard approach is searching for mid-sized e-commerce companies in traditional B2B databases. You get the exact same list as every competitor, leading to identical outreach that prospects have seen dozens of times. Generic data leads to generic outreach, which leads to terrible response rates and commoditized positioning. The Strategic Insight But here&#x27;s a valuable insight: Brands with huge social followings but low website engagement are essentially signaling "We have marketing budget and audience but need help with conversion optimization." This represents your perfect prospect: they&#x27;ve proven they can build an audience but struggle to monetize it. The challenge is systematically identifying these businesses when traditional databases don&#x27;t track this behavioral mismatch. The Clay Apify Workflow Here&#x27;s how to build competitive advantage through creative data collection: Step 1: Social Following Discovery - Use Instagram Business Scraper to find brands with 50K+ followers in your target industry. Step 2: Website Performance Analysis - Use Similarweb Scraper to check their websites for in-depth traffic data—visit counts, session duration, bounce rates, and traffic sources to detect any conversion gaps. Step 3: Intelligent Outreach - Use Clay&#x27;s AI to compose personalized copy referencing specific data points you&#x27;ve discovered about their business.
