Most technographic providers rely on web scraping and basic detection methods. They crawl websites looking for JavaScript snippets, tracking pixels, and other surface-level indicators. This gives you basic information like "Company X uses Salesforce" or "Company Y has Google Analytics installed." But here&#x27;s the problem: web scraping only captures what&#x27;s publicly visible on a company&#x27;s website. It misses the depth of their actual technology usage, spending patterns, and implementation details that really matter for sales and marketing. HG Insights takes a fundamentally different approach through document analysis. 📄 Document Analysis Methodology Instead of just scraping websites, HG Insights processes billions of business documents. We&#x27;re talking about SEC filings, press releases, contracts, RFPs, job postings, earnings calls, and other corporate documents that reveal the real story behind a company&#x27;s technology decisions. This document analysis methodology uncovers information that web scraping simply cannot access: actual spend amounts, contract terms, implementation timelines, and usage patterns. 🎯 The Difference in Practice Here&#x27;s the difference between basic technographics and HG Insights data: HG Insights tells you that Airbnb runs Salesforce Enterprise Edition plus Marketing Cloud, they&#x27;re spending approximately 180K annually across 50-plus licenses, they upgraded their implementation 8 months ago, and they&#x27;re currently evaluating additional Salesforce products based on recent job postings for Salesforce administrators. Or take a company like Stripe. A basic provider might detect that they use AWS. HG Insights reveals that Stripe has a multi-million dollar AWS contract, they&#x27;re using specific services like Lambda and RDS, they&#x27;ve expanded their usage by 40% in the last year, and they have dedicated AWS architects on staff. This level of detail transforms how you approach prospects because you understand not just what they use, but how they use it and what it means for their business priorities. 🏢 Corporate Structure Visibility HG Insights also provides corporate structure visibility that most providers miss entirely. Basic technographic tools typically focus on single domains or headquarters locations. But enterprise companies are complex - they have subsidiaries, regional offices, and different technology stacks across business units. HG Insights maps these relationships, showing you the complete technology footprint across an organization&#x27;s entire corporate structure. This means you can identify opportunities at subsidiary companies that other providers don&#x27;t even know exist, or understand how technology decisions flow between parent companies and their divisions. 📊 Enterprise Adoption 90% of Fortune 500 technology companies rely on HG Insights data for their go-to-market strategies. And 75% of Fortune 100 companies use their insights for competitive intelligence and market research. 💡 Clay <> HG Insights Integration But here&#x27;s where Clay changes the game for smaller teams and individual users. Traditionally, accessing HG Insights data required expensive annual contracts, often starting at $50,000+ per year with lengthy procurement processes. Clay&#x27;s integration eliminates these barriers entirely. You get the same enterprise-grade technographic data through Clay credits, meaning you get access to Fortune 500-level intelligence without the budget or procurement headaches. 🤔 When to Use HG Insights So when should you use HG Insights versus other technographic providers? Use HG Insights when you need depth over breadth. If you&#x27;re doing high-touch sales with longer deal cycles, the detailed spend and contract information can be the difference between a generic pitch and a conversation that resonates. Use it when you&#x27;re targeting enterprise accounts with complex corporate structures. The subsidiary mapping and organizational visibility helps you identify the right entry points and decision-makers. And use it when timing matters. The contract renewal dates and implementation timelines help you reach prospects when they&#x27;re actually in buying mode, not just when they happen to visit your website. 🚀 What&#x27;s Next In our next lesson, we&#x27;ll walk through exactly how to set up HG Insights enrichment in Clay, including the specific data points you can access and how to structure your tables for maximum efficiency. ‍ Table of contents TOC Heading TOC Heading Related resources Next lesson Next up How to Use HG Insights in Clay HG Insights in Action View next lesson View next lesson Explore, practice and master Clay Powered education Linkedin Youtube Slack community Explore Clay Visit Clay.com Integrations Multi-provider data enrichment Sculptor AI Claygent Audiences Sequencer Pricing Changelog Get started here Get started lesson Clay 101 Enroll in Clay cohorts Engage Find a Clay experts Hire a GTME talent GTM job board Community Join Slack FAQ Legal Privacy policy Terms of service Do not sell my data © Clay 2025 – Born in Brooklyn. Progress Intro to Inbound Automation ✔ 1 Intro to Inbound Automation Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow ✔ 2 Clay Inbound Automation: End-to-End Workflow Connecting Inbound Lead Sources ✔ 3 Connecting Inbound Lead Sources Your Inbound Enrichment Stack ✔ 4 Your Inbound Enrichment Stack Transforming Data for Inbound ✔ 5 Transforming Data for Inbound Lead Scoring for Inbound ✔ 6 Lead Scoring for Inbound Lead Routing ✔ 7 Lead Routing Personalized Messaging for Inbound ✔ 8 Personalized Messaging for Inbound Deep Dive: Web Intent ✔ 9 Deep Dive: Web Intent Responding to Inbound Leads (Exporting Data) ✔ 9 Responding to Inbound Leads (Exporting Data) Learn and master Clay with Clay university Featured in Clay University All courses / Automated Inbound / Your Inbound Enrichment Stack Lesson 4 / 9 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Your Inbound Enrichment Stack 🔎 Smart Inbound Lead Enrichment: From Basic Info to Sales Intelligence Today, we&#x27;re diving into the enrichment step of your inbound engine—the process that transforms basic lead information into comprehensive prospect intelligence. Enrichment is the difference between knowing a lead&#x27;s name and knowing whether that lead is worthy of a rep&#x27;s full attention right now. In this lesson, we’ll break down how to enrich smarter and efficiently, showing you how to think creatively strategically about what really matters for your team. 📄 Why Shorter Forms Win in Inbound The unique thing about inbound is that you get to decide how much to ask customers upfront. Spoiler alert: less is more. While more fields allow you to collect more customer data, the longer the form, the higher the friction is for leads. Research shows that just adding two extra form fields - from 3 to 5 - slashes average completing rates by nearly one half. Before Clay, there was an inescapable trade-off between form length and lead quality. Shorter forms led to better conversions but left reps scrambling to manually research basic information on leads just to qualify them. With longer lead forms, companies sought to pre-qualify leads in an attempt to minimize manual research. It’s why so many B2B software demo forms still ask questions like “What is your company size?” With Clay, you don’t need to ask those questions anymore. You can have the best of both worlds: short forms that maximize conversions and minimize speed to lead, without sacrificing the data you need for context-rich follow-up. In a post-Clay world, your inbound forms really only need to ask for one or two critical pieces of info: Name Email address or LinkedIn profile URL From just those data points, we can easily enrich our way to personal info like job title, years of experience, educational background, as well as company data like headcount, industry, description, tech stack, and anything else you might want to learn about. It’s same Jigsaw framework we discussed in Clay 101: we always want to start with those corner pieces before filling in the center. 🧠 Thinking Strategically about Inbound Enrichment Another key difference between enriching inbound leads versus outbound is how you prioritize what data to gather. With outbound, you often want a broad, complete picture of potential prospects in order to identify new targets. With inbound, that script flips: you’re working backwards from bare minimum data points, figuring out just how much data you need to confidently score and prioritize leads while maximizing speed to lead. To put it simply, it’s not about collecting every possible data point— it’s about doubling down on the essential signals that tell you whether or not a lead is worth immediate action. With Clay, you can get incredibly creative about what firmographic, demographic, and behavioral traits represent best fit custom data signals for your company. If you don’t know where to start, you can start by asking: What traits and behaviors do we see consistently in our best customers? At Clay, we know that some key data points for our own segmentation and scoring strategy are company size, which determines which internal team at Clay handles the lead, the lead’s seniority and title, which helps us know whether we’re speaking with a key decision maker, and industry - we tend to sell well to software companies because they usually have RevOps and marketing leaders who are comfortable working with tools like Clay and more open to experimentation. By defining these key must-have signals, we make sure that our enrichment process is focused and directly tied to our revenue motion. 🚿 Waterfall Enrichments: Contact Enrichment As you might remember from 101, all good enrichment starts with Waterfalls. Waterfalls help maximize data coverage and accuracy across our 100+ providers. Let’s start with contact enrichment. You can leverage waterfall enrichments to validate and find data, starting with email address and Linkedin URL. After collecting those corner pieces, you can continue using waterfalls to fill in useful contact data like phone number and social media profiles. With those bits of info, you can quickly extract tons of detailed information about a contact’s work experience and education that can help you understand someone’s background to determine their fit as a prospect or to craft personalized messaging. 💼 Job Change To inform personalized messaging, you might be interested in detecting whether an inbound lead recently changed jobs. The best way to do this is to use the “Job Start Date” enrichment. After identifying when a lead started their most recent role, you can add a formula column to generate a boolean response based on whether the start date falls within the last six months, or whatever time frame you select. Maybe you want to find mutual social media connections between your team and that of your new lead. You can leverage Clay’s integration with The Swarm to find those warm intros that you can mention later in outreach. 🤖 Claygent: Find job title and company Beyond native enrichments and integrations, AI formulas or Claygent are a great way to find nuanced info. Let’s say you want to find a person’s current title and company. While that might seem simple, people might have primary and secondary positions, in addition to advisory or board roles you might want to filter out. Here’s an example of a prompt that let’s you do just that: **You are a job title analyzer. Your task is to identify a person&#x27;s PRIMARY professional role and filter out secondary, advisory, or board positions. **CLASSIFICATION RULES:** **PRIMARY POSITIONS (Include these):** - Full-time executive roles: CEO, CTO, CMO, CFO, COO - Department heads: VP of Sales, Director of Marketing, Head of Engineering - Operational management: General Manager, Operations Manager, Regional Manager - Functional specialists: Senior Developer, Account Executive, Product Manager **SECONDARY/

University All courses / Clay 101: GTM Automation / Your First GTM Use Case Lesson 2 / 17 Next lesson About this lesson 00:00 Your First GTM Use Case This lesson is a small preview into the art of what&#x27;s possible in Clay. We&#x27;re going to quickly look at three different workflows that demonstrate Clay&#x27;s power. Don&#x27;t worry about memorizing every step or understanding all the technical details right now. The purpose here is to show you what kinds of business outcomes become possible once you start to grasp the basics of Clay. 💪 What Makes Clay Truly Powerful What makes Clay truly powerful isn&#x27;t any single feature—it&#x27;s how all these features combine into end-to-end workflows that automate what used to take hours or days of manual work. These workflows create real business outcomes: higher conversion rates, better targeting, more personalized outreach, and access to prospects your competitors can&#x27;t reach. Remember, we&#x27;re showing you possibilities here. The detailed "how to" on building these workflows are coming in the lessons ahead. 📈 Use Case 1: B2B Outbound Campaign Let&#x27;s start with a classic B2B outbound campaign, but supercharged with Clay&#x27;s capabilities. Here&#x27;s how this workflow unfolds: First, we find companies using Clay&#x27;s native dataset, filtering for specific criteria like industry, headcount, and location to match our ideal customer profile. Next, we enrich those companies with firmographic data—things like funding stage, revenue estimates, and technology stack. Then we filter the list down to our most promising prospects. Now we find people at those companies, targeting specific job titles and seniority levels that match our buyer personas. We enrich those people with contact information using Clay&#x27;s email waterfalls. Here&#x27;s where it gets interesting: we use AI formulas to extract the unique companies each person has worked at Finally, we export everything to our CRM and email sequencing tool, complete with personalized subject lines for each prospect. The business outcome? A highly targeted outbound campaign where every email includes genuine, personalized insights. Instead of generic "I saw you work at Company X" messages, you&#x27;re referencing their specific background and experiences. Compare this to the manual approach: what used to take a team of researchers weeks to compile, you can now build in hours. 🗺️ Use Case 2: Local Business Prospecting Now let&#x27;s look at something completely different—targeting local businesses that most B2B tools completely miss. This workflow starts with finding local businesses using Google Maps integration. We&#x27;re not limited to companies with strong online presences or LinkedIn pages. We can find every dentist in Austin, every restaurant in Brooklyn, or every auto repair shop in Phoenix. Then we use Claygent to gather specific business insights that matter to our offering. For example, if we&#x27;re selling to restaurants, Claygent can check if they offer delivery, what their specialties are, or whether they mention specific challenges on their website. We enrich with contact information and business details, including number of reviews and average rating. When we&#x27;re ready, we can export to our outreach tools with highly relevant, location-specific personalization. The business outcome is accessing markets your competitors can&#x27;t reach. While they&#x27;re all fighting over the same companies in traditional B2B databases, you&#x27;re building relationships with local businesses that have real needs but limited online visibility. This gives you a real advantage over competitors—you&#x27;re finding new business opportunities in untapped markets while others chase the same crowded prospects. 🔬 Use Case 3: Advanced Research and Personalization For our third example, let&#x27;s look at the advanced research capabilities that create truly differentiated outreach. This workflow leverages everything we&#x27;ll cover in Clay 101 to conduct deep research on leads and their companies by gathering insights from social mediaprofiles, company websites, and AI-powered web searches. You&#x27;ll discover non-traditional data points that matter, then use all this intelligence to create highly personalized outreach that actually resonates with your prospects. Here&#x27;s how it works: Start by importing your lead data, capturing key information like social mediaprofile URLs from sources like Typeform responses Gather detailed information about each lead&#x27;s experience, skills, and current company situation from social media profiles Enrich company data using social media company URLs to understand company size, industry, and other relevant firmographics Use AI-powered tools like Claygent and ChatGPT to analyze all this data and identify unique insights that others would miss Create personalized outreach materials including tailored messages, research briefs, and even custom memes that speak directly to each prospect&#x27;s situation The result? Sophisticated personalization that creates genuine connections. Instead of surface-level personalization, you&#x27;re reaching out with insights like "I noticed your company just posted three new engineering roles and mentioned AI transformation on your careers page" or "I saw your recent blog post about scaling customer success—we&#x27;ve helped similar companies in your situation." The business outcome is outreach that feels genuinely researched and relevant, leading to much higher response rates and better conversations. You&#x27;re not just another vendor—you&#x27;re someone who clearly understands their business and challenges. 🧩 The Framework Connection Here&#x27;s the best part of these three workflows—they all follow the exact same underlying frameworks we&#x27;re goin
